title: Analysis of Protein Kinase Interactions in Leishmania mexicana Using CRISPR-Cas9 and Two-Component miniTurbo Proximity Labelling.
abstract: A Leishmania mexicana cell line stably expressing the Leishmania CRISPR-Cas9 system comprising Cas9 endonuclease and T7 RNA polymerase was generated and further modified to express an FRB-FKBP two-component miniTurbo biotin ligase proximity labelling system. These cell lines allowed for the deletion and tagging of LmxMKKK19, a putative MAP kinase kinase kinase, with monomeric NeonGreen or FRB. LmxMKKK19 null mutant promastigotes exhibited no obvious phenotype and were as infective in mouse infection experiments as the parent cell line. However, LmxMKKK19 add-back mutants caused no to minor footpad lesions, suggesting that improperly controlled LmxMKKK19 expression in amastigotes can affect lesion development. LmxM.33.2090, a putative MAP2K (LmxMKK6), was identified as a putative interaction partner of LmxMKKK19 using in vivo proximity biotinylation. Co-localisation using TagRFP-T-tagged LmxM.33.2090 with LmxMKKK19-mNG, proximity labelling using FRB-tagged LmxM.33.2090, and AlphaFold3 modelling supported the interaction of the two kinases in L. mexicana promastigotes. This system shows promise as a useful means to detect transient protein-protein interactions in Leishmania and will aid in linking protein kinases in signalling networks.

title: Oxidative RNA Damage Governs Efficiency and Fidelity of RNA-Guided DNA Base Damage Repair.
abstract: RNAs are essential for gene transcription and protein translation. Yet they also play a crucial role in mediating DNA repair, including RNA-guided DNA base damage repair. However, it is unknown whether RNA integrity can alter DNA repair, modulating genome stability. To address this, we studied the effects of oxidative RNA damage 8-oxoG and an abasic site (AP site) on RNA-guided DNA synthesis and its fidelity by human DNA polymerases on an RNA-DNA hybrid and revealed the underlying molecular mechanisms. We showed that 8-oxoG on an RNA template inhibited pol β DNA synthesis and reduced the fidelity of pol β and pol η by promoting incorrect nucleotide and ribonucleotide incorporation in DNA. We found that an RNA AP site eliminated pol β DNA synthesis and promoted pol η incorporation of dA opposite the AP site. Using AlphaFold3-mediated molecular dynamics simulation, we found that the RNA 8-oxoG and AP site induced unique conformational changes in the RNA-DNA hybrid substrate to disrupt pol β and pol η substrate interaction, leading to RNA-guided nucleotide misincorporation. Our results provide the first insight into the new role of RNA integrity in modulating genome integrity through RNA-guided DNA repair on R-loops.

title: Mixed-Backbone Oligonucleotides for Therapeutics: The Way of the Future.
abstract: Conventional oligonucleotides, such as DNA and RNA, are extensively modified for therapeutic applications. The mixed-backbone oligonucleotides (MBOs) that are generated by combining different classes have superior properties such as enhanced mRNA binding affinity, improved distribution, and reduced toxicity. Oligonucleotides act on mRNA in different ways, such as RNase H-mediated decay, RNA interference, and splice switching, and require specific modification patterns in each case. Hence, understanding the scope of different modifications and their synthetic compatibility is fundamental to the blueprint of future MBOs. In this Perspective, the important design considerations of mixed-backbone oligonucleotides have been presented for the most common types of mRNA-targeting oligonucleotides. The synthetic principles employed for the generation of chimeric MBOs using different phosphorus chemistries and execution modes (manual/automated) have also been discussed. Finally, the evolution of MBOs in clinical studies has been presented with exemplification of FDA-approved ONs.

title: Targeted Liposomal Nanocarriers for High-Efficiency Neuronal mRNA Delivery.
abstract: Messenger RNA therapeutics enable rapid, transient protein expression without risk of genomic integration, but their delivery to post-mitotic neurons remains challenging. Here, we present a neuron-targeted liposomal platform designed to enhance mRNA delivery efficiency in neurons. We engineered DOTAP: DOPE liposomes to promote nucleic acid loading, stability, and endosomal escape, incorporated PEGylation to improve biocompatibility and circulation, and functionalized the liposome surface with a rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-derived peptide for neuronal targeting. We assessed particle size and surface charge, mRNA encapsulation/loading across different lipid: mRNA ratios, cytotoxicity in HEK293T cells as a function of cationic lipid content and PEGylation, and transfection performance in HEK293T cells and primary neurons, benchmarking against a commercial transfection reagent, with functional mRNA delivery further demonstrated in midbrain organoids following microinjection. The system enabled efficient mRNA encapsulation, maintained favorable particle size and surface charge characteristics, and supported low cytotoxicity. Across formulations, mRNA loading increased with lipid: mRNA ratio, with only modest reductions following PEGylation. In HEK293T cells, higher cationic lipid content increased its toxicity, whereas PEGylation reduced membrane interactions and improved tolerability. Transfection studies identified the 50:10 DOTAP: DOPE composition as optimal, yielding robust mRNA expression. In primary neurons, RVG-functionalized PEGylated liposomes containing 10 mol% DOPE achieved gene expression levels comparable to those of a commercial transfection reagent at a 10:1 lipid:mRNA ratio. Notably, incorporating 0.1% w/w RVG significantly outperformed the commercial formulation, yielding >30% gene-delivery efficiency in primary neuronal cultures. In midbrain organoids, the optimized mRNA-loaded RVG-functionalized liposomes produced GFP mRNA expression overlapping with NeuN staining, demonstrating functional mRNA delivery and translation within three-dimensional neural tissue. Neuron-targeted DOTAP: DOPE liposomes incorporating the RVG peptide represent a promising mRNA delivery system for neurological applications, achieving a favorable balance of potency, safety, and specificity and supporting transient gene modulation in the central nervous system.

title: The RdRp Thumb-1 Pocket Is a Conserved Target for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development.
abstract: RNA viruses cause human diseases ranging from mild colds to deadly pandemics. Direct-acting, broad-spectrum, non-nucleoside antivirals have been characterized as impossible to develop because allosteric binding sites are poorly conserved. The HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) Thumb-1 allosteric site and its interaction with the HCV NS5B Λ1-loop governs an essential conformational change required for polymerase initiation. The only approved NS5B Thumb-1 inhibitor, beclabuvir, has been shown to be inactive against a broad panel of non-HCV viruses, including poliovirus, rhinovirus, coronavirus, coxsackievirus, influenzavirus, and HIV. A conserved, homologous allosteric site on RdRp that spans multiple viral families has not been reported. Here, we report GALILEO's discovery that the Thumb-1 pocket, its associated Λ1-loop and their interaction are conserved between RNA viral families for the first time. The discovery is structurally validated through comparative analysis of Protein Data Bank (PDB)-deposited viral polymerases utilizing a method that allows independent, public validation. We further demonstrate that beclabuvir's dependence on its indole C6 carbonyl to interact with the HCV-specific residue R503 restricts its activity to HCV. The discovery is biochemically validated with MDL-001, which does not contain a C6 carbonyl substituent. MDL-001 directly blocks viral RNA synthesis in isolated HCV and SARS-CoV-2 replication complexes and selects for the canonical Thumb-1 resistance mutation P495S in HCV NS5B. The discovery is validated at the cellular level through demonstration of MDL-001's broad-spectrum, in vitro inhibition of both HCV and SARS-CoV-2. Preclinical proof of concept and development of MDL-001 in HCV, HBV, HDV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV have been previously reported. These findings establish RdRp Thumb-1 as a conserved allosteric pocket and a druggable target for broad-spectrum direct-acting antiviral development.

title: Strange Company: CCDC200, RNU2-1, and ERVK13 Retroviruses.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The human RNU2-1 locus combines a variable tandem array of U2 small nuclear RNA (snRNA) genes, retroviral sequences, and extensive linkage with BRCA1. How these features evolved and whether they are functionally related remain unclear. We characterize the structure and variation in this genomic region. Methods: We investigated RNU2-1 and flanking sequences by comparing the T2T-CHM13 assembly with 466 publicly available phased haplotype assemblies, from which we recovered 453 RNU2-1 arrays containing 10,256 U2-1 snRNA genes in total, and by estimating array length from long-read depth from a further 876 individuals. Results: The array is flanked by complex repetitive sequences, including three ERVK13 endogenous retroviruses and sequences predicted to form secondary structures near CCDC200. Although most U2 snRNA genes encode the canonical sequence, some haplotypes contain substantial proportions of variants. Sequence variation is lowest in the region that is most constrained in the single-copy paralogue RNU2-2, suggesting purifying selection on individual copies. Array size and variant composition are associated with extended haplotypes encompassing BRCA1, with larger arrays and more variant genes on certain haplotypes. Conclusions: RNU2-1 is a structurally complex, evolutionarily dynamic locus in which tandem gene amplification, sequence homogenization, and long-range linkage shape patterns of genetic variation. The association between array properties and BRCA1 haplotypes provides a framework for investigating the evolutionary forces acting on this region. The conserved features of its retroviral remnants and the distribution of variation among U2 snRNA gene copies also motivate further investigation of their potential functional significance.

title: Alternative Splicing of MBNL1 and MBNL2 Regulates the Nucleocytoplasmic Distribution of CUG RNA Foci in DM1 Cell Models.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is the most common form of adult-onset muscular dystrophy. DM1 is caused by a CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the 3'-untranslated region of the DMPK gene. Expanded CUG repeat RNA forms nuclear CUG RNA foci that sequester the RNA-binding protein MBNL1, leading to loss of MBNL1 function and resulting in splicing abnormalities. MBNL1 autoregulates its nuclear localization by repressing the inclusion of exon 5, which encodes part of its nuclear localization signal. In DM1, exon 5 inclusion is increased due to loss of MBNL1 function. However, whether inclusion of exon 5 contributes to the formation of nuclear CUG RNA foci remains unclear; we investigated this relationship in the present study. Methods: We used dCasRx, the catalytically inactive form of Cas13d, together with guide RNAs targeting sequences within and around exon 5 to identify an optimal sequence for exon 5 skipping. An antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designated ex5-ASO, designed from the selected sequence, was transfected into a cellular DM1 model and DM1 patient-derived fibroblasts to assess their effects on RNA foci. Results: ex5-ASO successfully induced skipping of not only MBNL1 exon 5 but also MBNL2 exon 5 in a dose-dependent manner. The cytoplasmic fractions of both MBNL1 and MBNL2 increased following ex5-ASO transfection. Remarkably, ex5-ASO treatment reduced nuclear RNA foci and induced the appearance of cytoplasmic foci. However, despite reduced nuclear RNA foci and substantial residual nuclear MBNL1/2, mis-splicing persisted after ex5-ASO treatment. Conclusions: The level of MBNL1/2 exon 5 inclusion affects nuclear RNA foci formation, suggesting that the increased exon 5 inclusion observed in DM1 is not merely a consequence of MBNL loss of function but may also contribute to the nuclear accumulation of RNA foci and sequestration of MBNL1/2.

title: Clinical Pharmacology of Personalized mRNA Neoantigen Vaccines in Oncology: Molecular Design, Cellular Disposition and Combination Chemotherapy Strategy.
abstract: Individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccines constitute a new pharmacological class of anticancer biologic, in which the drug substance is redesigned for every patient against the somatic mutations of their own tumour. This review appraises the molecular pharmacology, pharmaceutical development, cellular disposition and pharmacodynamic behaviour, dosing, drug interactions and toxicology of this class, and evaluates the evidence governing its integration into cancer chemotherapy strategy. No conventional pharmacokinetic dataset exists for any agent in this class, and no plasma concentration-time, clearance or exposure-response data have been reported; disposition is therefore described throughout at the level of lipid-nanoparticle biodistribution, transgene expression kinetics and immunological pharmacodynamics, and the title and terminology of this review have been framed accordingly. Narrative critical review conducted under a protocol registered on the Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/8tgx4/ ). PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, SPORTDiscus and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 10 September 2026, restricted to English-language reports, combining controlled vocabulary (MeSH: Cancer Vaccines; mRNA Vaccines; Antigens, Neoplasm; Immunotherapy) with free-text terms for neoantigen, neoepitope, mutanome, frameshift peptide, individualised neoantigen therapy, mRNA or RNA vaccine, lipid nanoparticle and immune checkpoint inhibitor, together with named-agent and named-trial searches. Reference lists of included reports were screened for further studies. A targeted update search restricted to the named agents and trials was performed on 2 November 2026 during revision. The search strategy, eligibility criteria, selection process and their limitations are reported in full in Sect. 2 and Table 1. Neoantigen target selection remains pharmaceutically inefficient: fewer than 1 in 200 screened mutations is confirmed immunogenic, and consortium benchmarking found a positive predictive value of approximately 6% for epitope-prediction pipelines. Unlike small-molecule cytotoxics, these agents show no classical absorption-distribution-metabolism-excretion pharmacokinetics; disposition instead reflects lipid-nanoparticle biodistribution and transgene expression kinetics, with murine data indicating that CD8 + T-cell priming proceeds through a type I interferon-dependent cross-dressing pathway independent of conventional cDC1 cross-presentation. Clinically, intismeran autogene (1 mg intramuscularly every 3 weeks, up to 9 doses) combined with pembrolizumab produced a recurrence-free survival hazard ratio of 0.561 (95% CI 0.309-1.017; one-sided P = 0.053, a confidence interval that crosses unity) at primary analysis and 0.510 (95% CI 0.294-0.887) at five years in resected melanoma. The phase III INTerpath-001 trial (n = 1,137), reported in full at the 2026 ESMO Congress at a median follow-up of 24.6 months, reduced recurrence or death (RFS hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.45-0.75; P < 0.001; 24-month RFS 82.2% versus 70.0%) and distant metastasis or death (DMFS hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.45-0.85; P = 0.002), with overall survival immature (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.45-1.31). A prespecified piecewise analysis showed no effect in the first six months (RFS hazard ratio 0.99) and a large effect thereafter (0.42), the clearest clinical signature yet of a therapy that requires immune priming rather than immediate target engagement. Conversely, autogene cevumeran given as adjuvant monotherapy without checkpoint blockade was terminated in a randomized phase II colorectal trial for futility and an overall survival imbalance. Because these two programmes differ simultaneously in tumour type, delivery platform, patient selection and construct capacity as well as in the presence of checkpoint blockade, the contrast is associative and hypothesis-generating; concurrent checkpoint blockade is the most clinically tractable of several sufficient explanations, not an established requirement. The pharmacology of this drug class appears to be context-dependent rather than construct-dependent: Clinical benefit appears to depend on disease context, treatment setting and combination strategy, although the relative contributions of these factors remain incompletely established. Rational incorporation into chemotherapy strategy will depend on pharmacogenomic patient selection, ctDNA-anchored pharmacodynamic endpoints, manufacturing timelines that outpace tumour evolution, and evidence-based combination partnering.

title: Machine Learning-Guided Design of Peptide-Targeted CRISPR Vectors for Tissue-Specific Non-Coding RNA Knockdown.
abstract: CRISPR-based genome/epigenome editing and RNA-targeted therapeutics offer unprecedented precision for correcting disease-causing mutations, yet clinical translation remains constrained by two unresolved bottlenecks: suboptimal guide RNA (gRNA) design limiting editing efficiency and specificity, and the absence of safe, tissue-selective delivery platforms. While machine learning (ML)-driven gRNA design and peptide-mediated delivery have each advanced substantially in isolation, to our knowledge, no existing framework jointly optimizes predictive guide-design models and delivery-vector design within a single pipeline a disconnect that likely underlies persistent efficacy-safety trade-offs in clinical translation. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing ML-driven guide design and peptide-engineered delivery within a single mechanistic and computational framework. We first outline the structural basis of peptide-derived vectors, emphasizing how charge, hydrophobicity, secondary structure, and receptor-targeting functionalization govern organ- and cell-type specificity. We then critically appraise ML methods for predicting on-target activity, off-target propensity, and specificity across CRISPR platforms, alongside computational approaches for non-coding RNA target identification, focusing on training-data limitations, feature representation, and cross-platform generalizability that constrain predictive reliability. We synthesize design principles for tissue-specific delivery, including nanocarrier integration, and highlight preclinical cases where ML-guided peptide engineering enabled targeted delivery of mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, and CRISPR ribonucleoproteins. Finally, we assess persistent barriers data sparsity, limited model transferability, off-target genotoxicity, immunogenicity, and delivery constraints and propose emerging directions: multi-omics integration, AI-enabled de novo peptide design, and translational frameworks. This review establishes a convergent paradigm in which joint ML-guided optimization of guide and delivery design enhances the specificity, efficiency, and safety of next-generation precision genetic medicines.

title: Bioinformatic Analysis of Brain Region Proteomes in a Mice Model of Affective Disorders Annotated Using Panther GO.
abstract: The proteomic approach to studying the pathogenesis of affective disorders is becoming increasingly effective, thanks to bioinformatics tools. However, investigating changes occurring in the brain is primarily possible only through animal models. In this study, for the first time, mass spectrometry analysis and proteomic annotation with the "Panther GO" tool were applied to examine the protein composition of the brain in a genetic mouse model of affective disorders, the Disc1-Q31L-/- (Q31L) strain. In the prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and hypothalamus of this genetic line, we identified over 1000 proteins that showed significant differences compared to the wild type, as determined by qualitative analysis. Using the "Panther GO" database, we investigated protein classes, biological and molecular functions, and related pathways of unique proteins in each structure. In the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of mice with the Q31L model of affective disorders, a decrease was observed in the detection frequency of proteins, biological processes, and molecular functions related to immunity, alongside an increase in the detection frequency of RNA-dependent processes. In all brain structures examined in mice with a model of affective disorders, specific signaling pathways were identified that primarily involve neurotransmitter and neuroendocrine systems and participate in immune and inflammatory responses, as well as in processes regulating oxidative stress and vesicular transport. Thus, for the first time, qualitative changes in the brain proteome have been identified in the Q31L mice model of affective disorders, compared to wild-type mice. These preliminary results will serve as a foundation for further investigation into the mechanisms underlying disorders associated with the dysfunction of the Disc1 gene.

title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity.
abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)-mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

title: Stress granules: formation, biological functions, cellular signaling, diseases, and therapeutic targets.
abstract: Stress granules (SG) are dynamic, membraneless condensates formed via liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) under acute stress. By transiently rewiring RNA and protein networks, SG mediate cellular adaptation and homeostatic maintenance. Persistent or recurrent stress, prolongs SG retention and drives cellular and molecular network remodeling, shifting SG from a reversible, adaptive state toward a stable, pathological state. This dynamic SG dysregulation is directly implicated in the onset and progression of diverse human diseases. Integrating SG biogenesis, function, signaling regulation, and disease-related alterations, this review proposes the spatiotemporal condensate state-transition (SCST) framework. This framework conceptualizes disease-associated SG aberrations as dynamic state transitions coordinately driven by alterations across four dimensions: temporal persistence, spatial context, molecular composition, and condensate state. With neurodegenerative diseases as the primary context, this review systematically elucidates and demonstrates the theoretical value of the SCST framework in understanding SG-related pathological processes, and further extends it to fields such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and metabolic diseases. Based on this framework, we critically evaluate SG-targeted intervention strategies. We focus on therapeutic avenues including regulating molecular components and networks, inhibiting the formation of pathological condensates, promoting SG disassembly, and restoring clearance pathways, while emphasizing the preservation of the stress-adaptation capacity of physiological SG. Together, this work provides new theoretical insights for therapeutic strategies and clinical translation aimed at restoring SG dynamics.

title: Revealing the Hydration Structure and Association Behavior of Aqueous Sodium Sulfate Solutions.
abstract: We conducted a comprehensive examination of the concentration-dependent structural evolution of aqueous Na2SO4 solutions (1.076-3.150 mol/L) using wide-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS), empirical potential structure refinement (EPSR) modeling, Raman spectroscopy, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Na+ adopts a predominantly six-coordinated local environment; the average Na-OW(H2O) coordination numbers (CNs) obtained from EPSR and MD simulations decrease from 5.1 to 3.5 and from 5.4 to 4.8, respectively, with increasing concentration, confirming that SO42- progressively enters the first hydration shell of Na+ to form contact ion pairs (CIPs). The Na-OS(SO42-) CNs increase from 1.0 to 2.3 (EPSR) and from 0.6 to 1.1 (MD), while total oxygen coordination around Na+ remains about six. For SO42-, the first hydration shell maintains rigidity with a well-defined S-OW(H2O) distance of 3.69 Å. SO42--H2O hydrogen bonds (H-bonds) are stronger than H2O-H2O ones, but their occupancy diminishes with concentration, suggesting that SO42- acts as a mild, concentration-dependent structure maker whose ordering influence on the H-bond network attenuates toward saturation. Raman spectroscopy shows blue shifts in both S-O and O-H stretching vibrations, supporting the transition from isolated hydrated ions to CIPs and the associated reorganization of the H-bond network. Two distinct CIP configurations are identified: monodentate (rNa-S ≈ 3.51 Å) and bidentate (rNa-S ≈ 3.03 Å), the former becoming more prevalent at higher concentrations. In concentrated solutions, further association leads to the formation of triple-ion clusters, multiple-ion clusters, and complex chainlike structures. DFT calculations further indicate that within finite-sized clusters ([NaSO4(H2O)12]- and Na2SO4(H2O)12), Na+ preferentially forms CIPs with SO42-, and the monodentate configuration is more stable than the bidentate one. These results provide a quantitative molecular-level picture of ion hydration and association in aqueous Na2SO4 solutions, offering insights that may help inform the understanding of the supercooling and phase separation phenomena relevant to Na2SO4·10H2O phase-change materials.

title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy.
abstract: The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

title: Structure-Based Design of Potent Pan-YTHDF Ligands.
abstract: The reader proteins YTHDF1-3 recognize m6A-RNA in the cytosol. Here, we present a structure-based medicinal chemistry campaign that culminated in the pan-YTHDF inhibitor 34 (Kd = 0.14 μM for YTHDF2 by calorimetry), which is selective against YTHDC1 and YTHDC2. The high-resolution crystal structures of the complex of YTHDF2 with six members of the series validate the structure-based design. Using the structural information, we designed compound 31 (IC50 = 0.22 μM for YTHDF2) and a negative control, i.e., its methylated analogue 31b. The cellular thermal shift assay provides evidence of YTHDF2 target engagement in cells for inhibitors 34 and 31, while the negative control 31b is inactive. Compounds 34 and 31 inhibit the proliferation of the AML cell lines MOLM-13 and THP-1. The inhibition of the YTHDF readers by 31 increases the level and stability of the transcript of TNFRSF1B. This renders THP-1 cells more sensitive to TNF-α-induced toxicity.

title: Mass Spectrometry-Guided Discovery of Plant-Derived Antiviral Candidates Against SARS-CoV-2: Analytical Strategies, Mechanisms, and Translational Challenges.
abstract: Plant-derived natural products are a promising source of antiviral compounds; however, their chemical complexity complicates metabolite identification and biological validation. Mass spectrometry (MS) provides powerful analytical tools to characterize phytochemicals with potential activity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). This review critically examines the applications of liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) in metabolite profiling, molecular networking, dereplication, and structural characterization. The integration of MS with nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, molecular docking, network pharmacology, and multiomics approaches is discussed to highlight their complementary roles in compound identification, candidate prioritization, and mechanistic investigation. Representative studies involving flavonoids, phenolic compounds, alkaloids, and terpenoids are evaluated regarding their proposed interactions with SARS-CoV-2 targets, including the main protease, papain-like protease, RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, spike protein, and host entry factors. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing tentative metabolite annotations and computational predictions from experimentally confirmed compound identities, target inhibition, and antiviral efficacy. Key limitations include incomplete spectral libraries, analytical variability, uncertain structural assignments, and insufficient experimental validation. Integrating high-confidence MS characterization with biochemical assays, target-engagement studies, cell-based antiviral evaluations, and pharmacological investigations is essential for strengthening mechanistic evidence. Overall, this review highlights the importance of rigorous analytical characterization and complementary experimental validation in advancing plant-derived natural products toward credible antiviral leads.

title: Single-molecule quantitative analysis of mechanical stability and unfolding kinetics of intermolecular G-quadruplexes.
abstract: Intermolecular G-quadruplexes (Inter-G4s) are implicated in long-range nucleic acid interactions, transcriptional regulation, and phase separation, yet how RNA/DNA strand composition shapes their mechanical stability and folding behavior remains poorly understood. Heterotypic RNA-DNA (R-D) Inter-G4s are particularly difficult to resolve because ensemble measurements cannot readily distinguish them from coexisting RNA-RNA (R-R) and DNA-DNA (D-D) assemblies. We developed Inter-GDP, a single-molecule platform that tethers two G-rich strands within one DNA construct, enabling repeated Inter-G4 folding and unfolding measurements. We established the platform using CSB II and two additional G4-forming sequences derived from structurally resolved bimolecular DNA G4s. Across three sequence contexts, the mean unfolding force followed the same ordering, R-R > D-D > R-D. BG4 responses were sequence- and construct-dependent, with reduced mean unfolding forces observed for Inter-G4 constructs associated with parallel bulk CD signatures. Simulations of a D-D Inter-G4 model suggested local conformational remodeling and lower G-quartet-core hydrogen-bond counts in BG4-containing trajectories. Together, our work establishes Inter-GDP as a single-molecule method for quantitative analysis of Inter-G4 mechanical stability and protein-associated effects.

title: Photo-Removable CRISPR-Cas12a Systems for Programmable Translational Modulation.
abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for developing new therapeutics and biotechnologies due to its inherent ability to express proteins. However, the lack of precise control over protein expression remains a critical limitation for mRNA-based biomedical applications. Herein, we developed a novel photoactivatable mRNA translational modulation strategy that leverages a photoremovable Cas12a-crRNA ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex as a programmable translational modulator. This RNP consists of Cas12a and a crRNA engineered with photocleavable (PC) linkers in its spacer region. The resulting binary complex binds specifically to the 5'-untranslated region (5'-UTR) of target mRNAs and inhibits translational initiation. Upon light irradiation, the PC-linkers are cleaved, leading to RNP dissociation and rapid restoration of protein expression. This strategy demonstrated robust phototriggered protein expression both in vitro (firefly luciferase) and in living cells (firefly luciferase, EGFP, and mCherry). Furthermore, the therapeutic potential of this approach was demonstrated in Hep3B cells, where phototriggered translation of tumor suppressor p53 mRNA successfully induced apoptosis. Our study demonstrates an innovative attempt at employing photoremovable RNP to modulate mRNA translation and provides distinct insights for rational exploration of mRNA-based precise therapeutics.

title: The WRKY transcription factor FaWRKY71 modulates the response of strawberry to drought stress.
abstract: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) is a high-value horticultural crop whose productivity and fruit quality are severely compromised under drought conditions. To minimize the impact of water deficit, plants deploy complex regulatory networks that coordinate physiological and molecular responses, many of which are governed by transcription factors. Among these, members of the WRKY family are recognized as key regulators of stress-induced signalling cascades. In this study, we identified and functionally characterized a ripening-induced WRKY transcription factor, FaWRKY71, that is strongly associated with drought responses in strawberry. Suppression of FaWRKY71 expression through RNA interference revealed alterations in biological processes linked predominantly to the 'response to abiotic stimulus', indicating its pivotal role in adaptive stress pathways. Transactivation assays confirmed a glutathione S-transferase (FaGST17), a cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase (FaCAD3), and an abscisic stress ripening protein-like protein (FaASR) as direct downstream targets of FaWRKY71, validating its regulatory capacity. Moreover, transgenic strawberry lines overexpressing FaWRKY71 exhibited enhanced antioxidant defences characterized by increased peroxidase and catalase activities when compared with nontransgenic controls. These biochemical changes were consistent with improved tolerance to drought-induced oxidative stress. Collectively, our findings establish FaWRKY71 as a central component of the transcriptional network that integrates fruit development and abiotic stress adaptation. The dual role of FaWRKY71 in ripening regulation and stress resilience highlights its potential as a promising target for genetic strategies aimed at improving both fruit quality and drought tolerance in strawberry.

title: Source-Associated Proteomic Signatures of Bone Marrow-, Dental Pulp-, and Periodontal Ligament-Stem Cell-Conditioned Media.
abstract: Tissue origin contributes to mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) heterogeneity and may influence the molecular composition of MSC-derived conditioned media (MSC-CM). This study compared conditioned media from bone marrow MSC (BMSC-CM), dental pulp stem cell (DPSC-CM), and periodontal ligament stem cell (PDLSC-CM). MSC were characterized according to established criteria, and CM generated under serum-free conditions were analyzed by label-free liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Global proteomic variation was assessed by principal component analysis, correlation, and hierarchical clustering. The common proteome was characterized using Gene Ontology Biological Process (GO:BP), Reactome, and regenerative-associated categories. Differential abundance was analyzed using donor-blocked limma modeling, with differentially abundant proteins (DEPs) defined by Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 0.5. A common quantitative proteome of 1,400 proteins was identified. No protein met the predefined criterion for reproducible source-selective detection. Global analyses showed source- and donor-associated variation, with BMSC-CM relatively distinct and greater overlap between DPSC- and PDLSC-CM. The common proteome represented extracellular-matrix-, wound-healing-, immune-, angiogenic-, proliferative-, migration-, survival-, skeletal-, and neurogenesis-related processes. BMSC-referenced analysis identified differences in GO and Reactome protein sets, whereas none of the 14 regenerative-associated categories differed significantly after multiple-testing correction. Differential-abundance analysis identified 145 DEPs between BMSC- and PDLSC-CM, 136 between BMSC- and DPSC-CM, and 494 between donor-matched DPSC- and PDLSC-CM. Directional enrichment associated BMSC-CM-higher proteins with developmental, migration, adhesion, morphogenesis, extracellular-matrix, and skeletal-related processes; PDLSC-CM-higher proteins with extracellular-matrix, collagen, adhesion, skeletal-development, and glycosaminoglycan processes; and DPSC-CM-higher proteins predominantly with nucleic-acid- and RNA-related processes in the donor-matched comparison. Overall, the three MSC-CM sources shared a regenerative-associated proteomic profile but differed substantially in relative protein abundance. The pronounced differences between donor-matched DPSC- and PDLSC-CM provide particularly strong evidence that tissue origin contributes to MSC-CM composition and support source-specific functional validation.

title: Viral Suppressor p20 Modulates Superoxide Accumulation by Interacting with Alcohol Dehydrogenase to Facilitate Mycovirus Replication in Fusarium graminearum.
abstract: Mycoviruses are emerging as novel biocontrol resources against fungal diseases, including Fusarium head blight and crown rot in wheat caused by Fusarium graminearum. Our previous research showed that the mycovirus FgHV1 encodes p20, an RNA silencing suppressor that also induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) in tobacco. However, the mechanism by which p20 modulates host redox status and facilitates viral replication remains unclear. Here, we show that p20 expression in F. graminearum leads to increased superoxide anion accumulation without affecting hydrogen peroxide tolerance. We identified FGSG_07683, a (2R,3R)-2,3-butanediol dehydrogenase involved in NAD/NADH-dependent redox reactions, as a p20-interacting protein. Deletion of FGSG_07683 elevated superoxide anion levels and increased FgHV1 accumulation, while the NAD+/NADH ratio decreased significantly. In vitro enzymatic assays showed that p20 markedly inhibits FGSG_07683 activity. Notably, FgV1, a mycovirus that does not encode p20, did not show increased viral accumulation or reduce the NAD+/NADH ratio in the FGSG_07683 deletion mutant. These findings suggest that p20 interacts with and directly inhibits FGSG_07683 dehydrogenase activity, thereby disrupting NAD+/NADH homeostasis, leading to mitochondrial electron leakage and superoxide accumulation, which in turn facilitates FgHV1 replication. Our study reveals a novel mechanism by which a viral suppressor protein modulates host redox to promote mycovirus replication.

title: Glycosylation of the Premembrane Protein Is Required for Dengue Virus Replication in Both C6/36 and Vero Cells.
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne, positive sense, single-stranded RNA virus that includes four serotypes (DENV1-4) that are further divided into distinct genotypes within a serotype. DENV causes approximately 100 million human infections each year. DENV virions encode a capisd surrounded by a lipid bilayer that encodes two glycoproteins, E and prM. During virion maturation, the premembrane protein (prM) is cleaved to form a mature virion, which includes partially mature and fully mature particles. The maturity state of the DENV virion affects both the infectivity of DENVs and the ability of antibodies to neutralize the virus. The prM glycoprotein is glycosylated and highly conserved across all DENVs. In particular, the N-linked glycosylation site at position 69 is present in over 99% of DENV genomes. In this manuscript, we investigated the importance of the N69 glycosylation site by generating both DENV2 and DENV4 loss-of-function viruses. These N69 glycosylation knockout viruses were generated by introducing a single amino acid mutation at site 69. Neither mutant virus had detectable titers despite multiple passages in vitro. To further investigate the importance of the glycosylation site, we generated another variation in which the N-linked glycosylation site was repositioned to a site proximal to residue 69. One of these proximal-glycosylation mutants showed viral replication at levels that approached wild-type (WT) DENV strains. Overall, this study demonstrated the importance of retaining an N-linked glycan on the prM protein at position 69 for DENV infectivity of mosquito cells and that inserting a glycosylation site in close proximity to position 69 may restore infectivity in some DENV4 strains.

title: Diversity of RNA Virus Populations Is Increased in the Presence of Engineered Synonymous Mutations That Disrupt RNA Structural Elements.
abstract: Previous studies have shown that engineered mutants of cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) with synonymous changes in the coat protein (CP) open reading frame (ORF), accumulate de novo amino acid (aa) substitutions in the CP when passaged in planta. To explore this phenomenon further, we applied whole-genome sequencing to assess the repeatability and extent of these de novo substitutions. Infectious mutants were engineered to contain synonymous changes in one of four ORF stem-loop (SL) structures, SL1362, SL1439, SL1745 and SL1816, or in a highly conserved structure, SL2073, in the 3' untranslated region. These changes occurred either in the loop or stem, thereby either maintaining or disrupting the predicted SL structure. The mutants were inoculated and then passaged on plants of Nicotiana tabacum, after which the full-length viral sequence (8 kb) was sequenced by an amplicon tiling approach using the Illumina Nextera platform. Across the whole genome, a statistically significant increase (all mutants vs. all wild-type) in de novo single nucleotide polymorphisms (synonymous and non-synonymous) occurred across the mutants as minor (≥10%) and dominant populations, which is suggestive of compensatory genome-wide epistatic changes induced by changes in SLs. Importantly, the results corroborated previous findings by confirming the repeated emergence of substitution P77L in the CP, while also identifying novel substitutions, particularly in the replication-associated 1a protein. This study provides additional genome-wide evidence on a newly described phenomenon, paving the way for additional studies on the function of these de novo changes.

title: Identification and Characterization of Wenshan Mosquito Virus, a Putative Novel Bisegmented RNA Virus from Mosquitoes in Yunnan Province, China.
abstract: Mosquito-associated viruses pose significant public health threats globally, with Yunnan Province in southwestern China representing a critical hotspot for arboviral emergence. In this study, 2612 female mosquitoes belonging to three species (Culex tritaeniorhynchus, Anopheles sinensis, and Culex quinquefasciatus) were collected from Wenshan during summer 2023. Viral metatranscriptomic analysis identified a novel bisegmented positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, designated Wenshan mosquito virus (WSMV). Its genome comprises 4741 nucleotides across two segments: Segment 1 (3127 nt) encodes an S39 family peptidase and an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), while Segment-2 (1614 nt) encodes a capsid protein and a hypothetical protein. Pairwise nucleotide identity analysis revealed 87.62% and 86.96% identity with Hubei mosquito virus 2 (HMV-2) for Segments 1 and 2, respectively. Given the absence of established species demarcation criteria for this lineage, WSMV is described as a putative novel virus within the HMV-2-related group. Phylogenetic analyses using a common taxon set placed WSMV consistently with HMV-2 across both segments. WSMV was detected in Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles sinensis pools (MIR 2.08 and 1.54 per 1000, respectively), but not in the limited number of Culex quinquefasciatus pools tested; the host range of WSMV therefore remains to be fully defined. This study expands knowledge of mosquito-associated viral diversity in Yunnan's border regions and provides a molecular foundation for future investigations.

title: Multi-Omic Profiling and Functional Validation Identify an NF-κB-Centered Pro-Survival Network Underlying Resistance to Oncolytic VSV in Prostate Cancer Cells.
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of oncolytic viruses is often limited by tumor cells that resist virus-mediated killing. Here, we investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance to Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV) in PC3 cells, an aggressive, metastatic prostate cancer cell line, using the VSV-sensitive LNCaP cell line as a comparator. RNA sequencing revealed that, relative to untreated cells, VSV-infected PC3 cells upregulated both pro-apoptotic genes, including BIM, PUMA, and NOXA, and anti-apoptotic and antiviral genes, including A20 and RIG-I. In addition, genes associated with antiviral and pro-survival pathways, including NF-κB and PI3K-Akt signaling, were more highly expressed in PC3 cells than in LNCaP cells. At baseline, PC3 cells also exhibited elevated expression of pro-survival genes, including BCL-xL, MCL1, and CK2, compared to LNCaP cells. Complementary phospho-protein array analyses identified increased phosphorylation of proteins associated with NF-κB, PI3K-Akt, and MSK1 signaling in VSV-infected PC3 cells relative to infected LNCaP cells. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of BCL-2 family proteins or NF-κB signaling sensitized PC3 cells to VSV-induced cell death. These findings support a model in which NF-κB-centered pro-survival signaling networks contribute to the resistant phenotype of PC3 cells and suggest that combining oncolytic virotherapy with targeted inhibitors may improve therapeutic efficacy in resistant prostate cancers.

title: Physicochemical Characterization, Manufacturing, and Stability of Liposomal Drug Delivery Systems: From Formulation Design to Pharmaceutical Translation.
abstract: Liposomal drug delivery systems have evolved into clinically relevant platforms for delivering small molecules, biologics, and vaccines. Nevertheless, a persistent translational gap remains between promising laboratory-scale formulations and reproducible pharmaceutical products. This review provides a practical framework linking liposome formulation, physicochemical characterization, manufacturing, and stability to pharmaceutical translation. Particular emphasis is placed on relationships between critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, including vesicle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, lamellarity, encapsulation efficiency, drug loading, and in vitro release behavior. Preparation and cargo-loading strategies are discussed across conventional research-scale methods and approaches with potential for scalable manufacturing. Microfluidic production of conventional liposomes is distinguished from the manufacture of structurally distinct RNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles. Purification strategies and analytical determination of encapsulation efficiency are examined, with attention to the distinction between separation techniques and quantitative analytical methods. Lamellarity is highlighted as a structural determinant of encapsulation capacity, membrane organization, and release behavior, with complementary assessment by cryo-TEM, 31P-NMR, and small-angle X-ray scattering. Quality-control challenges associated with aggregation, fusion, cargo leakage, phospholipid hydrolysis, oxidation, and sterilization are also considered. Dry-state stabilization through lyophilization and spray drying is discussed for its potential to improve long-term stability and reduce cold-chain dependence. Ligand-targeted liposomes introduce additional requirements for surface characterization and biological evaluation, while approved products and investigational formulations illustrate achievements and limitations in clinical translation. Overall, this review emphasizes the importance of establishing relationships between formulation composition, processing, structural organization, stability, and functional performance to support more reproducible development and informed pharmaceutical translation.

title: Substitution of Hydrophobic Tails on Hydrophilic Polyethyleneimine via Urethane Linkages Yields Cleavable Lipopolymers with Effective mRNA Delivery.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery to circulating, suspension-growing cells remains challenging due to their inherent barriers to mRNA uptake. This study aimed to develop a novel lipopolymer-based nanoparticle (NP) platform to improve mRNA delivery and gene expression in suspension-growing cells and investigate the influence of NP physicochemical properties on delivery efficiency. Methods: Polyethyleneimine (PEI) was functionalized with lipidic moieties through degradable urethane linkages to generate lipopolymers with varying lipid modifications. mRNA delivery and gene expression were evaluated in suspension-growing myeloid leukemia cells in vitro and following systemic administration in mice. The effects of incorporating the anionic additive Trans-Booster (TB) into binary and ternary NPs were investigated. Machine learning analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was performed across 125 formulations to identify key physicochemical determinants of delivery performance. Results: Geraniol-conjugated PEI demonstrated the highest gene expression among the lipid modifications investigated. Incorporation of TB further enhanced transfection efficiency by modulating NP surface charge. In mice, binary NPs preferentially enhanced mRNA delivery to the spleen and lungs, whereas ternary NPs promoted gene expression primarily in the liver and intestine. SHAP analysis identified TB-charge interactions, TB presence, steric hindrance, lipid double bonds, and effective hydrophobicity as key determinants of mRNA delivery efficacy. Conclusions: The developed lipopolymer-based NP platform demonstrates potential for improving mRNA delivery to suspension-growing cells. Lipid functionalization and TB incorporation influenced transfection efficiency and tissue distribution, while SHAP analysis provided insights into the physicochemical factors governing delivery performance. These findings support further development of engineered lipopolymer NPs for mRNA-based applications targeting circulating cells.

title: [(Trimethylsilyl)cyclopropenyl]rifampicinium-A Novel Antitubercular Antibiotic Active Versus NIAID Category A/B Priority Pathogens.
abstract: Rifampicin was selectively quaternized at the distal methyl piperazine nitrogen with the chemical compound 3-bromo-1-(trimethylsilyl)-1-propyne in >99% purity. A nitrogen ylide-driven rearrangement finally left isolated 4'-[(1S)-2-(trimethylsilyl)cycloprop-2-en-1-yl]rifampicinium-4-olate (TPR). The intermediate product 4'-[3-(trimethylsilyl)prop-2-yn-1-yl]rifampicinium-4-olate was not isolable. TPR was tested against the Mycobacterium tuberculosis laboratory strain H37Rv, and against a panel of six clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis covering acquired resistance towards isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, streptomycin, kanamycin A, amikacin, capreomycin/viomycin, and ethionamide/prothionamide. TPR was (3.7-1.8)-fold (molar) more potent than rifampicin against M. tuberculosis H37Rv, and was elucidated to act bactericidal, extra- and intracellularly, and under low-oxygen conditions versus M. tuberculosis, while exerting no cell cytotoxicity. TPR was highly active against an MDR-TB clinical isolate carrying the bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase β subunit enzyme protein RpoB Asp435(516)Val mutation conferring resistance to rifampicin. TPR in co-administration with the steroidal (gluco)cortico(stero)id nuclear receptor antagonist ORG34517 was highly active versus Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA and MRSA) and Streptococcus pneumoniae [including penicillin- and (lev)ofloxacin-resistant isolates]. Bacillus sp. are very susceptible to TPR, predicting TPR's activity towards sporulating B. anthracis (anthrax). In the Gram-negative sector, TPR showed high activity versus drug-sensitive Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1 biovar El Tor serotype Inaba, and Liberibacter crescens BT-1T. TPR showed remarkable in vivo activity against Francisella tularensis, far superior to the resistance-inducing and disease-relapse-suffering rifampicin. The efficacious in vivo activity of TPR versus F. tularensis Schu S4 was shown to be synergistic with doxycycline, to be devoid of any induction of resistance development, and to evoke 100% cure of murine tularemia without any disease relapse off-treatment. The superior antimicrobial in vivo activity of TPR in comparison to rifampicin (and other antibiotics) is proposed to rely on covalent inactivation of the bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase β subunit RpoB enzyme protein by the TPR aromatic split-off product (trimethylsilyl)cyclopropen(yl)ium.

title: From Supportive Care to Precision Medicine: Emerging Therapies for Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa.
abstract: Background: Inherited epidermolysis bullosa (EB) comprises monogenic disorders characterised by tissue fragility, recurrent blistering, chronic wounds and multisystem complications. Although multidisciplinary supportive care remains fundamental, it cannot correct the molecular defect or prevent cumulative tissue damage. This narrative review examines emerging disease-modifying therapies for inherited EB, emphasising their application in clinical practice. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched using terms relating to EB subtypes and pharmacological, gene-, RNA-, protein-, cell- and genome-editing therapies. Reference lists, clinical guidelines, consensus statements and regulatory documents were also examined. Clinical studies and preclinical investigations were synthesised qualitatively; no meta-analysis was performed. Results: Recent advances have expanded treatment beyond conventional wound care. Oleogel-S10 enhances endogenous wound healing independently of genotype, whereas beremagene geperpavec delivers functional COL7A1 copies directly to dystrophic EB wounds. Prademagene zamikeracel combines ex vivo correction of autologous keratinocytes with epidermal grafting, offering potentially sustained closure of selected chronic wounds. Nevertheless, these treatments remain predominantly local and do not fully address generalised skin fragility or extracutaneous disease. Mesenchymal stromal cells, haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, recombinant type VII collagen, RNA-based treatments and genome editing may provide broader or more durable benefits, but evidence remains limited, and concerns regarding delivery, safety, durability and accessibility persist. Conclusions: Precision and regenerative therapies are transforming EB management but remain complementary to multidisciplinary supportive care. Clinical evaluation should extend beyond wound closure to include pain, function, growth, quality of life and caregiver burden. Long-term surveillance and personalised combination strategies are essential to determine whether early treatment can safely alter the natural history of EB.

title: Reduced Susceptibility to Transmissible Gastroenteritis Virus in Porcine ANPEP N783A-Edited Cell Clone.
abstract: Transmissible gastroenteritis virus (TGEV) uses porcine aminopeptidase N (pAPN), encoded by the alanyl aminopeptidase gene (ANPEP), as a cellular receptor. Complete ANPEP disruption can restrict TGEV infection but may compromise APN-associated functions. Here, we investigated whether limited modification of pAPN at residue N783 could reduce cellular susceptibility to TGEV without eliminating APN protein expression or the aminopeptidase activity examined in this study. Prime editing was then used to generate an ANPEP N783A-edited clone in PE7-expressing PK15 cells. The edited clone retained APN protein expression, cell-normalized aminopeptidase activity, and membrane-associated APN staining. Following TGEV exposure at multiplicities of infection of 0.01, 0.1, and 1, intracellular RNA containing the TGEV nucleocapsid (N) gene sequence at 24 h post-infection was reduced by approximately 83%, 73%, and 74%, respectively. The edited cells also maintained higher relative viability under most infected conditions, with the greatest difference observed at 36 hpi and an MOI of 1 (83% vs. 42%). Relative LDH release was reduced by approximately 28% and 22% at MOIs of 0.1 and 1, respectively. The edited cells also displayed weaker dead-cell fluorescence and milder morphological damage. These findings provide preliminary, clone-specific evidence that an ANPEP N783A-edited clone can display reduced susceptibility to TGEV while retaining the APN-related phenotypes examined.

title: Viral Metagenomic Characterization of the Tick Virome in Tibet and Phylogenetic Analysis of Representative RNA Viruses.
abstract: Viral metagenomic sequencing was used to characterize viral sequences in six pools comprising 90 ticks collected in Tibet in 2026. Viruses belonging to 35 families were identified based on read-level taxonomic assignments. Chuviridae, Phenuiviridae, and Rhabdoviridae were prominent RNA viral families in the pooled profiles. Five representative RNA viral sequences were examined by annotation and phylogenetic analysis: one Phenuiviridae-associated partial L-region sequence, two Chuviridae-associated sequences, and two Rhabdoviridae-associated partial L-region sequences. Their recovered L-protein regions were closely related to previously reported tick-associated viruses, with amino acid identities of 98.67-99.95% over the compared regions. The Phenuiviridae-associated sequence grouped with Uukuvirus-related sequences, the Chuviridae-associated sequences with Mivirus-related references, and the Rhabdoviridae-associated sequences near Deltarhabdovirinae references. Chu4909 has read coverage across the assembled sequence, but its circular configuration remains putative, and its topology and genome completeness remain unconfirmed. No novel viruses were identified in this study. These observations provide additional sequence data from Tibetan tick pools. The sequence detections were not independently confirmed by PCR/RT-PCR and do not establish individual-tick infection prevalence, active infection, or viral replication.

title: Identification of a Major-Effect Locus on Tomato Chromosome 8 Associated with Tolerance to Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus (ToBRFV).
abstract: Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) is an emerging threat to tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) production worldwide, and new resistance sources are needed for sustainable disease control. We investigated the inheritance and genetic architecture of tolerance to ToBRFV in an F2 population derived from a resistant line carrying an introgression from Solanum habrochaites LA1777. After mechanical inoculation, 94 of 128 F2 plants remained asymptomatic and 34 were susceptible, fitting the 3:1 ratio expected for a single dominant determinant. DAS-ELISA on apical non-inoculated leaves showed that asymptomatic plants carrying the LA1777 allele were systemically infected, indicating tolerance rather than resistance. Genotyping of 110 F2 individuals by methylation-content-sensitive double-digest restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing (MCSeEd) yielded 70,379 high-confidence variants. Genome-wide association analysis identified 78 significant variants defining an approximately 3.40 Mb interval on chromosome 8, with the strongest association at SL4.0ch08_58258671, independently confirmed with TASSEL5, GAPIT3, and PLINK2. The interval contains biologically plausible candidate genes encoding an RPP13-like disease resistance protein, a lectin receptor-like kinase, transcription factors, and a DEAD-box RNA helicase. Of four cleaved amplified polymorphic sequence (CAPS) markers developed, two showed reproducible marker-trait co-segregation and were concordant with phenotypes in naturally infected greenhouse populations. These results provide a major chromosome 8 locus and breeding-ready markers for ToBRFV tolerance in tomato.

title: Long Non-Coding RNAs in Metastatic Dormancy and Drug-Tolerant Persistence: Regulators of Residual-Cell Plasticity.
abstract: Cancer can recur when cells that survive dissemination or treatment resume growth. A smaller metastatic burden can reflect slower proliferation, greater immune clearance or fewer viable residual cells. We review long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) perturbation studies that separate these effects. In breast cancer models, NR2F1-AS1 increases NR2F1 translation. This favors dissemination but limits proliferation in the lung. BORG promotes outgrowth from latency through tripartite motif-containing protein 28 (TRIM28), while MALAT1 helps emerging metastases survive immune attack. These experiments illustrate why a change in lesion burden can point to different interventions. The same question arises in drug-tolerant persistence (DTP). Drug-response studies identify candidate RNAs, but few test whether the RNA is needed once reversibly tolerant cells have formed. For relapse prevention, experiments need to count viable residual cells separately from growing lesions and establish when the RNA interaction matters.

title: Spike mRNA Encoding JN.1-RBD Elicits Broad Omicron-Neutralizing Antibodies and Protects Against Infection.
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the single-stranded RNA virus responsible for Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), continues to circulate globally, with the emergence of antigenically distinct variants posing ongoing challenges to vaccine effectiveness. In particular, Omicron subvariants harbor numerous mutations in the receptor-binding domain (RBD), which contribute to immune evasion and reduced susceptibility to neutralization by antibodies. Previous COVID-19 mRNA vaccines encoding the spike (S) protein of the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 or early variants of concern have demonstrated limited efficacy against Omicron subvariants, underscoring the need for next-generation vaccines capable of eliciting broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies against Omicron and providing cross-protection against antigenically distinct variants. In this study, we designed an mRNA vaccine encoding a conserved Omicron-S backbone incorporating the JN.1 RBD (S-JN1-RBD), formulated the mRNA with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), and evaluated its neutralizing activity and protective efficacy. This mRNA-LNP formulation exhibited an appropriate particle size and high thermal stability. It elicited cross-reactive antibodies against S proteins harboring diverse Omicron-RBDs, resulting in broad neutralizing activity against multiple pseudotyped and authentic SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants. Importantly, this vaccine conferred cross-protection against challenge with the heterologous, antigenically divergent XBB.1.5 Omicron subvariant in human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-transgenic mice. Furthermore, passive transfer of immune sera protected mice against infection with the Omicron-KP.3 subvariant, providing additional evidence of the vaccine's broad protective potential. These findings underscore the potential of the designed mRNA immunogen to elicit broad-spectrum neutralizing antibody responses and to confer cross-protection against diverse and emerging SARS-CoV-2 subvariants.

title: Plant ER Proteostasis Through a Framework of Protein Load, Processing Capacity and Clearance.
abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) must coordinate protein entry, maturation and removal to sustain plant growth and stress adaptation. Although unfolded protein response (UPR) signaling and quality control pathways are well characterized, their activation alone does not reveal which process limits ER function. Here, we propose a Load, Capacity and Clearance (LCC) framework that organizes these mechanisms by their effects on protein flux. The Load module regulates protein influx, Capacity supports productive folding, maturation, assembly and export, and Clearance removes misfolded proteins and selected portions of the ER. We examine transcriptional remodeling, translational regulation, regulated RNA decay, ER-associated degradation and selective autophagy, distinguishing mechanisms demonstrated during plant ER stress from those established in other stress responses. How these processes are coordinated, and how much each contributes to ER recovery, remain to be quantified. We outline testable predictions and experimental approaches to determine which processes limit recovery, how the timing of influx restoration affects recovery, and whether combined measurements of influx, processing and clearance explain or predict stress outcomes better than UPR markers alone. This framework may guide strategies to improve plant stress resilience and recombinant protein production.

title: Integrated Comparative Analysis Reveals Structural Diversification and Functional Associations of Arabidopsis DEAD-Box RNA Helicases.
abstract: DEAD-box RNA helicases (RHs) constitute one of the largest and most conserved families of RNA metabolism factors in eukaryotes, yet the evolutionary relationships and functions of many plant members remain unresolved. We present an integrated comparative analysis of the Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis) DEAD-box RH family by combining structural curation, orthology inference, comparative analyses of protein features, and cross-species comparisons of biological pathway enrichment among co-expressed genes. Structural curation established a reference set of 53 intact genes and four putative pseudogenes (RH43, RH44, RH45, and RH55) for subsequent analyses. Orthology inference using the DRSC Integrative Ortholog Prediction Tool (DIOPT) identified high- and moderate-confidence orthologous relationships, revealed conserved helicase lineages and putative lineage-specific expansions, and enabled systematic comparisons with Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) and Homo sapiens (humans). Comparative analyses of protein features revealed that non-canonical DExD-box motif variants occur in 10 of the 57 Arabidopsis, three of the 26 yeast, and five of the 38 human DEAD-box RHs. Although the DECD variant appears to be shared across plant, fungal, and metazoan lineages, other variants show restricted or patchy distributions, as exemplified by the DEVD variant, whose distribution is consistent with its independent emergence in several lineages, indicating that the canonical DEAD sequence is not universally conserved. Annotated accessory motifs and domains were identified in only a small subset of proteins, although annotation-based counts probably underestimate their frequency, and the helicase core architecture was broadly conserved. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses of genes co-expressed with Arabidopsis DEAD-box RHs and their orthologs provided a basis for generating functional hypotheses for previously uncharacterized proteins, even in the absence of prior experimental evidence of ortholog function. Although these hypotheses require further investigation and experimental validation, the findings provide an integrated framework for investigating the structural and functional diversification of the Arabidopsis DEAD-box RH family. This approach may also be extended to other poorly characterized multigene families.

title: Metabolic Control of the Spliceosome in Cancer: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities.
abstract: Aberrant RNA splicing is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of cancer, yet the metabolic mechanisms that regulate spliceosome function remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that cellular metabolism can directly influence RNA processing by controlling the energy availability, metabolite concentrations, and post-translational modifications of spliceosomal proteins. In contrast to previous reviews that primarily examine how alternative splicing drives metabolic reprogramming or discuss individual metabolic pathways in isolation, this review integrates the reverse relationship-how cancer metabolism regulates the spliceosome itself. This mechanism-oriented narrative review examines the spliceosome as a metabolically responsive molecular machinery, with particular emphasis on pathways that generate therapeutically exploitable vulnerabilities. Methionine metabolism and S-adenosylmethionine availability regulate protein methylation through methionine adenosyltransferase 2A and protein arginine methyltransferase 5, while loss of methylthioadenosine phosphorylase creates a metabolically defined dependency that can be targeted pharmacologically. Polyamine-dependent metabolic shielding represents an emerging regulatory mechanism whereby polyamines can modulate the accessibility of selected spliceosomal phosphorylation sites and thereby influence alternative splicing; however, this mechanism has so far been demonstrated in a single prostate cancer study and has not yet been independently replicated. Additional metabolic inputs include adenosine triphosphate-dependent remodeling, divalent metal ions, acetyl-coenzyme A-dependent acetylation, and nutrient-sensitive glycosylation. These mechanisms collectively demonstrate that spliceosome activity is tightly integrated with cellular metabolic state. Therapeutically, MAT2A and PRMT5 inhibitors have entered clinical testing, whereas approaches targeting polyamine-dependent shielding, splicing kinases, or combined metabolic-spliceosomal vulnerabilities remain predominantly preclinical or conceptual.

title: The RNA/Protein Symmetry Hypothesis: Implications for the Origin of the Genetic Code.
abstract: The advent of the genetic code and translation would have been the most important event in the early evolutionary stage of primordial cells. Although many theories on the origin of the genetic code have been proposed, no definitive answer has yet been reached. In 2001, we proposed the RNA/protein symmetry theory for the origin of life, in which both RNAs and proteins coevolved, forming a stable metabolic complex from the very beginning of the origin of life. In this theory, the genetic information can be generated from existing cellular proteins through reverse translation, which proceeds in the 3' to 5' direction using a set of reverse transfer RNAs (rtRNAs). Here, the original model of reverse translation was revised by modifying the rtRNAs to naturally include forward translation. Inspired by the structures of the modified rtRNAs, we analyzed the relationship between the sizes of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids and the stability of each codon/anticodon pair for each amino acid. We found strong correlations between the molecular weights of the 18 amino acids excluding tryptophan and arginine and the ΔG values for the formation of each codon/anticodon duplex. These correlations may have implications for the origin of the genetic code.

title: Candidate Roles for Initiator Methionine Processing in Ribosome Assembly and Function: A Cross-Species Census.
abstract: How initiator methionine processing relates to ribosomal protein interfaces remains incompletely understood. This study integrated 68 ribosome structures from 61 species (1873 family-species records, 95 families) and characterized termini and published assembly intermediates to examine comparative associations and identify specific candidate interfaces. Residue-2 predictions agreed with 388 out of 393 characterized termini in 12 species. In 58 switching families, the burial-based RNA only versus exposed odds ratio for predicted retention was 0.31 (95% confidence interval 0.18-0.53) with family strata, 0.64 (0.32-1.29) with family by domain strata, and 0.76 (0.29-1.99) with family by clade strata; the reconstructed family by clade estimate was 1.21 (0.48-3.07). Common position scoring preserved the pooled RNA association, whereas matched phylogenetic estimates remained inconclusive and protein contact contrasts depended strongly on the scored position. An exploratory analysis of 21,485 reference proteomes identified a bacterial association at order, one out of five ranks tested, surviving within-domain but not three-domain multiplicity adjustment. Conserved permissive families showed no detected difference between RNA-contacting and protein-packed groups, and observed bS16 retention opposed a uniform cleavage requirement. At individual interfaces, uL15 and eL24 exhibited alternative terminal contact registers, while yeast uS12 and eS27 occupied supported RNA and protein interfaces, respectively, in pre-40S and mature particles. These comparisons extend processing-associated functional studies by identifying specific molecular interfaces and their assembly contexts. They prioritize uS12 and eS27 for investigating how terminal processing influences ribosome organization and function; the functional consequences at each site remain to be established.

title: First Record of Verticia fasciventris from Mainland China and Its Mitogenome (Diptera: Calliphoridae, Bengaliinae).
abstract: Verticia fasciventris Malloch, 1927 is a biologically distinctive blow fly whose larvae develop as internal parasitoids of soldiers of fungus-growing termites. Previously recorded from Malaysia and Hong Kong, China, its occurrence in mainland China has not been formally documented. In this study, we report V. fasciventris from mainland China for the first time, based on a male specimen collected in Yunnan Province, provide a redescription of the male, and document the first complete mitogenome of Verticia. The circular mitogenome is 15,586 base pairs in length and contains the typical set of 37 insect mitochondrial genes, including 13 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA (tRNA) genes, two ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes, and a control region. The gene arrangement of the mitogenome is consistent with the conventional pattern for Diptera. Phylogenetic analyses based on mitochondrial protein-coding and rRNA genes recovered Calliphoridae as monophyletic and supported Bengaliinae as sister to Rhiniinae. Within the limited sampling of Bengaliinae, V. fasciventris was recovered as sister to Tricyclea sp. These results expand the known distribution of V. fasciventris and provide new evidence for the phylogenetic placement of this termite-parasitoid genus.

title: BeetleFormer: A Sequence Transformer for Identifying Effective Double-Stranded RNAs in the Red Flour Beetle, Tribolium castaneum.
abstract: Selecting double-stranded ribonucleic acid (dsRNA) reagents remains a bottleneck in insect gene-function research and RNA interference (RNAi)-based pest management. We developed BeetleFormer to learn sequence patterns associated with RNAi screening outcomes in Tribolium castaneum. The model integrates multiscale convolutions, long-range attention, complementary-strand symmetry and sequence descriptors. Following previous dsRNA prescreening research, 14,821 iBeetle reagents meeting mortality or phenotype criteria were used as positives and 14,825 messenger RNA (mRNA) fragments as negative samples. Source genes and overlapping sequences were separated across training, validation and testing. On 6083 test sequences, BeetleFormer achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.978, accuracy 0.913 and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.831, compared with 0.888, 0.817 and 0.636 for an adapted convolutional-recurrent comparator. Ablations supported local processing and strand symmetry; AUC remained 0.976 after exact-length matching. External testing on 20 published dsRNAs and 20 mRNA negatives yielded AUC 0.928. Model interpretation revealed terminally concentrated sequence sensitivity and organized learned representations. These findings establish an improved sequence-based prescreen that turns genome-scale RNAi observations into candidate-selection evidence, supporting functional-genomics experiments and the development of RNAi-based pest control.

title: Advancing Precision siRNA Therapeutics for Osteoporosis Through Rational Design of Bone-Targeted Delivery Systems.
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a degenerative skeletal disorder driven by disrupted homeostasis between bone-forming osteoblasts and bone-resorbing osteoclasts. Conventional anti-osteoporotic therapeutics are hindered by insufficient bone-targeting efficacy, undesirable systemic adverse reactions, and prolonged treatment durations. Small interfering RNA (siRNA), a prototype of small nucleic acid therapeutics, enables specific silencing of pivotal bone metabolic genes and restores balanced bone remodeling via dual modulatory effects on osteogenic and osteoclastic cascades. Signaling pathways associated with bone formation drive osteoblast maturation, while bone resorption-related signaling pathways facilitate osteoclast differentiation. Targeting the key regulatory molecules of these pathways can suppress osteoclastic signaling or boost osteogenic activity, thereby restoring disrupted bone metabolic homeostasis. This review systematically summarizes siRNA chemical modification schemes and bone-homing nanodelivery platforms, dissects the underlying anti-osteoporotic mechanisms of nucleic acid therapeutics, discusses outstanding translational hurdles, and offers theoretical insights for the rational design of next-generation bone-targeted nucleic acid nanomedicines.

title: RNA Interference for Insect Pest Management: Linking dsRNA Structure-Function Relationships, Delivery Biology, and Field Performance.
abstract: RNA interference (RNAi) is a sequence-guided approach to insect pest management, but its efficacy depends on more than the choice of an essential target gene. The biological activity of exogenously applied double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is shaped by its molecular properties, extracellular stability, interactions with delivery materials, cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, and access to the RNAi machinery. This review examines these linked determinants and considers how differences in insect physiology contribute to variation in RNAi susceptibility.
