We discuss target-gene selection and sequence specificity alongside nuclease activity, gut barriers, endosomal processing, and systemic transport. Particular attention is given to nanomaterial-based formulations, including chitosan, liposomes, and layered double hydroxides, as well as microbial, symbiont-mediated, host-induced gene silencing (HIGS), and spray-induced gene silencing (SIGS) platforms. Their potential benefits are assessed in relation to formulation reproducibility, production costs, environmental fate, non-target exposure, and regulatory requirements. By connecting dsRNA structure-function relationships with delivery biology and application performance, this review identifies mechanistic questions and validation steps that must be addressed to develop reliable RNAi-based tools. RNAi is best regarded as a complementary component of integrated pest management, with field deployment requiring species-specific optimization and evidence-based environmental assessment.

title: Decoding Human Milk Lactoprotein Heterogeneity: From Genetic Variation to Proteoforms and Peptidoforms in a Comparative Mammalian Context.
abstract: Human milk proteins exhibit extensive molecular heterogeneity arising from genetic variation, transcript diversity, post-translational modifications, and proteolytic processing. This review integrates evidence on major human milk caseins and selected whey proteins within a genome-transcript-proteoform-peptidoform framework, incorporating comparative mammalian data where relevant. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing predicted molecular consequences, relationships supported by indirect evidence, and experimentally demonstrated molecular entities and transitions. Genomic variation and alternative RNA processing provide potential sources of primary-sequence diversity, whereas phosphorylation, glycosylation, and proteolysis further expand protein and peptide heterogeneity. Human β-casein provides a particularly informative example, with experimentally characterized phosphorylation- and glycosylation-defined proteoforms and corresponding modification-resolved peptidoforms. However, evidence remains uneven across molecular levels, and direct tracing from maternal genotype to expressed transcripts, secreted proteoforms, and downstream peptidoforms within the same individual remains limited. By identifying experimentally established relationships and unresolved molecular connections, this review provides an evidence-based framework for interpreting human milk lactoprotein heterogeneity and guiding future integrated proteogenomic investigations.

title: From Formulation Quality to Anti-Tumor Immunity: A Multimodal Imaging and Translational Framework for mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticle Cancer Vaccines in Preclinical Tumor Models.
abstract: mRNA-Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for cancer vaccines are often considered a linear progression, in which formulation, biodistribution, innate stimulation, antigen expression, and tumor control form a continuum. They are not. This review connects the manufacturing inputs and lipid composition to particle attributes, innate sensing, organ and cell exposure, cytosolic translation, antigen presentation, therapeutic response, and hepatic safety. This review aims to provide a mechanism-aligned framework from critical quality attributes (CQAs) and critical process parameters (CPPs) to innate sensing, multimodal imaging, and preclinical efficacy and safety that can be used to design and interpret preclinical studies of mRNA-LNP cancer vaccines, with explicit attention to orthotopic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) models. Principal findings: (i) total organ signal is an inadequate surrogate for productive delivery; the decisive variable is translation of antigen in a permissive antigen-presenting cell (APC) during a defined inflammatory window; (ii) formulation and process variables including size, PDI, encapsulation, RNA integrity and capping, lipid composition, PEG-lipid architecture, mixing conditions, and storage history alter this conversion; and (iii) multimodal imaging is most informative when carrier or payload tracking is paired with reporter or antigen expression, immune profiling, tumor response, and liver-safety assays. We propose a release-to-response architecture for preclinical studies and identify the evidence required for clinically interpretable pharmacology. We reviewed peer-reviewed studies on mRNA cancer vaccination, quantitative imaging, PDAC models, LNP quality-by-design, and formulation-dependent innate immunology. The total organ signal is an inadequate surrogate for productive delivery; the decisive variable is translating antigen into an antigen-presenting cell during a permissive inflammatory window. Particle size, polydispersity, encapsulation, RNA integrity and capping, lipid composition, PEG-lipid architecture, mixing conditions, and storage history can alter this conversion. Multimodal imaging is most informative when carrier or payload tracking is paired with reporter or antigen expression, immune profiling, tumor response, and liver safety assays. PDAC studies have shown that hepatic or splenic exposure can be either a liability or intentional immune reprogramming. We propose a release-to-response architecture for preclinical studies and identify the evidence required for clinically interpretable pharmacology.

title: Plant microRNA Mobility and Extracellular Vesicles: Current Understanding, Controversies and Therapeutic Potential of Plant-to-Animal Communication.
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a predominant class of small non-coding RNA (sRNA) which regulates target gene expression to occupy fundamental roles in growth, development, metabolism, stress responses, pathogen defence, and disease onset and progression. Traditionally viewed as intracellular regulators, the discovery that specific miRNAs can move between cells, tissues, organs, and even organisms has reshaped our understanding of the extent of their biological significance. In plants, miRNA mobility is a well-established component of long-distance signalling networks that coordinate phase changes across development, nutrient uptake and homeostasis, and responses to the external environment. In animals, extracellular miRNAs are transported within extracellular vesicles, protein complexes, and lipoproteins, where they mediate intercellular communication. More recently, the identification of extracellular RNA transport systems in both kingdoms has led to considerable investigation into cross-kingdom RNA communication. A growing body of evidence indicates that plant extracellular vesicles (PEVs) play important roles in the transport and protection of their harboured miRNA cargo. The strongest evidence supporting cross-kingdom RNA silencing originates from plant-pathogen systems, where PEVs transport regulatory sRNAs into invading pathogens to silence the activity of genes associated with virulence and pathogenicity. Alongside these exciting discoveries, PEVs are attracting even more attention as potential mediators of plant-to-animal communication, thus acting as natural nanocarriers for delivery of therapeutic RNAs. Several studies have reported that plant-derived miRNAs can be detected in animal tissues, wherein they maintain functionality to regulate the expression of targeted genes associated with cancer, viral infection, inflammation, and metabolism. However, the physiological significance of dietary plant miRNA uptake remains highly debated. While some investigations provide evidence supporting cross-kingdom regulation, other reports detail limited uptake, low bioavailability, and an insufficient final concentration in host tissues to elicit any form of biologically relevant effect. Consequently, plant-to-animal miRNA transfer remains one of the most actively debated topics in RNA biology. In this review, we outline the production and mobility of miRNA silencing signals in both the plant and animal systems, discuss the biogenesis and biological functions of PEVs, evaluate evidence supporting cross-kingdom RNA transfer, critically assess the controversies surrounding plant miRNA-directed regulation of mammalian target gene expression, and provide an informed discussion on the future directions in plant-to-animal miRNA transfer.

title: Unveiling the genetic architecture of primary aldosteronism: a multi-omics investigation into subtype-specific insights.
abstract: Hypertension is a global public health challenge, with primary aldosteronism (PA) being the most common cause of secondary hypertension. Understanding the genetic architecture of PA is crucial for identifying potential therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify genetic underpinnings associated with PA subtypes, including aldosterone-producing adenoma (APA) and bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (BAH). We conducted a genome-wide Mendelian randomization analysis using adrenal tissue-specific expression quantitative trait loci and hyperaldosteronism genomic data. Replication analysis was performed using a series of independent genome-wide association study datasets. Protein-protein interaction network, pathway enrichment analysis, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data, and Bayesian colocalization analysis were employed to validate and prioritize candidate genes. A total of 168 genes were identified as having causal relationships with PA subtypes. Pathway enrichment analysis highlighted aldosterone synthesis and lipid metabolism as key pathways. FBN2 emerged as the most significant gene associated with APA, showing enriched expression in aldosterone-producing cells and correlating with KCNJ5 gene expression. RXFP2 was identified as a robust candidate gene for BAH, with evidence of shared causal variants. Our study provided novel insights into the genetic inferences of PA subtypes, implicating FBN2 as a potential contributor to APA, and RXFP2 as a key contributor to BAH, respectively. Further experimental and clinical validations are required.

title: Actin-Related Protein 2/3 (Arp2/3)-Associated Gene Expression in Repetitive Head Impacts and Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy: Analysis of Two Human Transcriptomic Datasets.
abstract: We evaluated actin-related protein 2/3 (Arp2/3)-associated and SOX9/MEGF10 gene-expression modules in repetitive head impacts (RHI) and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). Public bulk RNA-sequencing data (GSE193407; 136 brains) and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data (GSE261807; 28 donors) were analyzed. Sensitivity analyses examined neuronal and astrocytic marker adjustment, cell-type selection, and alternative Arp2/3 module definitions. In bulk tissue, nominal CTE-stage associations with Arp2/3 (P = 0.0151) and SOX9/MEGF10 (P < 0.001) were attenuated after adjustment for neuronal and astrocytic markers (P = 0.2751 and P = 0.6899, respectively). In exploratory single-nucleus analyses, the six-cell-type omnibus comparison was nonsignificant (P = 0.0617), and no individual cell-type association survived false discovery rate correction. The post hoc three-cell-type composite did not establish a CTE-versus-RHI difference (95% CI, -0.532 to 0.539). Single-nucleus analyses were unadjusted for donor-level covariates; cell-type annotations were not independently validated, and donor overlap between datasets could not be excluded. The principal sensitivity analyses did not establish robust CTE-specific expression differences. These predominantly null findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: TRIM69 Suppresses the Cellular AMPK Pathway to Inhibit Viral Replication.
abstract: Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) mount an antiviral defense by targeting both viral components and cellular pathways required for infection. Here, we show that the interferon- and virus-inducible antiviral factor TRIM69 suppresses cellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling and restricts replication of both RNA and DNA viruses. Ectopic expression of TRIM69 inhibited Sendai virus (SeV)-induced autophagy and suppressed phosphorylation of AMPK and its downstream target, ULK1, in response to viral infection and nutrient deprivation. Consistent with inhibition of this proviral AMPK signaling pathway, TRIM69 expression strongly restricted replication of paramyxoviruses and pneumoviruses, including SeV, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV3), and herpesviruses, e.g., herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). Consistent with these findings, knockdown of endogenous TRIM69 enhanced viral replication, demonstrating a physiological antiviral role for TRIM69. In addition to suppressing viral replication, TRIM69 supported the expression of antiviral genes, including IFNB1, IFIT2, and IFIT3, suggesting amplification of the innate antiviral signaling. Together, these findings identify TRIM69 as a broad antiviral ISG that targets the cellular AMPK pathway and contributes to host innate immune responses against viruses.

title: The Chiral Isomers of Chlorogenic Acid Exert Distinct Antiviral Effects on Coxsackievirus A16 Infection.
abstract: Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) is one of the major pathogens responsible for hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), for which no specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Neochlorogenic acid (NCGA) and chlorogenic acid (CGA) are a pair of chiral isomers with highly similar chemical structures. While the antiviral activity of CGA has been extensively investigated, that of NCGA remains largely unexplored. In our study, we found that NCGA exhibited antiviral activity against CVA16, whereas CGA was completely inactive. Notably, NCGA also displayed extremely low cytotoxicity, and its antiviral efficacy was further confirmed in vivo. We further identified RNA-binding motif protein 24 (RBM24) as a host factor involved in the antiviral effect of NCGA against CVA16, as its knockdown attenuated the antiviral activity of NCGA. Collectively, our findings not only identify a novel natural product against CVA16 but also provide clues for the discovery of host factors involved in CVA16 infection.

title: Porcine ISG20 Restricts PEDV Replication Independent of Its Exonuclease Activity and Is Associated with Enhanced IRF3 Activation.
abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) causes severe enteric disease in swine and remains a major threat to the global pig industry. Interferon-stimulated gene 20 (ISG20) is a well-characterized antiviral effector; however, its specific role against PEDV remains poorly understood. This study investigated the antiviral function and underlying mechanism of ISG20 during PEDV infection. We observed that PEDV infection significantly induced ISG20 expression at both mRNA and protein levels in porcine intestinal epithelial cells (IPEC-J2). Functional assays demonstrated that ectopic expression of ISG20 potently suppressed PEDV proliferation, whereas shRNA-mediated knockdown facilitated viral replication. An exonuclease mutant of ISG20 (D94G) retained antiviral activity comparable to the wild-type ISG20 protein. Further investigation revealed that ISG20 overexpression was associated with increased IRF3 phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation and with elevated IFN-β mRNA abundance. These findings suggested that ISG20 may restrict PEDV by enhancing the IFN-β signaling pathway through phosphorylation of IRF3, rather than through direct viral RNA degradation, providing new insights into antiviral strategies against coronaviruses.

title: EGR1 Contributes to Pam3CSK4-Induced IL33 Transcription Through a Proximal Promoter Element in Epidermal Keratinocytes.
abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is implicated in atopic dermatitis (AD), but the transcriptional mechanisms regulating its expression in epidermal keratinocytes remain incompletely understood. Exploratory reanalysis of a previously generated RNA-seq dataset from house-dust-mite-exposed wild-type and Egr1-deficient mouse skin identified Il33 as a candidate EGR1-regulated gene. Subsequent cellular and molecular experiments were performed to investigate this potential regulatory relationship. In keratinocytes, stimulation with the TLR1/2 agonist Pam3CSK4 increased EGR1 and IL-33 expression, whereas EGR1 depletion attenuated IL33 mRNA and protein induction. Promoter deletion and mutagenesis analyses identified a proximal EGR1-responsive sequence (-146/-138 bp) contributing to IL33 promoter activity under basal and Pam3CSK4-stimulated conditions. Electrophoretic mobility shift, DNA affinity precipitation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays provided additional evidence of EGR1 association with this promoter region. Collectively, these findings support the involvement of EGR1 in Pam3CSK4-induced IL33 transcription in keratinocytes and identify a proximal EGR1-responsive element within the human IL33 promoter.

title: Isoform Switching as a Regulatory Mechanism of Glycolytic Reprogramming in Cancer.
abstract: Cancer-associated metabolic reprogramming is a dynamic process that supports tumor growth, adaptation, and therapeutic resistance. Among the post-transcriptional mechanisms contributing to this plasticity, alternative splicing has emerged as an important regulator of glycolytic metabolism by generating transcript and protein isoforms with distinct biochemical and regulatory properties. This review examines the molecular mechanisms linking alternative splicing to cancer glycolysis, with particular emphasis on pyruvate kinase M1/pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM1/PKM2) isoform regulation as the best-characterized, but context-dependent, model of splice-associated metabolic control rather than as a universal tumor-specific switch. Additional splice-dependent mechanisms affecting glycolysis-related enzymes, transporters, receptors, and regulatory proteins further illustrate that the metabolic impact of alternative splicing extends beyond PKM and may influence glucose uptake, glycolytic enzyme activity, pyruvate fate, and lactate metabolism. The review further highlights the regulatory roles of key RNA-binding proteins and splicing factors, together with upstream oncogenic signaling pathways, in establishing cancer-associated splicing programs. Hypoxia, glucose and energy stress, lactate-dependent protein lactylation, and oxidative stress can modify spliceosomal activity and splicing-factor function, whereas extracellular acidosis is better regarded as a potential modulatory input whose independent role in splice-site selection remains less firmly established. Functionally, splicing-driven glycolytic remodeling contributes to tumor growth, metabolic adaptation, invasion, metastasis, cancer stemness, and therapy resistance. Therapeutically, the splicing-glycolysis axis may be exploited through modulation of the splicing machinery, antisense oligonucleotide-mediated splice switching, isoform-directed strategies, and combined or synthetic-lethal approaches targeting splice-induced metabolic dependencies. Future studies integrating isoform-resolved transcriptomics with proteomics, metabolomics, spatial and single-cell approaches, and metabolic flux analysis will be essential for distinguishing functionally relevant splice variants from non-functional transcript diversity and for identifying clinically actionable metabolic vulnerabilities.

title: TTC7A: A Novel Host Restriction Factor That Negatively Regulates Porcine Deltacoronavirus Infection and Is Associated with the Viral Spike C-Terminal Domain.
abstract: Porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV) is an important enteric pathogen of piglets, yet the host factors that restrict its infection remain poorly understood. Tetratricopeptide repeat domain 7A (TTC7A) is a scaffold protein involved in intestinal epithelial function and membrane-associated cellular processes, but its role in PDCoV infection is unknown. Here, we investigated the role of TTC7A and its association with the PDCoV spike protein through tissue expression analysis, gain- and loss-of-function experiments, co-immunoprecipitation, structure-guided prediction, and site-directed mutagenesis. TTC7A was expressed at approximately 4-5-fold higher levels in porcine intestinal tissues, the principal sites of PDCoV infection, than in muscle. Functional analyses showed that TTC7A overexpression (approximately 3-fold higher protein levels) suppressed PDCoV infection, whereas RNA interference-mediated knockdown enhanced infection by approximately 30% relative to the control, demonstrating that endogenous TTC7A restricts PDCoV infection. Co-immunoprecipitation assays further revealed an association between TTC7A and the C-terminal domain of the PDCoV spike protein. Structure-guided analysis identified candidate residues at the interaction interface, and site-directed mutagenesis of these residues impaired the TTC7A-spike interaction (a decrease of approximately 46%), supporting their contribution to this association. Together, these findings identify TTC7A as a host restriction factor for PDCoV and characterize its interaction with the viral spike protein. This study expands our understanding of host-mediated restriction of PDCoV and provides a basis for determining how TTC7A-spike association contributes to its antiviral activity.

title: MiR-277 Drives Sexually Dimorphic Development in Ericerus pela Through Differential Regulation of Dlg1 and Lar.
abstract: Insects exhibit diverse developmental strategies, yet the molecular basis of sexual dimorphism in metamorphosis remains largely elusive. The white wax scale insect Ericerus pela (hereafter, WWS) displays extreme sexual dimorphism: females undergo paurometamorphosis (four stages), while males undergo hyperpaurometamorphosis (five stages). Although miR-277 is highly expressed in both sexes, its functional role in this process was unknown. Here, we demonstrate that miR-277 drives sexually dimorphic development through differential regulation of two distinct targets. Combining gain- and loss-of-function assays, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and RNA interference, we show that miR-277 suppresses Discs large 1 (Dlg1) in females, disrupting cellular signaling and causing growth retardation and morphological abnormalities. In males, miR-277 inhibits tyrosine-protein phosphatase Lar (Lar), a receptor tyrosine phosphatase linked to nervous system development; knockdown of Lar severely impairs male metamorphosis but does not affect females. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized, sex-specific miRNA regulatory switch: miR-277 concurrently modulates a cell-growth pathway in females and a neurodevelopmental pathway in males, thereby generating divergent developmental outcomes. Our study provides the mechanistic insight into miRNA-mediated sexual dimorphism in insects and advances the understanding of how post-transcriptional regulators shape metamorphic diversity.

title: Functional Characterization of Prothoracicotropic Hormone in Larval Development and Diapause of Ostrinia furnacalis.
abstract: Prothoracicotropic hormone (PTTH) is a secretory neuropeptide initiating insect metamorphosis via ecdysteroid synthesis. While the PTTH-ecdysone axis is well-established in development, its specific role in diapause regulation and the underlying mechanisms in agricultural pests like Ostrinia furnacalis are less understood. To address this, we identified O. furnacalis' PTTH gene (OfPTTH) and investigated its spatiotemporal expression and function using RNAi and 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) rescue assays. Our findings show that OfPTTH expression was lowest during diapause, significantly increasing upon its termination, and exhibiting an extended developmental periodicity during diapause. OfPTTH-silencing was associated with reduced expression of ecdysone-signaling genes, leading to broad physiological disruptions including altered ecdysone and juvenile hormone signaling, inhibited insulin/IGF signaling, suppressed lipid metabolic reprogramming (triglyceride accumulation), and decreased heat shock protein expression. These events ultimately caused larval diapause-like developmental arrest, pupation failure, and mortality. Exogenous 20E treatment promoted pupation in OfPTTH-knockdown larvae and restored the expression of several downstream ecdysone-signaling genes, suggesting that impaired 20E signaling contributes to the observed developmental abnormalities. This study supports an important role of the PTTH-20E axis in O. furnacalis development and diapause-associated regulation and provides a basis for further evaluation of OfPTTH as a potential target for RNAi-based pest management.

title: Comparison of PMA-treated DNA and RNA-based 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing for viable bacterial profiling in patients with cystic fibrosis.
abstract: 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing remains the most widely used technique in microbiome studies. However, conventional 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing cannot distinguish DNA from live versus dead bacteria, which can be important for understanding bacterial community dynamics and guiding therapy in cystic fibrosis (CF). Two commonly used strategies to target viable communities are propidium monoazide (PMA) pretreatment of DNA and RNA-based (cDNA) sequencing. However, their direct comparison in CF sputum has not been systematically evaluated. We analysed 41 sputum samples collected during clinical stability (n = 26) or exacerbation (n = 15). Paired aliquots underwent PMA-treated DNA extraction or RNA extraction followed by cDNA synthesis, and were subjected to 16S rRNA gene (V4) sequencing. We then compared the bacterial community structure, ecotype, and predicted functional profiles between the two methods. PMA-treated samples exhibited higher alpha diversity (P < .0001) and lower dominance (P = .0001) than RNA-based profiles, along with significant differences in beta diversity (R 2 = 0.04, P = .017). These differences were seen primarily in stable samples, contrary to high concordance in exacerbation samples. Seven community types were identified, dominated either by CF pathogens (Pseudomonas, Staphylococcus, Burkholderiaceae) or diverse oral commensals (Streptococcus, Neisseria, Veillonella, Prevotella). Pretreatment-associated cluster shifts occurred mainly in stable communities enriched with Prevotella and Veillonella (PMA-enriched) or Staphylococcus (RNA-enriched). Functional prediction revealed that 28.22% of Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) Orthology identifiers differed significantly between methods, particularly pathways related to membrane transport, energy metabolism, and quorum sensing. Overall, RNA-based sequencing provides 16S rRNA amplicon profiles comparable to PMA-treated DNA, especially in pathogen-dominated exacerbation samples, and may represent a practical alternative for viable microbiota assessment in CF airway studies.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress in multiple myeloma: adaptive mechanisms, therapy resistance, and emerging therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM), a hematological malignancy of antibody-producing plasma cells is one of the most common hematological malignancies alongside leukemia and lymphoma. Despite a significant number of therapeutic advances in immunotherapy, proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T Cell therapies, it remains incurable hematologic cancer, mostly due to acquired resistance during therapy. Disease relapse and therapeutic resistance continue to be major clinical challenges. High rate of immunoglobulin production in MM cells, imposes chronic endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and renders myeloma cells highly dependent on adaptive protein quality control mechanisms particularly, unfolded protein response (UPR). The three principal UPR signaling include inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE1), protein kinase RNA-like ER kinase (PERK), and activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6) coordinate cellular adaptation by restoring proteostasis, promoting cell survival, and enabling resistance to therapeutic stress. Increasing evidence indicates that dysregulation of ER stress pathways is interconnected with several other cellular stress pathways such as oxidative stress, the integrated stress response (ISR), mitochondrial dysfunction autophagy, and metabolic reprogramming, collectively supporting myeloma cell survival and disease progression. In this review we highlighted the importance of ER stress-associated pathway and emerging novel molecular targets with translational potential in MM. Relevant literature was selected based on its focus on ER stress, drug resistance and their molecular mechanisms in myeloma, were critically reviewed and interpreted. A comprehensive understanding of these mechanisms is important for the development of innovative therapeutic strategies to combat drug resistance and improve patient outcomes in MM.

title: Local PD-1/PD-L1 RNAi to complement immune checkpoint blockade: the dual-hit hypothesis in cutaneous malignancies.
abstract: Programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have substantially improved outcomes in advanced skin malignancies. However, many patients still show resistance, experience immune-related adverse events (irAEs), or have uneven antibody penetration into tumors. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) provide an alternative means of targeting the same pathway by promoting RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC)-mediated degradation of PD-1/PD-L1 transcripts rather than blocking the corresponding proteins with antibodies. We propose that intratumoral siRNA could reduce PD-1/PD-L1 expression in treated tumors and alter the local immune microenvironment, while systemic ICI could extend checkpoint blockade beyond the injected lesion. We refer to this strategy as the Dual-Hit hypothesis. This article examines its mechanistic basis and summarizes the available preclinical evidence and early clinical experience, including the first-in-human study of PH-762. It also considers the delivery, intracellular, and safety-related factors that may affect clinical development. Whether this combination can improve antitumor activity over ICI alone, alter treatment requirements, or benefit patients with ICI-refractory disease remains unknown and requires clinical testing.

title: Experimentally Defined T m-Guided Exon-Exon Junction Primer Design Enables Specific Discrimination of Transcript Variants with High Structural Overlap.
abstract: Accurate detection of individual RNA transcript variants remains challenging when closely related transcripts share extensive exonic sequences and differ primarily in exon connectivity. Analysis of curated human RefSeq transcripts identified 9,546 protein-coding genes containing at least one structurally contained transcript variant (defined as a transcript whose exons are each fully contained within those of a sibling transcript), highlighting the need for transcript-discriminating assays beyond conventional exon-targeted polymerase chain reaction (PCR). We developed a melting-temperature (T m)-guided exon-exon junction reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) strategy that independently evaluates the 5' and 3' exon-matching arms of junction-spanning primers. Systematic experiments demonstrated that amplification became undetectable when the T m of a partially matched primer segment was approximately 13 to 16 °C below the PCR annealing temperature, supporting an approximately 15 °C arm-specific threshold as a conservative empirical design guideline. T m-guided exon-exon junction primers, including those generated using the automated TransPrimer tool, enabled selective amplification of structurally contained transcript variants of HTRA1-AS1, apurinic/apyrimidinic endodeoxyribonuclease 1, and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase; reduced heteroduplex formation; and yielded single predominant quantitative PCR (qPCR) melting peaks. Most evaluated primer pairs exhibited amplification efficiencies of 90% to 110% and coefficients of determination (R 2) greater than 0.98. Together, these findings establish an experimentally supported framework for designing transcript-discriminating RT-PCR and qPCR assays, particularly when unique exonic sequences are limited or absent.

title: Imbalanced Coordination of Inflammatory and Antiviral Responses to Rhinovirus in Asthmatic Nasal Epithelial Cells.
abstract: Backgroud: Rhinovirus (RV) infection is a major trigger of asthma exacerbations, yet targeted therapies for virus-induced exacerbations remain lacking. Although impaired interferon responses have been proposed to underlie increased susceptibility to viral infections in asthma, findings remain inconsistent. Objective: We aimed to investigate the magnitude and temporal dynamics of primary human nasal epithelial inflammatory and antiviral responses to RV infection in asthma. Methods: Primary human nasal epithelial cells (hNECs) derived from asthmatic and healthy donors were infected with rhinovirus 1B (RV1B). Cytokine production, interferon responses, interferon-stimulated gene expression, and viral RNA levels were assessed at multiple time points following infection. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured using the DCFDA assay. Transcriptomic profiling was performed 6 h post-infection. Results: RV1B infection persisted for at least 48 h post-infection and induced robust inflammatory and antiviral responses in both asthmatic and healthy hNECs. Asthmatic epithelial cells exhibited enhanced IL-6 responses at 24 h post-infection, whereas IL-29/IFN-λ1 mRNA expression showed a transient pattern, declining over time despite persistent viral RNA levels. In contrast, IFN-λ (IL-29/IL-28B) protein, IL-8, IL-1β, MCP-1, and the interferon-stimulated gene OAS1 remained elevated. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enhanced immune-associated signaling together with reduced expression of genes involved in epithelial homeostasis and repair in asthmatic epithelial cells following RV infection. Conclusions: Nasal epithelial responses to RV infection in asthma are not simply impaired, but dysregulated, with preserved antiviral capacity but altered coordination between inflammatory, antiviral, and structural pathways. These findings highlight the importance of temporal coordination and pathway integration, and suggest that restoring epithelial balance may represent a targeted strategy for reducing virus-induced asthma exacerbations.

title: Extracellular Vesicles as a Delivery and Therapeutic Platform for RNA- and Protein-Based Cardiovascular Therapeutics: A Multi-Omics, Ancestry-Aware Roadmap.
abstract: RNA- and protein-based medicines are expanding cardiovascular therapeutic options, but efficient delivery to cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, vascular cells, and lesional immune cells remains difficult. Target selection also relies disproportionately on European-ancestry datasets, limiting causal resolution and portability. This narrative review evaluates extracellular vesicles (EVs) as carriers and active biological products for cardiovascular RNA and protein therapeutics. We distinguish EVs carrying a defined active ingredient, intrinsically bioactive EV preparations, and EV-inspired synthetic systems. We link delivery design to human multi-omics by integrating diverse-ancestry genome-wide association studies, fine-mapping, molecular quantitative trait loci, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell or spatial transcriptomics. Hepatic targets such as PCSK9, LPA, APOC3, ANGPTL3, AGT, and TTR provide benchmarks against which EV platforms can be assessed. The strongest rationale for EVs lies in extrahepatic programs where tissue access limits otherwise compelling myocardial, fibrotic, vascular, or regenerative targets. We propose a stage-gated roadmap connecting causal evidence and cell-state specificity to modality selection, cargo loading, targeting, endosomal escape, biodistribution, human cardiac models, manufacturing, potency, and safety. We then apply the framework to worked examples (LPA, CAMK2D, COL6A3-derived endotrophin, AGER/RAGE, and VEGFA), in which fine-mapping, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, ancestry-specific evidence, and cell-state localization jointly determine the modality and the carrier, including targets for which an EV is not the appropriate choice. Cited delivery studies are graded on a four-level evidence ladder spanning tissue association, intact-cargo delivery, cytosolic release, and pharmacodynamic activity, because most cardiovascular EV reports establish only the lower levels. The cardiovascular EV studies reviewed do not establish clinical benefit or an advantage over optimized lipid nanoparticles at matched active-cargo dose in a cardiovascular disease model. Clinical translation depends on reproducible functional delivery, a defined mechanism, consistent product quality, and meaningful benefit relative to established treatments.

title: Evidence of Natural Nervous Necrosis Virus Infection in Juvenile Greenfin Horse-Faced Filefish (Thamnaconus septentrionalis) During an Aquaculture Mortality Event.
abstract: Viral nervous necrosis (VNN), caused by nervous necrosis virus (NNV), is a devastating viral disease affecting marine fish aquaculture worldwide, particularly during larval and juvenile stages. Although NNV has a broad and expanding host range, the susceptibility of greenfin horse-faced filefish (Thamnaconus septentrionalis) has not been established. To determine whether T. septentrionalis is susceptible to NNV, we investigated an outbreak of abnormal mortality in juveniles from a marine aquaculture farm in Rizhao, Shandong Province, China. A comprehensive etiological investigation combined bacterial isolation and identification, real-time quantitative RT-PCR (RT-qPCR), tissue-distribution analysis, histopathology, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and RNA2-based phylogenetic analysis. Diseased fish exhibited characteristic VNN-like neurological signs, including spiral swimming, loss of equilibrium, anorexia, and body darkening. Several bacterial taxa, including Vibrio- and Tenacibaculum-related isolates, were recovered from diseased fish, indicating the possibility of bacterial involvement. However, the concurrent detection of abundant NNV RNA in neural tissues, together with characteristic neurological signs, compatible histopathological lesions, and NNV-like particles, provided convergent evidence supporting natural NNV infection. NNV RNA was detected in all ten diseased fish, whereas the other screened viral pathogens were not detected. Pooled brain-eye samples contained 4.62 × 108 to 1.33 × 109 NNV RNA copies/μg total RNA, and abundant NNV RNA was also detected in brain, spleen, kidney, and trunk tissues. Histological examination showed vacuolar and degenerative lesions in the brain and retina, and TEM revealed numerous non-enveloped, spherical virus-like particles approximately 25 nm in diameter in neural tissues, consistent with NNV morphology. Phylogenetic analysis of the RNA2 capsid protein gene placed the detected virus within the RGNNV RNA2 lineage. Together, the neurological signs, NNV RNA detection, compatible histopathological lesions, NNV-like particles in neural tissues, and RNA2 phylogenetic evidence provide evidence of natural NNV infection in T. septentrionalis. These findings document evidence of natural NNV infection in T. septentrionalis under aquaculture conditions, highlight the need for further investigations into pathogenicity and transmission, and provide a basis for VNN surveillance and biosecurity management in filefish aquaculture.

title: A PdhR Regulator Controls Bacterial Motility and Biofilm Formation in Vibrio alginolyticus.
abstract: Vibrio alginolyticus is a widespread opportunistic marine pathogen. Flagellum-driven motility and biofilm formation are core virulence traits that support environmental survival and host infection and are tightly controlled by diverse transcriptional regulators. Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex regulator (PdhR), a conserved GntR-family transcription factor, regulates pyruvate metabolism in Escherichia coli. However, its physiological function in V. alginolyticus remains unclear. In this study, a pdhR deletion mutant (ΔpdhR) and a complemented strain (C-ΔpdhR) were constructed to investigate the regulatory roles of PdhR. Swimming motility assays and transmission electron microscopy revealed that pdhR deletion markedly impaired motility, indicating that PdhR is required for normal motility. The ΔpdhR mutant exhibited significantly increased biofilm biomass and increased exopolysaccharide (EPS) content but lower extracellular protease activity. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis identified 1135 differentially expressed genes in ΔpdhR, including downregulated flagellar assembly genes (e.g., fliF, flhA) and upregulated genes encoding outer membrane protein A (OmpA) family proteins and glycosyltransferases. These findings suggest that PdhR is associated with motility and negatively regulates biofilm formation in V. alginolyticus. This study expands our understanding of how a metabolic GntR-type transcription factor coordinates virulence-associated physiological traits in marine opportunistic pathogens.

title: Redistribution of CD163+ CCR2+ Monocytes from Blood Circulation to the Ascites as a Potential Indicator of Progression in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: This study aimed to identify tumor-specific changes in circulating and ascites-derived monocytes from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) patients using flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, RNA sequencing, and in vitro experiments. Our results demonstrate that the tumor induces a decrease in the total number of circulating monocytes but an increase in the proportion of CD163+ monocytes. Notably, CD206-expressing monocytes were reduced in HGSOC patients, with extremely low CD206 levels in peripheral blood mirroring those in tumor tissues. In contrast, a marked accumulation of CD206-positive monocyte-derived macrophages was observed in malignant ascites. The presence of CCR2 on the monocyte surface further amplified the increase in CD163+ monocytes and reversed the decrease in CD206+ monocytes in cancer patients. Transcriptional levels of CD163 corresponded to protein levels and were elevated in monocytes of HGSOC patients. Moreover, the percentage of CD163+CCR2+ monocytes was decreased in peripheral blood but increased in ascites of patients with progressive disease. A functional migration assay confirmed extensive recruitment of monocytes toward malignant ascites in vitro. Collectively, our findings suggest that the redistribution of CD163+CCR2+ monocytes from blood to malignant ascites may represent a candidate indicator of disease progression in HGSOC patients.

title: Multi-Omics Profiles Reveal Molecular Regulation of Ovarian Aging in Chickens.
abstract: Ovarian aging shortens the laying cycle in hens, thereby reducing egg production and posing a major constraint on the economic efficiency and sustainability of the poultry industry. This study integrates three omics approaches to investigate the molecular alterations underlying age-related ovarian functional decline. We employed an integrated approach combining RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), and data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, with selected targets validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. Ovarian tissues with follicles > 8 mm removed were collected from a total of 12 hens, including six 30-week-old hens (W30, n = 6) and six 90-week-old hens (W90, n = 6), to identify age-associated changes in gene expression, ribosome footprints (RFs), and protein abundance. A total of 18,836 genes, 17,007 RFs, and 6738 proteins were detected. Among these, 562 genes, 430 genes with altered translation efficiency (TE), and 252 proteins were differentially expressed between the two groups. Further analyses indicated that, in aged ovaries, the down-regulation of steroidogenic genes, including STAR, CYP11A1, HSD3B1, and FDX1, was associated with reduced steroid hormone synthesis. The up-regulation of matrix stiffness-related proteins, including MFAP4 and SGCE, together with the down-regulation of genes and proteins associated with matrix degradation and autophagic clearance, including ADAMTS15, MRC1, RAB7A, and CTSB, was indicative of ovarian tissue sclerosis. In summary, the multi-omics data revealed that ovarian aging in laying hens is associated with coordinated alterations across multiple molecular layers. This study identifies key genes and proteins associated with ovarian aging and provides a foundation for generating mechanistic hypotheses regarding the molecular processes involved.

title: Integrative Small RNA and Degradome Sequencing Reveals Salt-Responsive microRNA-Target Interactions in Soybean Roots.
abstract: Soybean (Glycine max) is a leading source of plant protein and vegetable oil. However, soil salinization adversely affects its planting area and yield. The salt-responsive microRNA (miRNA) layer is uncharacterized, particularly in roots, where stress originates. We generated 24 small RNA and two degradome libraries from roots of a salt-tolerant (QH34) and salt-sensitive (DN50) cultivar sampled before and 2, 4, and 8 h after NaCl treatment. These findings were integrated with published transcriptome data from the same cultivars and time points. In total, 117 high-confidence miRNA loci (90 conserved; 27 candidate novel) were annotated, of which 56 mature miRNAs (45 conserved; 11 novel) were differentially expressed in at least one within-cultivar contrast. Degradome sequencing identified 441 degradome-supported miRNA-target pairs (84 miRNAs; 422 target genes). Conserved miRNAs were mostly down-regulated, whereas novel miRNAs varied more significantly and were predominantly up-regulated in QH34. Salt also altered miRNA processing: 149 significant isomiR switches occurred across 24 loci, and shifted variants were predicted to recognize transcripts that canonical forms did not. The loci encoding gma-miR319p and gma-miR160e also showed haplotype associations with salt tolerance across 172 accessions. Overexpression of Glyma.08G301200, a degradome-supported gma-miR2109 target in a network module associated with gma-miR160e, increased root elongation and survival under 150 mM NaCl. These results link natural variation at miRNA loci to a salt-responsive regulatory network, and identify Glyma.08G301200 as a candidate for improving soybean salt tolerance. More broadly, the combination of cleavage-supported targets, haplotype-associated loci, and a validated target gene offers starting points for improving salt tolerance in this crop, pending validation in independent populations.

title: Form and Function in Flux: Molecular Ensembles from Structure to Therapy.
abstract: Molecular structure, revealed by crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, imaging, and prediction, remains foundational to biology and drug design, yet function also depends on how structures flex, adapt, and interact. Proteins and RNA populate alternative conformations and binding states, while chromatin, membranes, glycans, metabolites, water, ions, and biominerals vary in composition and organization. This narrative review treats form and function as interdependent properties of molecular ensembles: structure constrains which states are accessible, whereas regulatory inputs, partners, and cellular environments determine which states are occupied, exchanged, and used. Without assuming a shared physical mechanism, we compare these systems and propose a cross-class evidence map that links each claimed state variable to its regulatory input, matched measurement, causal test, and organismal or clinical outcome. Examples from cancer, neurodegeneration, infection, and metabolic disease show how specific states become dysregulated, and why restored binding, assembly, or imaging readouts need not indicate functional recovery. Therapies are compared by primary mode of action-direct state modulation, target-abundance reduction, or genetic and RNA-level correction-with clinical successes, failures, and safety limits reported separately. The synthesis identifies where measurement methods must advance to resolve interrelated ensembles in native contexts and to determine when targeting them yields meaningful patient benefit.

title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Bromodomain Gene Family in Olive (Olea europaea) and Its Association with Salt Stress Responses.
abstract: Bromodomain (BRD) proteins are evolutionarily conserved epigenetic readers that bind acetylated lysine residues on histone tails, linking chromatin remodeling to transcriptional regulation and abiotic stress adaptation. Although salinity is among the most economically damaging abiotic stresses worldwide, the bromodomain-level epigenetic mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in the perennial crop olive (Olea europaea L.) remain unstudied. This study aimed to identify and characterize the complete Olea europaea bromodomain (OeBRD) gene family in olive, resolve its evolutionary relationships with Arabidopsis thaliana, and identify candidate genes potentially associated with salt-stress responses. Genome-wide identification, physicochemical characterization, promoter cis-regulatory element analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, orthogroup clustering, conserved-motif and gene-structure analysis, AlphaFold3 structural modeling, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data (BioProject PRJNA841838) from control, primed (75 → 150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants, and Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING)-based protein-protein interaction (PPI) and Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analyses were performed. Twenty-one non-redundant OeBRD genes were identified in the O. europaea genome (GCF_002742605.1), with molecular weights of 43,076-242,620 Da, isoelectric points of 5.05-9.67, and universally negative grand average of hydropathicity (GRAVY) values. Phylogenetic analysis resolved four clades, including olive-specific paralog groups, and orthogroup clustering against A. thaliana identified 16 orthogroups, eight of which are strict 1:1 orthologs, five show copy-number differences between the two species (more copies in olive in three groups, including OeBRD6a/6b/6c, and more copies in Arabidopsis in two), one is a balanced 2:2 group and two contain only Arabidopsis genes. Multiple Em for Motif Elicitation (MEME) analysis identified 10 conserved motifs. Promoter analysis revealed abundant abscisic acid (ABA)-, myeloblastosis (MYB)/myelocytomatosis (MYC)- and jasmonate-responsive cis-elements. DESeq2 differential expression analysis of primed (75→150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants relative to untreated controls identified four of the 21 OeBRD genes as significantly differentially expressed (adjusted p < 0.05): OeBRD6b, OeBRD6c, OeBRD10 and OeBRD26 were up-regulated in primed roots, OeBRD26 was also up-regulated in non-primed roots and non-primed leaves, and no gene was significant in primed leaves; STRING PPI analysis identified OeBRD24 and OeBRD13 as the most connected nodes in a network inferred from Arabidopsis orthologues, with chromatin, chromatin remodeling and histone acetyltransferase activity among the most significantly enriched GO terms. Ten proteins-OeBRD26, OeBRD6c, OeBRD6b, OeBRD10, OeBRD13, OeBRD24, OeBRD11, OeBRD16, OeBRD28 and OeBRD29-were prioritized as candidates for future experimental validation of a possible role in salt-stress responses in olive.

title: AP2V-2 Is Required for Tachyzoite Proliferation in Toxoplasma gondii.
abstract: Toxoplasma gondii undergoes multiple developmental transitions during its complex life cycle, which are controlled by coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic regulation. The MORC/HDAC3/ApiAP2 complex has been implicated in the repression of merozoite- and sexual-stage genes in tachyzoites. AP2V-2 (TGGT1_285895) was previously identified as a component associated with this regulatory network, but its biological function remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized AP2V-2 using conditional protein depletion combined with phenotypic, transcriptomic, and genome-wide occupancy analyses. AP2V-2 localized to the parasite nucleus and was detected throughout the tachyzoite cell cycle. Conditional depletion of AP2V-2 markedly impaired plaque formation and intracellular replication but had little effect on parasite invasion. The replication defect was reversible after removal of indole-3-acetic acid. RNA sequencing identified 211 differentially expressed genes after AP2V-2 depletion. Of these, 79.6% overlapped with genes dysregulated after MORC depletion, with particularly strong overlap among upregulated genes. In contrast, CUT&Tag identified only 45 AP2V-2-associated peaks, most of which were located in intergenic regions. Although a subset of enteroepithelial-stage genes was upregulated after AP2V-2 depletion, AP2V-2 did not occupy their promoter regions, typical merozoite markers were not induced, and no endopolygeny-like division was observed. These findings indicate that AP2V-2 is required for normal tachyzoite replication but differs functionally from the ApiAP2 factors that directly control merozoite developmental programs.

title: From Vesicle Cargo to Cargo Selection in Obesity-Associated Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS).
abstract: In polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), extracellular vesicle (EV) microRNA (miRNA) profiles differ from those of comparison groups, but those groups vary across studies. Lean healthy women, women with obesity and no PCOS and lean women with PCOS do not answer the same question, and lean healthy controls confound the syndrome with adiposity. Most work treats these miRNAs as biomarkers and leaves the prior question open: how an miRNA is selected for export. Selection is not passive. Sumoylated hnRNPA2B1 recognises GGAG motifs, YBX1 sorts miR-223 and other small non-coding RNAs, SYNCRIP binds an extra-seed motif and sorting sequences differ by cell type. Obesity alters the inputs to that step: adipose tissue is a major source of circulating exosomal miRNAs, its vesicles alter insulin sensitivity at a distance and gastric bypass changes their content. In the ovary, body mass index associates with EV-linked miRNAs in follicular fluid, and PCOS follicular exosomes carry miRNAs acting on granulosa cell apoptosis, senescence and glycolysis. Those effects are the readout of a loading step that, to our knowledge, has not been quantified in adipose tissue, serum, or follicular fluid of women with obesity-associated PCOS. Future work should measure hnRNPA2B1, YBX1 and SYNCRIP alongside EV miRNA profiles, with comparison groups that separate adiposity from diagnosis. Paired bariatric surgery samples offer one suitable design.

title: Discordant Protein- and Transcript-Level Expression of TRAF7 and the EDA2R-Apoptotic Axis in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by dysregulated apoptotic and inflammatory signaling, yet the tissue-level behavior of several candidate regulators remains poorly defined. Materials and Methods: We quantified ectodysplasin A2 receptor (EDA2R), TNF-receptor-associated factor 7 (TRAF7) and the apoptotic fragments cleaved-PARP1 and cleaved-CASP3 by immunofluorescence in 49 ccRCC and 27 matched non-tumoral cortex samples and analyzed the corresponding transcripts in TCGA-KIRC and GTEx. Results: TRAF7 protein was higher in tumor than in control tissue (median 0.81% vs. 0.63% positive area, p = 0.015), an increase concentrated in grade 2-3 tumors, whereas EDA2R and the apoptotic fragments did not differ (all p > 0.59). The positive EDA2R-cleaved-PARP1 correlation in low-grade tumors (ρ = +0.54, p = 0.002) was attenuated in high-grade tumors (ρ = +0.06, p = 0.84). In TCGA-KIRC, EDA2R mRNA was overexpressed in tumors, and higher expression was associated with better overall survival (HR = 0.60, p = 0.0011), including after mutual adjustment for the four transcripts (HR = 0.66, p = 5.3 × 10-5) and after adjustment for age, sex, stage and grade (HR per standard deviation = 0.83, p = 0.008). TRAF7 mRNA did not differ between tumor and normal tissue, but higher levels were associated with worse overall survival after the same adjustment (HR = 1.38, p < 0.001). Conclusions: TRAF7 and EDA2R show opposite, marker-specific discordance between protein- and transcript-level data across cohorts, consistent with, but not demonstrating, regulation beyond transcription. EDA2R is a candidate transcript-level prognostic marker requiring validation, and TRAF7 is a protein-level feature of ccRCC; paired RNA-protein and functional studies are needed.

title: Peripheral Blood Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Divergent Average Daily Gain in Liaoyu White Cattle.
abstract: Average daily gain (ADG) is an economically important trait in beef cattle, yet the systemic transcriptional characteristics underlying divergent growth rates remain insufficiently characterized in Liaoyu White cattle. This study aimed to identify peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures associated with divergent ADG. Twelve Liaoyu White cattle maintained under comparable feeding and management conditions were selected after a 6-month observation period, including six fast-growing and six slow-growing animals according to ADG. Peripheral blood RNA was subjected to RNA sequencing, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using DESeq2, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. The fast-growing group exhibited significantly higher ADG than the slow-growing group, while initial and final body weights did not differ significantly. A total of 1633 DEGs were identified using the criteria of |log2FC| ≥ 1 and padj < 0.05, including 1524 upregulated and 109 downregulated genes in fast-growing cattle. Several DEGs previously associated with growth-related traits in cattle were identified, including SPP1, NCAPG, and LCORL in the fast-growing group. GO analysis indicated enrichment in intracellular transport, secretion, protein localization, and related molecular functions, whereas KEGG analysis highlighted the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, cell cycle, ribosome biogenesis, cellular senescence, and immune-related pathways. These findings indicate that divergent ADG in Liaoyu White cattle is associated with distinct peripheral blood transcriptional profiles involving growth-related signaling, cellular proliferation, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and systemic metabolic and immune processes.

title: The Importance of Multi-Omics Studies for Stress Tolerance and Plant Growth in Sustainable Agriculture.
abstract: One of the most important transformative strategies for better understanding of plant resilient against abiotic and biotic stresses are the integration of omics approaches, encompassing genomics, metabolomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and phenomics. Genomics explores genome structure, evolution, and function, and advances in next-generation genome annotation and sequencing have enabled the accurate and complete decoding of different plant genomes. Epigenetics involves heritable gene expression alterations without DNA sequence changes, mainly through histone modification, and DNA methylation. Among the main epigenetic mechanisms, DNA methylation is particularly important in plants and is maintained throughout mitosis. Transcriptomics is a study of all RNA molecules transcribed in a cell or organism, providing useful information about dynamic patterns of gene expression. Recent advances in sequencing technology have enabled more evolutionary and accurate transcriptomic analysis. Metabolomics is a powerful approach because metabolites and their concentrations Metabolomics is known to provide a direct functional readout of the physiological state of an organism. It can deal with qualitative and quantitative assessment of metabolites, which are necessary intermediates and end products of metabolism. Metabolomics uses targeted approaches such as quantitative and hypothesis-driven as well as non-targeted approaches to characterize plant metabolites. This article aims to study the importance of multi-omics studies for crop abiotic and biotic stress tolerance while considering plant growth in sustainable agriculture. To provide a comprehensive understanding of the metabolic, epigenetic, and genetic bases of main agronomic traits in crops, considering the integration of multi-omics data is necessary. The integration of different technologies can induce better optimized farming activities, sustainable agriculture, and crop improvement.

title: Development of a Calreticulin-Based Endogenous Control for Use in Culex restuans RT-qPCR Assays in Massachusetts.
abstract: Hematophagous arthropods and associated pathogens are becoming more prevalent globally. With limited treatment options, prevention is the top priority to reduce disease. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) has emerged as a standard detection method for many laboratories, but it has several drawbacks. Degraded sample quality, failed RNA preparations, and the presence of reaction inhibitors can lead to false negative results, introducing the need for a positive control. Existing control methods rely on adding exogenous nucleotides during amplification reactions, which may not reflect the quality of the sample. Incorporating assays to detect endogenous mosquito mRNA transcripts provides assurance that sample quality is sufficient for the downstream amplification of pathogen RNA. In the present study, we applied the Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (RACE) technique to obtain a full-length calreticulin cDNA sequence from the Culex restuans mosquito, collected in Massachusetts, USA. We then used the newly discovered cDNA sequence to design primers and probes spanning the first exon-exon junction of the calreticulin gene, which allowed for specific and accurate RNA transcript detection in an RT-qPCR assay. This assay detected the presence of calreticulin transcripts in extracted pools of mosquito RNA. This approach may be further developed to include other relevant mosquito species and, with extensive validation, may have potential for use as an endogenous control in arbovirus surveillance.

title: Aspirin Eugenol Ester Alleviates Fatty Liver Hemorrhagic Syndrome in Laying Hens by Modulating AMPK/mTOR-Mediated Autophagy.
abstract: Fatty liver hemorrhagic syndrome (FLHS) is a nutritional-metabolic disorder of laying hens with pathological features analogous to human non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Aspirin eugenol ester (AEE) has lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities; however, its protective effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms against FLHS remain unclear. In this study, we established an in vivo FLHS model in laying hens using a high-energy low-protein diet and an in vitro steatosis model induced by free fatty acids in LMH cells, to explore the hepatoprotective function of AEE. AEE alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation and histopathological lesions, and decreased lipid levels in serum and liver tissue. AEE downregulated the expression of key lipogenic enzymes and upregulated the expression of genes responsible for fatty acid β-oxidation. RNA-seq analysis indicated that the AMPK signaling pathway and autophagy were tightly linked to the hepatoprotective effects of AEE. Treatment with the autophagy activator rapamycin recapitulated the protective effects of AEE, whereas the autophagy inhibitor chloroquine abrogated these beneficial effects. Furthermore, the AMPK inhibitor dorsomorphin partially reversed AEE-mediated liver protection, while the AMPK activator AICAR reproduced the protective effects of AEE. These results indicate that AEE alleviates FLHS in laying hens at least partly through modulation of fatty acid metabolism, likely associated with AMPK/mTOR-mediated autophagy. This work provides mechanistic insights for AEE as a candidate agent for preventing diet-triggered hepatic steatosis.

title: Identification and Molecular Characterization of a TYLCV Novel Isolate Associated with Disease in Tomato Cultivars Carrying Bred Resistance.
abstract: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is a devastating viral pathogen threatening agricultural crops globally. In this study, we identified a novel TYLCV isolate (TYLCV-YN6244), which was associated with disease outbreaks in resistant tomato cultivars in Yuanmou County in Yunnan Province, China. We determined the complete genome of TYLCV-YN6244 and found it encoded six viral proteins characteristic of Geminivirus. We identified its V2 protein as a potent viral suppressor of RNA silencing (VSR), and generated an infectious clone of wildtype TYLCV-YN6244, or V2-defective TYLCV-YN6244 (TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2) in which V2 was deleted. Both infectious clones were capable of systemically infecting tobacco and tomato. However, TYLCV-YN6244 but not TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2 could cause disease symptoms in wildtype tobacco or tomato plants, and viral accumulation was drastically reduced in plants infected with TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2 compared to TYLCV-YN6244 while the efficiency of virus-derived small interfering RNAs (vsiRNAs) biogenesis was conversely increased in plants infected with TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2. Surprisingly, small RNA profiling indicated that the 21nt and 22nt rather than 24nt vsiRNAs were predominantly produced in tomato plants infected with either TYLCV-YN6244 or TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2. It is likely that 21nt and 22nt vsiRNAs play a significant role in plant resistance to DNA viruses. Furthermore, transcriptome analyses revealed that TYLCV-YN6244 or TYLCV-YN6244-ΔV2 infection differentially modulated metabolism and defense-related pathways in tomato, probably underlying distinct viral pathogenicity and disease symptoms induced in plants. Overall, our research not only identified a novel pathogenic TYLCV isolate but also characterized molecular biology and host response in tomato with infectious clones developed in this study, with implications for untangling virus-host interaction for developing novel resistance in crop tomato.

title: Poikiloderma with Neutropenia, Clericuzio Type (OMIM #604173): From USB1 RNA Biology to a Candidate Model of Compartmentalized Cyclic Nucleotide Signaling.
abstract: Poikiloderma with neutropenia, Clericuzio type (PN; OMIM #604173), is a rare autosomal recessive genodermatosis caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in U6 snRNA Biogenesis 1 (USB1), with approximately 100 molecularly confirmed cases. Beyond the defining post-inflammatory poikiloderma and non-cyclic neutropenia, affected individuals show recurrent sinopulmonary infection, impaired wound healing, tendon contractures, and primary gonadal failure in males. USB1 is a 2H-superfamily 3' to 5' exoribonuclease that removes oligoadenylate tails added by Poly(A) polymerase associated protein 5 (PAPD5) and PAPD7; its loss destabilizes guide-strand microRNAs and blocks the emergence of CD45+ hematopoietic progenitors. Splicing is not measurably disturbed in patient cells, so the earlier splicing-centered account requires revision. Drawing on previously unpublished endocrine, neurologic and imaging data from two affected brothers, we develop a candidate model in which the microRNA lesion reaches cyclic nucleotide signaling by two routes: de-repression of phosphodiesterase E3B (PDE3B) after loss of miR-142-5p, and loss of a perinuclear and Golgi cyclic AMP compartment after coordinate reduction in A-kinase anchoring protein 6 (AKAP6) and PDE4D interacting protein (PDE4DIP). We state where the model is supported, where it conflicts with published effects, and what would refute it, arguing for compartment-restricted dysregulation rather than global deficiency. PAPD5/7 inhibition, leading to repression of PDE3B, is closest to the causal lesion, but its on-target neurotoxicity makes it an experimental tool rather than a candidate drug.

title: Eriodictyol Modulates Cell-Type-Specific Stress Response Pathways In Vitro and Improves Visible Signs of Skin Aging.
abstract: Skin aging involves progressive disruption of redox balance, proteostasis, inflammation, and extracellular matrix integrity. Flavonoids have attracted interest for their ability to regulate cellular stress responses relevant to these processes. This study investigated the natural flavonoid eriodictyol (EDL) in human skin cells and evaluated whether topical application improved visible skin quality. Primary human keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts were treated with EDL and profiled by RNA-sequencing to characterize cell-type-specific transcriptional responses. Functional validation assessed oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and senescence-associated markers, while a seven-flavonoid structure-function comparison contextualized EDL activity. Topical effects were assessed in a randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled cosmetic study (N = 60) using an EDL-containing formulation for 12 weeks. EDL induced distinct transcriptional changes in keratinocytes and fibroblasts, with enrichment of unfolded protein response pathways in both cell types. Keratinocytes showed increased expression of antioxidant and autophagy-related genes, whereas fibroblasts showed changes in gene expression pathways related to proliferation, metabolism, and senescence signaling. Functional assays further showed that EDL reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity. In a 12-week topical evaluation, EDL significantly improved overall skin quality across multiple parameters of visible aging compared with the vehicle. These findings demonstrate that EDL modulates stress-response pathways in human skin cells and improves visible skin quality following topical application.

title: MCOLN1/TRPML1 regulates lysosomal acidification through Ca2+-CAMK2/CaMKII-DMXL1-mediated V-ATPase assembly in cellular and mouse models of Alzheimer disease.
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline and amyloid beta (Aβ) pathology, with emerging evidence indicating that autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction acts as an early pathogenic event. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes remain incompletely understood. This study demonstrated that MCOLN1/TRPML1 (mucolipin TRP cation channel 1), a lysosomal Ca2+ channel, was consistently downregulated in the hippocampus of patients with AD, five familial Alzheimer disease mutations (5xFAD) mice, and neuroblastoma Neuro-2a cells stably expressing human APP695 (N2a-APP) cells. Knockdown of Mcoln1 specifically in the hippocampus of mice recapitulated key AD-related phenotypes, including impaired lysosomal acidification, defective autophagic degradation, lysosomal enlargement, Aβ accumulation, dendritic spine loss, and cognitive deficits. Conversely, pharmacological activation with Mucolipin synthetic agonist 1 (ML-SA1) or genetic overexpression of MCOLN1 alleviated these abnormalities and mitigated Aβ pathology and cognitive impairments in 5xFAD mice. Mechanistically, decreased MCOLN1 protein impaired the vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) assembly, potentially via diminished DMXL1 (Dmx like 1) phosphorylation through the Ca2+-CAMK2/CaMKII (calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase II) signaling pathway. Additionally, ATF2 (activating transcription factor 2) was identified as a transcriptional activator of MCOLN1, with its downregulation contributing to reduced MCOLN1 expression in AD. These findings collectively position MCOLN1 as a potential regulator of lysosomal function in AD, suggesting that restoring MCOLN1 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.Abbreviations: 5xFAD: five familial Alzheimer disease mutations; title: GTRD 2026: expanded content and resources for deep learning.
abstract: Gene Transcription Regulation Database (GTRD; https://gtrd.biouml.org/) contains uniformly annotated and processed NGS data related to transcription regulation: ChIP-seq, ChIP-exo, DNase-seq, MNase-seq, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq. The latest release significantly extends the number of available experiments. All new ChIP-seq data for human transcription factors (TFs) obtained by the Codebook Consortium were processed and annotated; GTRD now covers 85% of all known human TFs. We added new types of information related to transcription regulation: enhancer regions revealed from analysis of CAGE-seq data and single-cell ATAC-seq data. To facilitate the use of GTRD for building deep learning models, we provide direct access to the MySQL database where metadata are stored and have built profiles with single-nucleotide resolution for ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data.

title: CTHRC1 as a Novel Regulatory Target of Type I Collagen Synthesis via ATF4 in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a fatal interstitial lung disease characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix, primarily type I collagen. This study investigates the role of Collagen triple helix repeat containing 1 (CTHRC1) in pulmonary fibrosis. Analysis of public databases and validation in mouse models revealed that CTHRC1 expression is significantly upregulated and strongly correlates with type I collagen. Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence supported a close association between CTHRC1 and myofibroblasts in fibrotic lungs. In vitro, CTHRC1 knockdown in NIH3T3 fibroblasts attenuated TGF-β1-induced type I collagen production. Mechanistically, CTHRC1 silencing reduced phosphorylation of the TGF-β receptor I and its downstream effectors Smad2/3, accompanied by reduced protein expression of the transcription factor ATF4 and its target, the collagen synthesis enzyme PSAT1. These findings support a CTHRC1-TGF-β/Smad-ATF4/PSAT1 signaling model for type I collagen regulation, providing a basis for further investigation of CTHRC1 and the associated pathway as potential therapeutic targets in IPF.

title: Mouse Schlafen Family Proteins Control MHV68 Replication in Fibroblasts.
abstract: Schlafen proteins are interferon-responsive regulators of cellular and antiviral pathways that can profoundly influence viral replication and host defense. Diverse viral infections are known to induce expression of Schlafen family members in human cells, while infection studies in mice have been primarily limited to mSlfn2, a group I Schlafen protein without a clear ortholog in humans. RNA-seq analysis of three distinct infection models reveals that mouse Schlafens are induced in response to murine gammaherpesvirus 68 (MHV68) in fibroblasts, B cells, and primary peritoneal macrophages. Notably, mSlfn8 expression is induced under multistep low-MOI infection conditions, whereas infections initiated with higher viral inoculum fail to induce mSlfn8. To assess whether mSlfn8 or related Slfns impact MHV68 replication, we performed siRNA-mediated knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of mSlfn2, mSlfn8, and mSlfn9 in NIH 3T3 cells. Two independent clonal mSlfn2 and mSlfn8 knockout cell lines supported higher viral titer, indicating that these mSlfns are restriction factors for MHV68 replication in murine fibroblasts. Collectively, these results demonstrate that mSlfn2 and mSlfn8 function as antiviral effectors during MHV68 infection and support a model in which MHV68 counteracts interferon-induced mouse Schlafen expression to promote efficient replication.

title: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase 14 Improves Antioxidant Defense and Drought Stress Tolerance in Maize.
abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) play important roles in plant stress signaling, but the contribution of MAPK group D in maize drought tolerance remains unclear. Here, we investigated MAPK group D ZmMAPK14 through phylogenetic and structural analyses, kinase activity assays, transgenic functional characterization, physiological measurements, biochemical analyses and RNA sequencing. ZmMAPK14 was classified as a group D MAPK containing the threonine-aspartate-tyrosine (TDY) motif, and drought stress significantly induced an increase in its kinase activity. ZmMAPK14-overexpressing lines exhibited higher survival rates, greater leaf relative water content, reduced detached-leaf water loss, lower membrane injury and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities. In contrast, ZmMAPK14-knockdown lines showed the opposite phenotypes. Transcriptome analysis identified 2005 drought-responsive genes in ZmMAPK14-overexpressing and knockdown lines. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of the "response to oxidative stress" term (GO:0006979) among drought-responsive genes in ZmMAPK14-overexpressing lines. This term comprised 313 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 13 antioxidant enzyme-encoding genes with diverse expression patterns. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that ZmMAPK14 positively regulates drought tolerance in maize by improving water status and strengthening antioxidant defense, providing a basis for further investigation of its underlying regulatory mechanisms.

title: Coenzyme Q10 Modulates Stress Responses to Simulated Galactic Cosmic Radiation in Human Retinal Organoids.
abstract: Long-duration space travel is anticipated to be associated with vision changes. The retina is responsible for relaying visual cues to the brain. Retinal neurons are especially vulnerable to changes in the space environment due to their susceptibility to increases in oxidative stress and inflammation. There are knowledge gaps on the changes that occur when human retinal neurons are exposed to space stressors, specifically galactic cosmic radiation (GCR). GCR is highly relevant to long-duration missions. To ameliorate the effects of GCR, we utilized Coenzyme Q10, which has been demonstrated to be useful in neurodegeneration. We developed retinal organoids and exposed them to 0.5 Gy of simulated GCR at Brookhaven National Laboratory. At 48 h and eight days post irradiation, RNA, protein, and conditioned media were collected to investigate changes to the retinal organoids. Through this exploratory study, we identified differential expression of a retinal ganglion cell marker and inflammatory signaling in the Coenzyme Q10-treated organoids after GCR. Further, we found single nucleotide polymorphism differences between our donors.

title: EZH2 Knockdown Reshapes Protein-Coding and Long Non-Coding Transcriptional Programs in Primary Human Airway Basal Cells.
abstract: Background: Airway basal cells (BCs) maintain epithelial homeostasis and contribute to epithelial regeneration after injury. How enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), a key epigenetic regulator, controls the transcriptional programs, especially the coding and non-coding transcriptional consequences underlying human airway basal cell states, remains poorly understood. Methods: Here, we performed rRNA-depleted total RNA sequencing of donor-matched control and shEZH2 primary human airway basal cells from four independent donors and integrated coding and non-coding transcriptomic analyses with basal-cell state inference and multi-criteria candidate prioritization. Results: EZH2 depletion broadly remodeled the BCs transcriptome.
