GSEA showed prominent negative enrichment of nucleosome organization, chromosome segregation, DNA replication, and cell-cycle programs, accompanied by positive enrichment of extracellular matrix- and signaling-related processes. Reference-guided analysis further revealed a marked reduction in the transcriptional similarity to the Cycling Basal reference state, accompanied by increased similarity to Basal and Suprabasal reference states, indicating a shift in the basal-cell transcriptional landscape away from a Cycling Basal-like program. In parallel, differentially expressed lncRNAs were associated with distinct transcriptional programs, while multi-criteria integration prioritized eight consensus lncRNA-PCG relationships for further investigation. Conclusions: These findings define coordinated coding and non-coding transcriptional remodeling following EZH2 knockdown in primary human airway basal cells and nominate candidate lncRNA-PCG regulatory relationships that may contribute to human airway basal-cell state regulation, providing a framework for understanding epigenetic regulation of basal-cell states and its potential relevance to airway epithelial remodeling in respiratory disease.

title: CD36 in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Membrane Trafficking, Redox Injury, and Therapeutic Targeting.
abstract: Cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36) links lipid handling to ligand-induced signaling in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), but its contribution to injury varies with cell type and metabolic conditions. This narrative review evaluates the evidence connecting CD36 to redox injury by comparing experimental interventions, functional measurements, and rescue studies. In podocytes, RNA turnover and palmitoylation regulate receptor availability. Tubular studies link CD36 manipulation to oxidative metabolism, mitochondrial oxidant signaling, and inflammatory amplification of lipid peroxidation. Alternative uptake routes, discordant localization findings, and lipid accumulation without a full fibrotic phenotype argue against a uniformly harmful role for CD36. We propose a model in which receptor availability affects ligand handling and signaling, while intracellular lipid processing and peroxide defense shape susceptibility to injury. Evaluation of receptor-directed interventions should account for the cell and protein-substrate selectivity of trafficking regulators. Human studies identify candidate CD36 measurements for evaluation in defined diagnostic, prognostic and treatment-response settings. Combining cell-specific receptor perturbation and appropriate reconstitution controls with substrate tracing and defined redox measurements provides a framework for testing renal protection after diabetic injury has developed.

title: MicroRNA spatial profiling for assessing drug efficacy in BRCA1-related triple-negative breast tumors
abstract: BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancers exhibit homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and are initially sensitive to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, but 40-70% of patients develop resistance, creating a need for predictive biomarkers that capture treatment-associated spatial heterogeneity. Using the K14-Cre Brca1f/fTrp53f/f model with tumors that acquired PARP inhibitor resistance, we evaluated PARP inhibitor combinations with either PI3K inhibition or Poly(I:C) in vivo. To determine how treatment altered tumor spatial microRNA (miRNA) profiles, we applied our hydrogel-based, nanoliter well array in situ miRNA assay to quantify and spatially profile miRNAs on FFPE sections from tumors treated for 10 days and developed spatial miRNA analysis frameworks integrating latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) and principal component analysis (PCA). We also incorporated immune architecture using Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) maps to assess local structural similarity of immune infiltration and miRNA topics. Both combinations improved antitumor activity compared to PARP inhibition alone in olaparib-sensitive tumors. The resulting spatial miRNA topics stratified early tumors according to established PARP inhibitor sensitivity or resistance and distinguished their treatment regimens, while SSIM analysis revealed local structural similarity of immune infiltration and miRNA topics. This integrative spatial miRNA assay and analysis identified a let-7a-dominant topic associated with PARP inhibitor resistance, indicating that spatial miRNA profiling may inform therapeutic stratification in BRCA1/2-related breast cancers.

title: Genomic GLO1 Deletion from Human Prostate Cancer Cells Suppresses EMT Gene Expression and Bone Metastasis in a Bioluminescent SCID Mouse Model.
abstract: Glyoxalase 1 (encoded by GLO1) is a glutathione-dependent enzyme detoxifying the glycolytic byproduct methylglyoxal (MG), an oncometabolite involved in metabolic reprogramming and tumorigenesis. Prior research has identified GLO1 overexpression as a critical molecular hallmark of prostate cancer progression, and high GLO1 protein levels strongly correlate with advanced histological tumor grade, pathological stage, and early biochemical recurrence. Here, after confirming GLO1 overexpression by TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq transcriptomic analysis of human tumor samples, we have performed CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genetic deletion of GLO1 from bioluminescent DU145-Luc2 metastatic prostate cancer cells to investigate transcriptomic and phenotypic impact in vitro and in vivo. NanoString nCounter™ ('PanCancer Progression' panel) comparative gene expression profiling (GLO1_KO versus GLO1_WT) revealed a significant downregulation of genes and pathways related to epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cancer progression as a consequence of GLO1 deletion; concordantly, phenotypical screening indicated a pronounced attenuation of matrigel invasiveness observable in GLO1_KO cells. Likewise, inhibition of GLO1 using a pharmacological inhibitor attenuated the invasive capacity of DU145-GLO1_WT cells, an effect recapitulated across additional prostate carcinoma cell lines (PC-3, LNCaP). In a bioluminescent SCID mouse bone metastasis model, intracardial injection of DU145-Luc2 isogenic lines [GLO1_KO versus GLO1 WT] led to extensive mandibular bone metastasis of GLO1_WT cells, contrasted by the complete absence of metastasis in response to GLO1 genetic deletion. In summary, our preclinical data are consistent with a molecular role of GLO1 in prostate cancer cell invasiveness and metastasis, warranting further experimental evaluation.

title: Bisphenol a is associated with ovarian cancer chemoresistance via ecmCAF-mediated stromal remodeling: an integrative multi-omics study.
abstract: BPA is a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor linked to ovarian cancer, yet its effect on chemotherapy efficacy is unknown. CAFs drive drug resistance via microenvironment remodeling. We investigated whether BPA exposure is associated with chemoresistance via CAF-mediated stromal reprogramming. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on ovarian cancer samples across treatment-naive, post-chemotherapy, and recurrent states (n = 10). BPA target gene set activity was quantified across cell types using AUCell scoring. Fibroblasts were re-clustered to characterize CAF subtypes. BPA target genes were integrated from public databases, with core targets prioritized through protein-protein interaction networks and molecular docking. Machine learning models were built for chemoresistance prediction, and in vitro validation was performed; CellChat inferred intercellular communication dynamics. Fibroblasts exhibited the highest BPA-driven activity among all tumor cells. The extracellular matrix CAF (ecmCAF) subtype showed elevated BPA scores. Integration of BPA targets, ecmCAF markers, and recurrence signatures yielded hub genes, with molecular docking predicting favorable BPA binding to PTGS2 (-7.7), MMP2 (-7.6), and SERPINE1 (-7.5 kcal/mol). CellChat revealed heightened CAF-to-epithelial pro-EMT and CAF-to-immune suppressive signaling in the recurrent sample. In vitro validation further showed that BPA treatment increased ACTA2 and COL1A1 expression in CAFs and that conditioned medium from BPA-treated CAFs enhanced SKOV3 resistance to cisplatin. The BPA-ecmCAF axis represents a novel mechanism linking environmental exposure to ovarian cancer chemoresistance through microenvironment remodeling. These findings identify ecmCAF effectors as candidate exposure biomarkers and suggest that environmental risk assessment should consider the potential of BPA to compromise cancer treatment outcomes.

title: m6A Methylation and Transcriptomic Responses in the Bovine Mammary Gland Following Intramammary Escherichia coli Challenge.
abstract: Escherichia coli is an important cause of bovine mastitis and induces inflammatory responses in the mammary gland. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is an important post-transcriptional RNA modification involved in gene regulation, but its association with the bovine mammary response to E. coli remains unclear. In this study, a within-cow mammary-quarter design was used in four clinically healthy Holstein cows, with quarters assigned to saline control, 12 h E. coli exposure, and 24 h E. coli exposure groups. MeRIP-seq and RNA-seq were integrated to characterize m6A enrichment and gene expression, with cow identity accounted for in the differential analyses. Compared with the saline control, 2242 and 1848 differential m6A peaks were identified in the 12 h and 24 h exposure groups, respectively. RNA-seq identified 591 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the 12 h exposure group and 1287 DEGs in the 24 h exposure group. Integrated analysis identified 264 and 476 differentially m6A peak-gene associations in the 12 h and 24 h exposure groups, respectively. Functional enrichment analysis showed that differential m6A peak-gene associations were mainly involved in immune and inflammatory processes, including NF-κB, NOD-like receptor, IL-17, and TNF signaling pathways. The patterns of m6A enrichment and gene expression differed between the exposure groups, although these differences cannot be attributed to exposure duration alone because of the staggered inoculation design. These findings indicate that changes in m6A enrichment are associated with gene expression during the bovine mammary response to E. coli challenge and provide candidate genes for further investigation of m6A-related regulation in bovine mastitis.

title: Surveillance for Peste Des Petits Ruminants Virus in Free-Ranging Wildlife of Russia Using an In-House ELISA Assay.
abstract: Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) is a highly contagious disease caused by the PPR virus (PPRV), a Morbillivirus, that affects small domestic ruminants and a range of wild ruminants. The disease is associated with significant socioeconomic losses and poses conservation threats due to its impact on susceptible wild ungulates. Wild species do not typically serve as independent reservoirs of PPRV. However, spillover from infected livestock at the wildlife-livestock interface is well documented. Therefore, understanding the role of wildlife in PPR epidemiology is important for the global campaign to eradicate the disease. This is the first large-scale surveillance of wild ruminants conducted across the Russian Federation, which included many species that were not previously tested for PPRV. In total, 1709 samples were collected from 19 wild species over 7 years (2018-2024) across 54 regions. All samples were examined using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and virus neutralization test (VNT). For the serological component of the study, an indirect ELISA was developed, based on recombinant nucleocapsid protein expressed in Escherichia coli, and was validated. The ELISA was validated against commercial competition ELISA and VNT. Results showed that the ELISA exhibited high performance with serum from multiple species, with a sensitivity of 97.5% and a specificity of 98% compared with the commercial kit, and with a sensitivity of 96.5% and a specificity of 99% versus VNT. All 1709 wildlife samples tested negative for PPRV antibodies and RNA, indicating no evidence of viral circulation in the surveyed populations. Although PPRV has been detected in goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa), saiga (Saiga tatarica), and wild goat (Capra aegagrus) in neighboring countries, none of the Russian specimens-collected from several species, including Caspian red deer (Cervus elaphus maral) and Siberian musk deer (Moschus moschiferus)-tested positive. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported widescale PPR surveillance in wildlife species of its kind. This first comprehensive nationwide surveillance of PPRV in wild ruminants across Russia found no infection in the species or samples tested. The newly developed ELISA offers a rapid and reliable cost-effective alternative to VNT for large-scale screening. Our findings indicate that wild ruminants do not currently serve as a PPR reservoir in the surveyed regions and support the inclusion of wildlife monitoring in PPR control strategies for a better understanding of PPR epidemiology in wildlife.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Identifies Valproic Acid as a Candidate for Hemophilia A.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Hemophilia A (HA) is caused by coagulation factor VIII (FVIII) deficiency, but its clinical heterogeneity suggests that biological alterations beyond impaired hemostasis may contribute to disease expression. This study aimed to characterize F8 knockout (F8-KO)-associated molecular changes and identify drug repositioning candidates with therapeutic potential for HA. Methods: An F8-KO human umbilical vein endothelial cell model was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 and profiled by RNA sequencing and data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics. Integrated multi-omics, enrichment, and protein-protein interaction analyses informed drug repositioning using Connectivity Map (CMap), EpiMed, and DrugBank. Valproic acid (VPA) was evaluated using cell viability assays, RT-qPCR, transcriptomic profiling, and H3K27ac CUT&Tag. Results: Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis identified 113 shared genes with predominantly concordant changes, and network-based analysis prioritized genes involved in endothelial homeostasis and inflammatory regulation. Drug repositioning identified VPA and irbesartan across three screening sources. VPA increased CD274 mRNA expression, partially reversed F8-KO-associated transcriptional alterations, and remodeled H3K27ac-associated regulatory programs involving vascular homeostasis- and inflammation-related pathways. Conclusions: VPA may modulate F8 deficiency-associated endothelial molecular alterations and represents a drug-repositioning candidate for HA. These findings may offer a new perspective for exploring potential therapeutic strategies beyond conventional correction of the coagulation defect.

title: Beyond Structural Classification: A 4S+G Functional Framework for Non-Coding RNA Biology in Cancer and Its Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) regulate gene expression at multiple levels in cancer, yet their functional plasticity and the slow pace of clinical translation remain incompletely explained. This review is organized around a unifying theme: ncRNAs act as integrative nodes connecting the epigenetic, transcriptional, signaling, and metabolic regulatory layers. Building on the established signal, sponge, scaffold, and guide archetypes of long non-coding RNA function, we extend this schema into a 4S+G model that adds a splice-regulatory archetype and embeds all five modes in a three-axis taxonomy spanning structural topology, subcellular localization, and molecular mode of operation, thereby capturing context-dependent functions that binary structural categories cannot accommodate. We dissect chromatin remodeling dynamics, evaluate the competing endogenous RNA hypothesis against stoichiometric evidence, and trace metabolic-epigenetic feedback circuits that stabilize malignant states. We then critically appraise the clinical record of ncRNA therapeutics, from the termination of MRX34 to the modest efficacy of subsequent candidates, and analyze the delivery, immunogenicity, and biomarker barriers that distinguish oncology from other indications for RNA drugs. Emerging solutions, including ligand-directed extrahepatic delivery, spatial transcriptomics, and deep learning-based target prediction, are assessed against these bottlenecks. The 4S+G framework links mechanistic understanding to a realistic roadmap for developing ncRNA-targeted cancer therapeutics with favorable risk-benefit profiles.

title: Molecular and Cellular Characterization of Core Genes Associated with Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress in Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: Background: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) contributes to myocardial injury following reperfusion and adversely affects clinical outcomes. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS), as a crucial cellular stress response mechanism, plays a central regulatory role in the development of MIRI. Currently, the molecular pathways and cellular phenotypic characteristics of ERS-related core genes regulating MIRI remain incompletely elucidated. Targeted research in this area could provide a solid theoretical foundation for developing novel myocardial protection strategies. Methods: In the present study, two microarray gene expression datasets (GSE100499 and GSE108940) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Simultaneously, ERS-related genes were collected from the GeneCards and Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) databases. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using the limma package, and key module genes were selected through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). An intersection analysis was performed among DEGs, genes from the selected WGCNA module, and ERS-related genes. Three machine learning algorithms [least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)] were employed to identify core ERS genes; functional association analysis was performed to explore potential relationships among the core genes. Concurrently, single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis was performed to investigate the functional mechanisms of core genes at the single-cell level. Furthermore, the pathological roles of these core genes in MIRI were validated by constructing rat MIRI models and H9c2 cell hypoxia-reoxygenation models, where 4-phenylbutyrate was used to inhibit ERS. Results: ERS-related DEGs were predominantly enriched in tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway, lipid metabolism and atherosclerosis, and leukocyte transendothelial migration pathways, which are all critical pathological pathways in the progression of MIRI. Four ERS-related genes (Bcl2, Thbs1, Cebpb and Calr) performed best in Lasso, RF and SVM analyses. All four genes showed significant interactions with pathways associated with MIRI and ERS, including ERS activation, inflammatory response, cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammatory cell migration. In the single-cell transcriptome of MIRI cardiac tissue, among the 12 cell types, the aforementioned four genes were primarily upregulated in cardiomyocytes, vascular endothelial cells and cardiac macrophages. Notably, cardiomyocytes and cardiac macrophages exhibited a pronounced pro-inflammatory state and the highest levels of pyroptosis. This suggests that they may be the primary effectors of the four key genes mediating MIRI-related injury. Conclusions: Collectively, Bcl2, Thbs1, Cebpb, and Calr may serve as potential ERS-associated biomarkers and therapeutic targets for MIRI, providing novel insights into ERS-mediated molecular mechanisms underlying myocardial injury.

title: Chlorogenic Acid Improves Porcine Oocyte Maturation and Post-Warming Survival Accompanied by Mitochondrial and Antioxidant Changes.
abstract: Porcine oocytes are susceptible to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction during in vitro maturation (IVM), which compromises their maturation quality, cryotolerance, and subsequent developmental competence. Therefore, improving the efficiency of IVM and cryopreservation is of great significance for the conservation of livestock genetic resources. In human medicine, oocyte IVM and vitrification can promote the development of assisted reproductive technology. In this study, we supplemented the maturation medium with various concentrations (0, 20, 30, 40, and 50 μM) of chlorogenic acid (CGA) to evaluate its effects on the porcine oocyte maturation rate. Transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) of pooled oocytes based on Smart-seq2 was performed to elucidate the key molecular pathways associated with CGA during porcine oocyte IVM. Compared with the control group, treatment with 30 μM CGA significantly improved the maturation rate (control group 64.83% ± 1.51% vs. 30 μM CGA treat group 77.86% ± 2.00%, p < 0.05). However, the Cumulus Expansion Index was not significantly altered by any of the CGA treatments (p > 0.05). RNA-seq identified 167 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between the two groups. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis revealed that these DEGs were predominantly enriched in ribosome, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), and thermogenesis. Gene Ontology functional enrichment showed that the upregulated genes were mainly associated with translation, ribosome, mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I assembly, and other related terms. Protein-protein interaction network analysis indicated that the DEGs were primarily enriched for genes involved in the composition of cytosolic ribosomal subunits (RPS27A, RPL13A, RPL26, RPL9, and RPS13). Real-time quantitative PCR validation of four randomly selected DEGs yielded expression trends consistent with the RNA-seq data. Furthermore, compared with the control group, supplementation of the IVM medium with 30 μM CGA significantly increased intracellular glutathione (GSH) levels (p < 0.05), mitochondrial membrane potential (p < 0.05), and MitoTracker fluorescence intensity in fresh oocytes (p < 0.01). In vitrified-warmed oocytes, 30 μM CGA treatment similarly elevated GSH levels (p < 0.01) and did not significantly alter ROS levels (p > 0.05), while significantly improving the short-term post-warming survival rate (control group 60.79% ± 3.92% vs. 30 μM CGA treat group 82.15% ± 5.22%, p < 0.05). However, in freshly matured oocytes, CGA did not significantly affect intracellular ROS levels, early apoptosis, or the subsequent developmental competence of embryos derived from in vitro fertilization (p > 0.05). Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 30 μM CGA improves oocyte maturation efficiency, increases intracellular GSH levels, and enhances mitochondrial status in porcine oocytes, and short-term post-warming survival of vitrified porcine oocytes. These beneficial effects are associated with changes in the expression of genes related to ribosome and OXPHOS pathways. This study provides a reference basis for optimizing the IVM and warrants future investigation into vitrification preservation for porcine oocytes.

title: Exploring candidate molecular links between aspartame and pulmonary arterial hypertension through network toxicology and transcriptomics.
abstract: To identify candidate molecular overlaps between aspartame target profiles and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH)-associated transcriptomic signatures. We integrated network toxicology, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), and 12 machine learning algorithms to prioritize candidate genes. Molecular docking, single-cell RNA sequencing, and virtual CAPN1 knockout analysis explored predicted interactions, cellular expression patterns, and network perturbations. We identified 21 overlapping genes enriched in renin-angiotensin and calcium-related processes. Machine learning prioritized CAPN1, ERAP2, ITK, PTGS1, and KDR. The five-gene panel achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.972 in lung tissue and 0.660 in external blood samples. Docking scores ranged from -8.0 to -5.7 kcal/mol. PAH samples showed lower hematopoietic-cell proportions and reduced CAPN1 expression within this population. Virtual CAPN1 knockout identified VNN2 and MLX as candidate network effectors. These analyses prioritize candidate genes for investigating molecular links between aspartame-related target profiles and PAH. The absence of exposure records, metabolite measurements, and experimental validation limits the findings to hypothesis generation.

title: Knockdown of STAT1 inhibits epithelial-mesenchymal transition and attenuates the migration of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells.
abstract: To investigate the expression pattern and functional role of signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), focusing on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cellular motility. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of 4 NPC and 3 non-cancerous nasopharyngeal tissues identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. STAT1 in situ expression was verified by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in paired clinical specimens. Stable STAT1-knockdown models were established in human 6-10B NPC cells using lentiviral shRNAs, with silencing efficiency confirmed via Western blotting. Protein levels of core EMT markers (N-cadherin, Snail, Vimentin, β-catenin, α-SMA, and E-cadherin) were evaluated, and two-dimensional cellular motility was assessed using real-time scratch wound healing assays (0-96 h). Transcriptomic profiling revealed 6,394 DEGs significantly enriched in cell adhesion and junction remodeling pathways. IHC confirmed prominent cytoplasmic and nuclear STAT1 overexpression in NPC tissues. Western blotting verified potent STAT1 knockdown (sh1: ~52.0% of NC, P< 0.05). STAT1 silencing significantly downregulated mesenchymal markers-including N-cadherin (P< 0.001), Snail (P< 0.0001), Vimentin (P< 0.01), β-catenin (P< 0.001), and α-SMA (P< 0.001)-without altering epithelial E-cadherin levels (P > 0.05). Consistently, STAT1 depletion markedly decelerated wound closure rates across 24 to 96 h compared to Mock controls (P< 0.05 or P< 0.01). STAT1 is aberrantly overexpressed in NPC. Targeting STAT1 attenuates mesenchymal phenotypic traits, EMT-associated molecular programs, and cell motility, identifying STAT1 as a candidate molecular vulnerability that warrants further preclinical evaluation.

title: Metabolic and Transcriptional Profiles of A549 Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells Following Prolonged IFNγ Exposure.
abstract: Interferon-gamma (IFNγ) plays an important role in antitumor immunity; however, persistent IFNγ signaling can subject tumor cells to persistent inflammatory stress, fostering adaptive cellular responses. Here, we investigated the transcriptional and metabolic features associated with prolonged IFNγ exposure in lung adenocarcinoma cells. A549 cells were continuously treated with IFNγ (10 ng/mL) for 23 days, with a control culture passaged in parallel. RNA sequencing and untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics were performed. Differential expression analysis, pathway enrichment, metabolite-gene correlation analysis, and two-way orthogonal partial least squares (O2PLS) modeling were used for exploratory multi-omics integration. Selected transcripts and proteins were examined by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting. Cell migration was assessed after IFNγ withdrawal and a separate experiment examined responses to 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI). Compared with the passage-matched control, the IFNγ-exposed cells exhibited altered redox and lipid metabolite profiles, along with activation of interferon-responsive transcripts and upregulation of stress-inducible HSP70-family genes. On day 23, total and phosphorylated STAT1 levels were higher in IFNγ-treated cells, while the ratio of phosphorylated STAT1 to total STAT1 was reduced. IRG1 and HSPA8 expression also increased at day 23, although a functional relationship between them was not established. Previously exposed cells showed greater migration after IFNγ withdrawal. In separate 4-OI treatment experiments, HSPA1A and HSPA6 protein levels were elevated, together with increased cell migration. Prolonged IFNγ exposure was associated with metabolic and transcriptional differences in A549 cells, including changes in interferon-responsive and HSP70-family genes. These exploratory findings identify candidate responses to prolonged inflammatory stimulation that require validation in independently established chronic cultures and functional studies.

title: Microbiota-Modulating Antibiotic Therapy in ICUs: Results of a Retrospective Data and Prospective Pilot Study in Patients with Intra-Abdominal Infections.
abstract: Background. Severe intra-abdominal infections and sepsis are among the leading causes of mortality in critically ill patients. Standard treatment relies solely on parenteral administration of bactericidal antibiotics. A promising alternative approach involves preserving host-microbiota homeostasis by adding modulation therapy to prescribed antibiotics. Agents inhibiting bacterial protein or RNA synthesis may affect microbial metabolic activity in addition to their antimicrobial effects. Objective. To evaluate whether microbiota modulation can improve treatment outcomes in critically ill patients with intra-abdominal infections. Methods. This study was conducted in two stages: a retrospective comparative study (n = 585), and a prospective observational cohort study with concurrent control. The study assessed the clinical course, duration of intensive care unit (ICU) stays, and treatment outcomes of patients with severe intra-abdominal infections treated with different antibiotic strategies. Results. In the retrospective analysis, hospital mortality was significantly lower in the Modulation Group (20.6% vs. 30.5%, absolute risk reduction 9.9% [95% CI: 2.8-16.9%], p < 0.01). In the prospective stage, after propensity score adjustment for baseline clinical severity, modulation therapy yielded an adjusted odds ratio for hospital mortality of 0.2219 (95% CI: 0.0399-1.2345, p = 0.0855; unadjusted: 17.2% vs. 44.4%). Competing risk analysis demonstrated that modulation therapy did not significantly alter the overall time to live ICU discharge (SHR = 0.7985, 95% CI: 0.3393-1.8792, p = 0.6063). Conclusions: A modulating regimen of antibiotic therapy may potentially be associated with lower hospital mortality in patients with severe intra-abdominal infections and requires confirmation in larger randomized controlled trials.

title: Systemic Genetic Susceptibility and Lung Tissue Remodeling in Autoimmune-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
abstract: Background: Systemic autoimmune disease-associated interstitial lung disease (SAID-ILD) involves systemic immune susceptibility superimposed on complex pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis. Methods: A multi-layer framework integrating two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) of 91 circulating inflammatory proteins and 1400 serum metabolites with lung-focused bulk transcriptomics, explanted-lung single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and bronchoalveolar-lavage single-cell RNA sequencing was used to connect systemic susceptibility signals with cell-resolved lung biology. Results: MR prioritized multiple inflammatory signals, including risk-increasing estimates for CD244 and CX3CL1; neither met the 91-protein BH threshold, and power at OR = 1.5 was below 25% for both. Bulk transcriptomic meta-analysis identified a reproducible disease context dominated by epithelial injury, myeloid activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Cell-resolved integration localized CD244 predominantly to T cells/natural killer cells and CX3CL1 to endothelial, epithelial, and stromal compartments, supporting evaluation of CD48-CD244 and CX3CL1-CX3CR1 as candidate communication axes. The CX3CL1-CX3CR1 recruitment program was increased in disease myeloid cells (Hedges g = 1.27, q = 3.86 × 10-4), whereas CD48-CD244 showed receiver-program compatibility, with CD48 ranking first among the two tested ligands in 20 of 21 NicheNet scenarios. Communication effects varied across pulmonary compartments, and neither focal axis represented the strongest disease-associated route; SPP1-CD44 showed the largest fixed-effect global shift, although its nine-pair evidence was not significant in the random-effects sensitivity analysis. Conclusions: These results distinguish systemic genetic susceptibility from local communication magnitude and identify CD48-CD244 and CX3CL1-CX3CR1 as biologically distinct, compartment-dependent hypotheses linking immune-cell state and recruitment to the fibrotic lung environment in SAID-ILD.

title: The molecular phenotypes of null alleles in cells (MorPhiC) data resource.
abstract: The MorPhiC Data Portal is the public resource for the Molecular Phenotypes of Null Alleles in Cells (MorPhiC) Consortium, which maps molecular and cellular consequences of targeted human gene inactivation. The portal integrates raw, processed and uniformly analyzed datasets from functional genomics and phenotyping assays, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, Perturb-seq, SLAM-seq, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and metabolomics. Release 4 (August 2026) expands the resource to perturbations of >300 genes in human induced pluripotent stem cells and derivative systems, including embryoid bodies, organoids, and differentiated models, using complementary perturbation strategies targeting DNA, RNA, and protein products. A central advance is gene-centered navigation: gene pages consolidate experimental context, perturbation strategies, cell models, datasets, phenotyping evidence, and standardized analyses, while interactive visualizations expose differential expression, enrichment, and assay-specific results. Dataset pages provide metadata, protocols, analysis summaries, and links to public repositories for raw and processed files; the portal also catalogs consortium-generated knockout cell lines. By integrating MorPhiC datasets with external annotations on essentiality, Mendelian disease associations and mammalian phenotypes, and by standardizing metadata, analysis outputs and archive submission workflows, the portal provides a reusable resource for studying human gene loss-of-function at scale. The resource is available at https://morphic.bio/data.

title: Age-related changes in the phenotype and function of mouse skin macrophages and their modulation by the secretome of peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
abstract: Skin ageing is accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation ("inflammaging") and progressive remodeling of the dermal extracellular matrix, yet the cellular events that initiate these processes early in life remain incompletely understood. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of dorsal skin from young (8-week-old), middle-aged (26-week-old), and aged (52-week-old) male C57BL/6 mice to map age-related shifts in cellular composition, with particular emphasis on macrophages. Although the relative proportions of most cell types remained broadly stable, the macrophage compartment expanded markedly in the oldest skin. Sub-clustering resolved four macrophage populations, three of which expanded or emerged with age. The Mac4 population, marked by S100a8 and S100a9 and a Cd14-high monocyte-derived signature, was detected mainly in aged skin and was confirmed in situ by F4/80, S100a8, and S100a9 co-staining. Cell-cell communication analysis predicted increased macrophage-to-fibroblast signaling in aged skin, including the pro-fibrotic mediators Thbs1 and Spp1, together with upregulation of collagen and fibrosis-associated genes in a subset of fibroblasts (FB3/FB4). Notably, collagen transcripts increased, whereas COL5A3 protein decreased, and dermal collagen architecture appeared disorganized by second-harmonic-generation imaging, suggesting post-transcriptional control of matrix remodeling. Ex vivo treatment of aged skin with the secretome of γ-irradiated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC-sec) shifted the macrophage compartment toward a younger-like composition and downregulated fibrosis-associated fibroblast genes. Overall, these findings identify the early emergence of monocyte-derived, pro-inflammatory, and potentially pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets as a feature of mouse skin ageing and suggest that PBMC-sec can partially counteract these changes.

title: A Pre-post Rehabilitation Study of Exosomal mRNA and lncRNA Expression Profiles Reveals Potential Role of UBE2G1 in Rehabilitation of Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and messenger RNAs (mRNAs) are implicated in the development and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aims to examine the potential of any lncRNA as biomarkers underlying PD rehabilitation. Pre-post rehabilitation study of lncRNA and mRNA expression profiles may identify the potential biomarkers associated with rehabilitation. We enrolled 6 patients with PD (PWP) and 6 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) in this study. Peripheral blood samples were collected before and after 14-day rehabilitation treatment to extract total RNA from exosomes. Differentially expressed mRNAs (DEmRNAs) and differentially expressed lncRNAs (DElncRNAs) were identified by next-generation sequencing (NGS). A co-expression network was built. Overall, pre-post rehabilitation study of exosomal mRNA revealed 1,662 DEmRNAs (606 upregulated and 1,056 downregulated) in PWPs. Compared with the HCs, 1,723 DElncRNAs (1,278 upregulated and 445 downregulated lncRNAs) and 1,931 DElncRNAs (1,561 upregulated and 370 downregulated) were identified in the blood exosomes of pre-rehab and post-rehab PWPs, respectively. GO and KEEG enrichment analyses revealed significant enrichment of proteasome-mediated ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process, and ubiquitin mediated proteolysis pathways, suggesting their potential role in the progression of PD. Co-expression network analysis identified one DElncRNA (ENST00000421331) and one positively related DEmRNA (ENSG00000132388, UBE2G1). RT-qPCR validated that ENST00000421331 and ENSG00000132388 were significantly downregulated in the pre-rehab PWPs compared with the HCs (P < 0.05), but significantly upregulated in the post-rehab PWPs compared with the pre-rehab PWPs (P < 0.01). This is the first report about the role of UBE2G1 in rehabilitation of PD patients. The preliminary findings suggest that UBE2G1 is implicated in PD rehabilitation. Correlation analyses between changes in UBE2G1/lncRNA expression and clinical outcomes, mechanistic study, and longitudinal validation are required to further confirm the role of UBE2G1 as a biomarker in PD rehabilitation.

title: Methods for Studying Circular RNAs in Viral Oncogenesis.
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are single-stranded, covalently closed RNA molecules expressed across diverse organisms, including humans and viruses. Emerging evidence indicates that circRNAs are critical modulators of the interplay between viral persistence, immune evasion, and oncogenesis. Viral- and host-derived circRNAs can rewire cellular signaling pathways through diverse mechanisms including microRNA sponging, protein scaffolding, and, in some cases, acting as templates for translation. As a result, circRNAs have emerged as potential therapeutic targets and disease biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis of various malignancies. Nevertheless, the study of these molecules presents various intrinsic technical challenges due to their lack of a poly(A) tail, low abundance, and high sequence similarity with their linear RNA counterparts. Moreover, circRNA research is a rapidly evolving field that lacks standardized methodologies, contributing to variability in detection, validation, and reproducibility across studies. This review provides a landscape of methodologies used to study viral and host circRNAs, especially in the context of viral oncogenesis. We compare techniques ranging from the computational identification and quantification of circRNAs in transcriptome datasets to their experimental validation and functional characterization. Showcasing current technological advances leading to biological insights, this article aims to offer a guide for investigating the roles of circRNAs in viral oncogenesis for better therapeutic opportunities.

title: Identification of Senescence-Associated RNA Editing as a Potential Biomarker for Senescence and Aging.
abstract: RNA editing is a post-transcriptional process that alters RNA nucleotide sequences, potentially affecting protein coding and RNA function. In this study, we identified 2132 senescence-associated RNA editing sites, defined as editing events present in highly senescent WI-38 fibroblasts at population doubling level (PDL) 50 but absent at earlier passages (PDL 20 or 25), by analyzing time-course bulk RNA-seq data from replicative senescence. Approximately 92% of these sites were located within Alu elements, predominantly in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs), suggesting widespread post-transcriptional regulatory remodeling during senescence. Numerous senescence-associated editing events exhibited elevated editing levels in tissues from older individuals in the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project. Among these events, F11 receptor (F11R) mRNA editing was observed across multiple tissues and exhibited higher editing levels in older individuals, showing a more consistent association with aging than F11R gene expression in human tissues. These findings reveal transcriptome-wide RNA editing patterns associated with cellular senescence and suggest that RNA editing may provide a complementary layer of molecular information for studying aging and senescence-related molecular changes.

title: An Integrative Analysis of Transcriptome and Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Identifies Key Calmodulin-Related Genes in Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disorder lacking disease-modifying therapies, highlighting an urgent need to identify pivotal molecular drivers. Given the crucial role of calcium signaling in chondrocyte biology, this study aimed to systemically identify and characterize key calmodulin-related genes (CaRGs) in OA pathogenesis. Methods: Transcriptomic data from OA and control synovial tissues (dataset GSE55235) were analyzed to screen for OA-associated CaRGs. Candidate genes were screened using three machine learning algorithms in GSE55235, followed by ROC and expression analyses in GSE55235 and GSE12021 to identify the final key genes. Their functions were explored through enrichment analyses, immune infiltration assessment, and drug prediction. Additionally, the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE216651 was further analyzed to delineate expression patterns, cell-cell communication, differentiation trajectories, and functional states of key cell types. The expression levels of biomarkers were verified by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in OA and tibial plateau fracture surgical controls. Results: MKNK2 and RYR2 were identified as key genes. MKNK2 was downregulated and linked to suppressed immune pathways, while RYR2 was upregulated and associated with activated immune/lysosomal activity. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant correlations between these genes and specific immune cells, including neutrophils and type 2 T helper cells. Drug prediction prioritized XMD-12 for MKNK2 and metoprolol for exploratory docking against an RYR2 calmodulin-binding peptide model. Moreover, single-cell analysis localized their high expression to myeloid cells, which in OA exhibited disrupted communication with T/B cells and a skewed early differentiation trajectory. Functional profiling revealed OA myeloid cells were enriched in pathways like Hedgehog signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In addition, RT-qPCR analysis showed that the expression of RYR2 was significantly upregulated, while the expression of MKNK2 showed the opposite trend in OA, which was consistent with the prediction results of the database. Conclusions: This study identified MKNK2 and RYR2 as crucial CaRGs in OA. Their distinct expression patterns and strong association with dysregulated myeloid cell function suggest that they may be involved in OA progression through modulation of calcium signaling and immune-stromal crosstalk; however, these mechanistic inferences are derived from computational analyses and require experimental validation. These findings offer potential new diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Porcine IFI35 as a Restriction Factor Against H1N1 Swine Influenza Virus and the Antagonism of IFI35 by Viral NS1.
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) poses a persistent threat to the swine industry and public health, and host restriction factors in pigs remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated whether porcine interferon-induced protein 35 (IFI35) restricts H1N1 swine influenza virus (SIV) replication and how the viral NS1 protein counteracts this defense. Porcine IFI35 was overexpressed in PK-15, HEK293T, and MDCK cells followed by H1N1 SIV infection; cytopathic effects, viral NP levels, and viral titers were assessed. RNA-seq and qPCR were used to profile and validate host transcriptional responses. The effect of NS1 on RIG-I-like receptor (RLR) signaling was examined by Western blotting. IFI35 overexpression attenuated SIV-induced cytopathic effects and reduced viral NP levels and titers. Transcriptomics revealed that IFI35 reshaped the host transcriptome, enriching antiviral, RLR, and NOD-like receptor pathways, and upregulated IFNB1, IFNE, MDA5, and interferon-stimulated genes; SIV infection counteracted these changes and downregulated endogenous IFI35, an effect associated with the viral NS1 protein. NS1 reduced MDA5, RIG-I, and MAVS protein levels. Porcine IFI35 restricts H1N1 SIV and is antagonized by NS1 through combined transcriptional suppression and RLR pathway blockade, revealing an IFN-ε-associated defense axis and candidate antiviral targets in the swine host.

title: Copper-Sensitive Metabolic Stress in IL-1β-Induced Dysfunction of Tendon Progenitor Cells: An In Vitro and Transcriptomic Study.
abstract: Tendinopathy is a complex disorder involving inflammation, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix damage, and changes in cellular metabolism. Cuproptosis is a type of regulated cell death that depends on copper and is associated with mitochondrial protein lipoylation and proteotoxic stress. This study investigated whether IL-1β-induced dysfunction of tendon progenitor cells (TPCs) is accompanied by changes in cuproptosis-associated genes and whether pharmacological modulation of copper availability alters this phenotype. Rat TPCs were stimulated with IL-1β, exposed to copper chloride (CuCl2) and the copper ionophore elesclomol (ES), and cotreated with the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate (TTM). Cellular metabolic activity, gene expression, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were assessed. Bulk RNA-sequencing data from IL-1β-treated rat TPCs (GSE253913) and single-cell RNA-sequencing data from cultured human tendon-derived progenitor cells (GSE150482) were analyzed. In rats, transcriptomic analysis showed mainly an inflammatory response to IL-1β, with only slight changes in genes associated with copper and mitochondrial functions. IL-1β decreased TPC metabolic activity and the expression of tenogenic markers such as Scx, Col1a1, and Col3a1, while it increased inflammatory and catabolic markers, ROS production, and the expression of Dld and Lipt1. TTM attenuated these effects, restoring metabolic activity and some tenogenic markers, and reducing ROS, Dld, and Lipt1 levels. Exposure to ES + Cu triggered a TTM-sensitive phenotype characterized by reduced metabolic activity, decreased expression of tenogenic genes, increased ROS levels, and altered expression of cuproptosis-related genes. The human single-cell dataset analysis also revealed condition-dependent changes in mitochondrial lipoylation genes, including DLAT and DLST. Overall, these findings suggest that inflammatory TPC dysfunction is linked to copper-sensitive mitochondrial stress and gene changes related to cuproptosis pathways.

title: Hakai links m6A RNA methylation to immune regulation in colorectal cancer.
abstract: To define the functional role of Hakai within the m6A writer complex in colorectal cancer (CRC) and to determine how its modulation influences RNA methylation dynamics and tumour-immune interactions. Hakai was knockdown in CRC cell models, followed by RNA sequencing to assess transcriptomic changes and MeRIP-seq to evaluate m6A methylation patterns. Protein expression and immune-related markers were validated using Western blot, flow cytometry, ELISA, and RT-qPCR. Protein-protein interactions were analysed by co-immunoprecipitation, and subcellular localisation was assessed by cell fractionation. Functional immune assays were performed by exposing peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy donors and lamina propria mononuclear cells from CRC patients to conditioned media from Hakai-knockdown cells. Hakai knockdown induced phenotypic alterations in both 2D and 3D CRC models, despite minimal global transcriptomic changes. Notably, significant modifications in m6A methylation were observed, particularly in immune-related transcripts, including cytokines TNF, IFNB1, CXCL1, and CXCL8, accompanied by an overall reduction in m6A levels. Mechanistically, Hakai interacted with the writer-associated protein VIRMA and regulated METTL3 subcellular localisation. Functionally, conditioned media from Hakai-knockdown cells altered immune marker expression in patient-derived immune cells, indicating modulation of tumour-immune crosstalk. Hakai functions as a regulatory component of the m⁶A writer complex in CRC, influencing RNA methylation and immune-related gene expression. Our findings support a previously unrecognised role for Hakai in tumour-immune crosstalk and suggest its potential relevance in the modulation of the CRC tumour microenvironment.

title: Sex-Stratified Regulatory Landscapes of Pancreatic β-Cells in Type 2 Diabetes: Single-Cell and Donor-Level Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) exhibits sex-dependent differences in islet β-cell dysfunction, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. By integrating two independent single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, we performed sex-stratified analyses at both the single-cell and donor levels to identify sex-prioritized candidate genes and candidate therapeutic interventions. At the single-cell level, differential expression and network analyses nominated AKT2 as a male-prioritized candidate and ALDOA and GAPDH as female-prioritized candidates; virtual gene knockout of these candidates indicated that they impair β-cell function through diffuse regulatory-network remodeling rather than through single marker genes; and female β-cells formed a discrete T2D-enriched functional state (T2D proportions of 32.5%, 56.8%, and 80.0% across the three states; p < 0.0001), whereas no disease-associated functional stratification was detected in males. Pathway-enrichment and CytoTRACE2 analyses revealed, at the cell level, correlation structures that differed between sexes for 6 pathways (e.g., Insulin_Secretion, r = +0.206 male vs. -0.103 female, cell-level p = 4.8 × 10-4), although these differences were not confirmed in donor-level sensitivity analyses and are presented as descriptive. Pseudobulk analysis across 24 donor units identified a significant signature of seven genes in the female-stratified analysis, dominated by glycolytic downregulation, with SPP1 upregulation reaching nominal significance; in males, four genes reached significance but rested on only two male T2D donors in the pseudobulk subset and are presented as descriptive, so no robust male disease signature was detected given limited statistical power. Machine-learning models with donor-grouped cross-validation yielded donor-level ROC-AUC values at or below 0.52 in both sexes, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals spanning 0.5 in all cases, consistent with chance-level performance. Drug screening nominated ten candidate compounds, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding of SB-431542 with AKT2 (-8.10 kcal/mol) and triamterene with ALDOA (-7.71 kcal/mol).

title: Exploratory miRNA Profiling and Network Analysis of Endometrioma Fluid: Identifying a Candidate Microenvironmental miRNA Signature and Putative In Silico Regulatory Networks.
abstract: Benign ovarian cysts encompass various lesions, including functional cysts and endometriomas. Given the complex pathogenesis of endometriosis, this study aimed to perform the first exploratory, high-throughput microarray profiling of microRNAs (miRNAs) directly from endometrioma fluid, comparing it with functional ovarian cyst fluid to establish a novel molecular baseline and map putative regulatory networks. Total RNA was isolated from uncentrifuged cyst fluid (n = 7). Profiling was performed using Affymetrix GeneChip miRNA 4.0 Arrays. Following differential expression analysis (FDR < 0.05, FC > 2.0), candidate target genes for the directly measured mature miRNAs were retrieved from miRTarBase. Standardized HGNC targets regulated by ≥4 distinct miRNAs were analyzed using Cytoscape v3.10.4 for network topology, g:Profiler (version e114_eg62_p19_27110d83) for Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment, and Metascape v3.5.20260701 for protein-protein interaction (PPI) modules. Principal Component Analysis demonstrated robust separation between cohorts (PC1: 93.5% variance). We identified 37 FDR-significant microarray features, including 35 mature miRNAs. The primary mature miRNA network comprised 234 unique target genes and 1072 interactions. Functional enrichment highlighted the regulation of primary metabolic processes (padj = 1.43 × 10-16), cell division (padj = 9.97 × 10-4), and nucleocytoplasmic transport. PPI clustering identified densely connected modules driving cellular stress responses, cell cycle progression, and AGE-RAGE signaling. The identified whole-fluid miRNA profile predominantly reflects the distinct cellular, inflammatory, and hemorrhagic composition of the endometriotic microenvironment. These highly filtered, database-curated networks provide a robust in silico reference framework for future targeted functional validation and biomarker discovery in endometriosis.

title: Transcriptome and Co-Expression Network Analysis Reveals Key Modules and Hub Genes Associated with Husk Number in Maize.
abstract: Background: Husk number is a key agronomic trait in maize that affects grain dehydration rate and yield, yet its regulatory mechanisms remain largely unknown. This study aimed to identify gene modules and hub genes associated with husk number by integrating transcriptome profiling, hierarchical clustering, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Methods: RNA-seq was performed on ear tissues from two maize inbred lines with extreme husk numbers (LJ311, ~20 husks; PHG35, ~5 husks) at four developmental stages (V7-V10). A total of 12,605 putative husk-associated genes were identified. Differential expression analysis, hierarchical clustering, and WGCNA were combined to prioritize candidate genes. Results: Hierarchical clustering revealed a late-stage-specific gene cluster (Cluster 3, 44 genes) strongly up-regulated at V8-V10 in the high-husk line. WGCNA identified three modules significantly correlated with husk number: MEblue and MEbrown (positively) and MEturquoise (negatively). Cluster 3 was enriched in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, DNA replication, and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Intersecting hub genes (|kME| > 0.9) with high-confidence differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (|log2FoldChange| > 2) yielded two prioritized candidate gene sets: up-regulated genes enriched in cell cycle, brassinosteroid (BR) signaling, and phospholipid metabolism; down-regulated genes enriched in mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, glycolysis, and cell wall degradation. Conclusions: These results suggest that husk number may be regulated by a potential BR-MAPK-cell cycle regulatory axis, providing a regulatory network and candidate genes for future validation and molecular breeding.

title: Codon Usage and Sequence-Composition Characteristics Associated with the Malignant Ductal Transcriptional State in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Codon usage bias is a fundamental feature of genomic organization whose relationship with cancer-associated transcriptional states remains incompletely understood. Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by aggressive progression and limited therapeutic options. Here, we investigated nucleotide, codon, and amino acid composition associated with the malignant ductal cell state using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data. Comparing malignant and nonmalignant ductal cells, we identified distinct sequence characteristics associated with malignancy. Genes up-regulated in malignant cells exhibited higher GC content, preferential use of G- and C-ending synonymous codons, higher frequency of preferred codons (FOP), lower effective numbers of codons (ENC), and lower length-normalized minimum free-energy values than did down-regulated genes. Distinct nucleotide and amino acid composition patterns were also observed. Expression-weighted codon demand analysis at the donor/pseudobulk level further revealed differences between malignant and nonmalignant transcriptional programs. These codon usage patterns were reproduced in a second PDAC single-cell RNA-seq cohort. Bulk RNA-seq analysis further showed that highly expressed transcript isoforms tended to exhibit higher FOP and lower ENC than did less highly expressed isoforms. Reporter experiments demonstrated associations between synonymous codon composition and mRNA abundance and protein output, with stronger effects in pancreatic cancer cells than in non-cancer-derived cells. Together, these findings indicate that malignant ductal transcriptional programs and highly expressed PDAC transcript isoforms exhibit distinct codon usage and sequence-composition characteristics. Their convergence across independent cellular, transcript-level, and experimental analyses supports an association between synonymous codon composition and gene-expression characteristics in pancreatic cancer, providing a foundation for further investigation of their functional relevance.

title: ROCK2 Expression in Colorectal Cancer: Clinicopathological, Molecular, and Prognostic Associations.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinase 2 (ROCK2) regulates the actin cytoskeleton, cell migration, and proliferation, but its clinical relevance in colorectal cancer remains unclear. This study evaluated the clinicopathological, molecular, and prognostic associations of ROCK2 expression in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and rectal adenocarcinoma (READ). Materials and Methods: RNA sequencing and clinical data from 439 COAD and 158 READ cases in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were obtained through OncoLnc. Patients were classified into high- and low-ROCK2 expression groups using the median expression level. Clinicopathological associations, molecular correlations, survival outcomes, and Hallmark gene-set enrichment were analyzed. Prognostic associations were further evaluated in the independent GSE39582 colon cancer cohort. Results: In READ, high ROCK2 expression was more frequent in patients aged ≤65 years (p = 0.017), and its distribution differed by tumor site (p = 0.005). In COAD, high ROCK2 expression was less frequent in patients with a history of colon polyps (p = 0.013). ROCK2 expression was positively correlated with APC and KRAS expression in both COAD (R = 0.363 and 0.293, respectively; both p < 0.001) and READ (R = 0.543 and 0.282, respectively; both p < 0.001), and negatively correlated with TP53 expression in COAD only (R = -0.198, p < 0.001). High ROCK2 expression was associated with longer overall survival in COAD (p = 0.021) and READ (p = 0.045). In COAD, this association remained after multivariate adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.82, p = 0.009), although it was attenuated after multiple imputation of missing CEA values (p = 0.051). In GSEA, the mitotic spindle gene set was enriched in the high ROCK2 group, whereas oxidative phosphorylation, interferon response, and DNA repair gene sets were enriched in the low ROCK2 group in both cohorts. In GSE39582, the HR for high ROCK2 expression was below 1, but the primary multivariable analysis of overall survival did not reach statistical significance (HR = 0.80, p = 0.119), whereas high ROCK2 expression was associated with longer recurrence-free survival, a secondary endpoint (HR = 0.72, p = 0.032); this association was not reproduced with an alternative ROCK2 probe. Conclusions: ROCK2 expression was associated with key molecular features, including APC and KRAS expression, and with overall survival in TCGA COAD and READ. A similar prognostic direction was observed in an independent colon cancer cohort, although the primary overall survival analysis was not statistically significant. These prognostic associations warrant validation in additional cohorts and functional studies.

title: Reprogramming and Epigenetic Modifications: Unraveling the Role of Histone Lactylation in Atherosclerosis.
abstract: Lactylation links cellular metabolism to histone regulation and nonhistone protein function; however, its functional consequences in atherosclerosis depend on the modified substrate, target residue, cell type, and disease stage. This narrative review distinguishes direct atherosclerosis evidence from cardiovascular but non-atherosclerosis evidence and cross-disease mechanistic context, framing mechanistic claims accordingly. Direct evidence in atherosclerosis implicates several pathogenic pathways, including endothelial H3K18 lactylation at NF-κB pathway and SNAI1 promoters, SLC22A6- and ACSS1-driven H3K9 lactylation, lactate- and AARS1-dependent FOXO1 lactylation under atheroprone flow, H4K12 lactylation at CDKN1A during endothelial senescence, and an H3K18 lactylation-METTL3 axis in macrophage ferroptosis. Conversely, direct evidence also supports atheroprotective pathways, notably nonhistone MeCP2 K271 lactylation in endothelial cells and macrophages. Observations from myocardial repair, valvular and medial calcification, aortic aneurysm, pulmonary hypertension, and oncology provide mechanistic context rather than direct proof of plaque-specific biology. Furthermore, we examine the interplay between lactylation and acetylation, methylation, and RNA modifications-including scenarios where lactylation functions upstream of acetylation-and critically evaluate the capabilities and limitations of current analytical methods. Key methodological considerations include lactyl-donor stoichiometry and site occupancy; antibody cross-reactivity; resolution of L-lactyl, D-lactyl, and carboxyethyl lysine isomers; mass-spectrometric site localization; chromatin profiling against matched acetylation controls; and stable-isotope tracing. Finally, we propose an integrative translational framework that pairs peripheral mononuclear cell and plaque sampling with single-cell and spatial multi-omics, strictly distinguishing lactate sensing from site-specific protein lactylation detection. To date, no clinically validated lactylation biomarker or lactylation-targeted therapy exists for atherosclerosis, and lactate abundance cannot be conflated with protein lactylation. Clinical translation ultimately requires site-specific causal validation in plaque-relevant models and prospective human cohorts.

title: The Putative Contribution of Gut Microbiota-Regulated Ferroptosis to Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Revealed by Combined Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing.
abstract: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) involves multifactorial disturbances, among which gut microbial imbalance and ferroptotic injury are increasingly recognized, yet their molecular links remain unclear. Public NAFLD liver transcriptome datasets, microbiota-related genes (MRGs), and ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) were integrated. Seurat analysis identified cell populations potentially regulated by gut microbiota, followed by coexpression network construction. Key genes (KGs) were prioritized through differential expression analysis, Venn intersection, machine-learning feature selection, ROC assessment, and expression validation. Their putative regulatory roles were examined using enrichment analysis, immune infiltration profiling, virtual knockout, drug screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, metabolic pathway evaluation, cell-cell communication inference, and pseudotime analysis. Single-cell analysis indicated that hepatocytes were the NAFLD cell population most prominently associated with gut microbiota regulation. In hepatocytes, 1155 module genes (MGs) were obtained, and 39 candidate genes were generated by intersecting differentially expressed genes (DEGs), MGs, and FRGs. Machine-learning cross-validation identified HPCAL1 and P4HA1 as KGs; both were significantly reduced in NAFLD and yielded a favorable combined diagnostic model. These KGs were linked to ferroptosis, adipogenesis, Toll-like receptor signaling, and immune infiltration, particularly M1 and M2 macrophages. Virtual knockout revealed 94 perturbed genes related to glycerophospholipid metabolism. Docking and molecular dynamics analyses suggested candidate small molecules with stable binding potential to P4HA1. NAFLD hepatocytes also showed metabolic remodeling, PLG-PARD3-mediated communication, and stage-dependent KG expression along pseudotime. HPCAL1 and P4HA1 are identified as candidate biomarkers potentially linked to ferroptosis and gut microbiota crosstalk in NAFLD, and may be proposed as therapeutic targets worthy of further investigation, although the mechanistic basis for targeted intervention remains to be experimentally defined.

title: Single-cell and clinical analyses reveal elevated HAX1 expression and cell-cycle-associated programs during metastatic progression of lung adenocarcinoma, particularly in brain metastasis.
abstract: Metastatic dissemination is a major determinant of poor outcome in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, molecular features associated with distinct metastatic states, particularly lymph node and brain metastases, remain incompletely defined. We investigated the relationship between HAX1 and LUAD metastatic progression. We reanalyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE131907 to characterize HAX1 expression and associated transcriptional programs across normal lung, primary LUAD, advanced tumors, metastatic lymph nodes (mLN), and brain metastases. Findings were validated using additional public datasets from GEO and TCGA, including the independent single-cell dataset GSE69405. Clinical LUAD specimens were analyzed to assess HAX1 protein expression and its clinicopathological associations. Functional validation was performed in A549 and H1975 cells, and tumor growth was assessed using an A549-derived subcutaneous xenograft model. HAX1 expression and the proportion of HAX1-positive epithelial cells increased across LUAD disease states and were significantly enriched in mLN and brain-metastatic epithelial populations compared with primary tumors. In a 125-patient clinical cohort, high HAX1 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis, advanced stage, and shorter overall survival, and remained independently associated with lymph node metastasis after adjustment for T stage (OR = 2.581, 95% CI 1.161-5.742; P = 0.020). An independent single-cell dataset further confirmed elevated HAX1 expression in brain-metastatic LUAD cells. HAX1-associated transcriptional programs converged on E2F, MYC, MTORC1, DNA replication, and cell-cycle signatures, whereas brain-metastatic epithelial cells additionally exhibited mitochondrial and translational programs. Integrated analyses identified UBE2S, PITX1, GGH, and PDCD2L as HAX1-associated candidates.EPIC and TIMER analyses consistently showed inverse correlations between HAX1 expression and estimated B-cell, CD4+ T-cell, CD8+ T-cell, and macrophage abundance. HAX1 knockdown also reduced cell viability, increased the G0/G1-phase fraction and decreased the S-phase fraction, reduced G1/S-related protein levels and PI3K/AKT signaling, and inhibited subcutaneous xenograft growth. HAX1 is closely associated with metastatic progression of LUAD, with strong clinical evidence for lymph node involvement and reproducible enrichment in brain-metastatic epithelial cells. Its associations with cell-cycle programs and immune cell infiltration, together with its functional role in G1/S progression, support further investigation of HAX1 in metastatic adaptation and tumor-immune interactions.

title: Ketohexokinase, the principal fructose-metabolising enzyme is downregulated in the kidneys of rodents and humans with chronic kidney disease.
abstract: Excessive renal exposure to fructose, either via oral consumption or de novo production via the polyol pathway is associated with kidney injury. This detrimental effect is attributed to the rate limiting enzyme in the 'fructolytic' pathway, ketohexokinase-C, activity of which results in intracellular phosphate depletion, uric acid production and inflammation.Multiple factors which characterise chronic kidney disease including hypoxia and uric acid production upregulate ketohexokinase-C, yet the expression profile of this enzyme in CKD has not been characterised. If upregulated in the context of chronic kidney disease ketohexokinase-C presents an attractive therapeutic target to slow disease progression. Renal ketohexokinase-C is upregulated in the context of chronic kidney disease. Chronic kidney disease was induced using an adenine diet model and validated by measuring creatinine clearance, urine protein creatinine ratio, Kidney Injury Molecule-1 and via histology. Ketohexokinase and megalin were quantified by Western blotting analysis. RT-qPCR was used to quantify KHK-C and KHK-A mRNA. RNA-Sequencing data of 24 human kidney biopsy samples (GSE137570) were identified for in silico validation, patient eGFR and percent tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis being matched to each sample. Unexpectedly, ketohexokinase protein and mRNA were significantly decreased in adenine treated animals compared with controls (N = 6, p=0.0001) and (N = 4, p=0.0002). This finding was replicated in a second cohort of animals. Furthermore, a significant positive linear association was observed between creatinine clearance and ketohexokinase protein in Wistar rats (N = 8, p<0.0001). The same association was evident in silico between eGFR and KHK RNA adjusted for interstitial fibrosis in human kidney (N = 24 p=<0.0001). Contrary to our hypothesis, these findings demonstrate reduction in protein and mRNA expression of the principal fructose metabolising enzyme in chronic kidney disease. This is at odds with existing data linking fructose metabolism with acute kidney injury and may represent a compensatory response limiting associated ATP depletion and inflammation in the chronic setting.

title: Network Toxicology Combined with Multi-Omics Identifies GNMT and LGALS3 as Key Genes Linking PM2.5 Exposure to Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
abstract: This study aimed to identify candidate molecular links bridging PM2.5 exposure and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and to elucidate their potential roles. A multifaceted approach was adopted in this study, integrating network toxicology, Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), multi-cohort transcriptomic validation, immune infiltration analysis, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular docking. PM2.5 targets and MASLD genes were collected from public databases. The eQTL data were used to assess potential causal associations via MR and SMR. Candidate genes were validated in three GEO datasets. Immune infiltration was analyzed with xCell, and single-cell transcriptomics assessed gene expression in immune subsets. Molecular docking was performed for PM2.5 components with target proteins. A total of 187 overlapping genes were identified, from which 10 hub genes were determined by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. MR and SMR analyses narrowed down the overlapping genes to GNMT and LGALS3, with GNMT showing a protective association (OR = 0.869, 95% CI: 0.794-0.951) and LGALS3 a risk association (OR = 1.773, 95% CI: 1.217-2.583). Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased infiltration of CD8+ T cells, B cells, and M2 macrophages in MASLD, and GNMT expression was found to be negatively correlated with CD4+ T cell infiltration. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of selected organic compounds and metal ions to both GNMT and LGALS3. GNMT showed a protective role in PM2.5-associated MASLD, whereas LGALS3 showed a risk association. The differential expression patterns of these two genes in immune cells, together with their predicted interactions with PM2.5 components, point to a potential dual mechanism. Together, these findings provide novel insights into PM2.5-associated MASLD and identify potential molecular targets.

title: HEATR3 as a Potential Biomarker in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Transcriptomic Identification and Validation in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Background: HEAT repeat-containing protein 3 (HEATR3) participates in ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar stress responses, but its clinical and molecular relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated HEATR3 expression, prognostic significance, and associated molecular networks in TCGA-HNSC, with independent transcriptomic validation in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Methods: HEATR3 expression and its association with clinical outcomes were investigated using TCGA-HNSC data. Survival analyses included Kaplan-Meier estimates and multivariable Cox regression. Tumor microenvironment correlations, functional enrichment, and protein interaction networks were examined using TIMER3, GEPIA3, STRING, BioGRID, and R-based analyses. HEATR3 expression was independently evaluated in GEO datasets GSE37991 and GSE30784. Results: HEATR3 expression was significantly elevated in TCGA-HNSC tissues compared with non-cancerous controls. High HEATR3 expression was associated with poorer overall survival (OS), and this association persisted after adjustment for clinicopathological variables. An association with progression-free interval (PFI) was observed in unadjusted analyses but was not retained following multivariable adjustment. HEATR3-associated genes were enriched in ribosome biogenesis and RNA-processing functions, while correlations with stromal cell abundance varied across deconvolution methods. Independent OSCC analyses showed increased HEATR3 expression with both probes in GSE37991, whereas only one of two probes demonstrated significant upregulation in GSE30784. Conclusions: HEATR3 is transcriptionally upregulated in TCGA-HNSC, with additional but probe-dependent evidence of increased expression in independent OSCC cohorts. Higher HEATR3 expression is also associated with poorer OS in TCGA-HNSC. Its molecular associations with RNA metabolism and ribosome biogenesis support further investigation of HEATR3 as a potential prognostic biomarker.

title: Anesthesia-associated pro-inflammatory microglial transcriptional signatures: transcriptomic identification and multi-dataset characterization of five candidate hub genes.
abstract: To identify candidate hub genes associated with anesthesia-related microglial pro-inflammatory transcriptional changes and to explore their computationally inferred upstream transcriptional regulators, providing candidate molecular correlates that require future clinical validation before any relevance to perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) can be inferred. Differential expression analysis and LASSO regression were applied to a rat basolateral amygdala transcriptomic dataset (GSE1779; isoflurane; n = 6). Hub gene expression was correlated with computationally estimated cerebral immune cell proportions via CIBERSORT. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; GSE217202; 9,451 microglial profiles derived from only two biological samples, one per condition) with pseudotime trajectory and SCENIC gene regulatory network analyses characterized microglial subpopulations and transcriptional regulators. Cross-dataset expression comparison was performed across five GEO datasets (two species, three anesthetics), with GSE141242 reserved for external validation of the five-gene classifier. In vitro, propofol-treated BV2 cells (30 μM, 4-12 h) were assessed by RT-qPCR and western blotting. Given the limited sample size (n = 6), findings should be interpreted as exploratory. Five candidate hub genes, Fibin, Scaf1, Plcb2, Kcnh4, and Ptprj, were identified from 58 differentially expressed genes. scRNA-seq resolved microglial subcluster MG1 as a subcluster enriched for pro-inflammatory transcriptional signatures, with each hub gene defining a transcriptionally distinct molecular program. Cross-dataset comparison revealed heterogeneous directionality: Fibin was significantly upregulated in GSE1779 and GSE106799, whereas Ptprj was significantly downregulated in GSE1779. Pseudotime analysis showed a weak, descriptive cell-level association between Plcb2 expression and the MG1 state (ρ = -0.061). SCENIC identified Mef2c and the NF-κB component Rel as candidate upstream regulators. In propofol-treated BV2 cells, Scaf1 and Plcb2 mRNA levels increased, accompanied by increased iNOS and phospho-NF-κB protein expression. Fibin, Scaf1, Plcb2, Kcnh4, and Ptprj represent candidate molecular correlates associated with anesthesia-related microglial transcriptional changes; because no PND or cognitive model was analysed, their relevance to PND remains to be determined. Mef2c and NF-κB (Rel) emerged as computationally inferred candidate regulators, and their biological and clinical relevance requires validation in primary-microglia and in vivo intervention studies before any diagnostic or therapeutic application can be claimed.
