title: Is a Positive RSV Test Enough? Assessing the Clinical Value of Multiplex PCR, Viral Load and Host-Response Biomarkers in Children.
abstract: Background: A positive respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) test establishes viral detection but does not necessarily explain disease severity, identify clinically relevant coinfections, or predict disease progression. Multiplex molecular testing, viral load assessment, and host-response biomarkers may provide additional information, yet their ability to improve clinical assessment and decision-making in children with RSV infection remains uncertain. Aim: This narrative review examines the clinical value of advanced diagnostic tools in pediatric RSV infection, addressing both antimicrobial stewardship through reducing unnecessary antibiotic use and acute clinical decision-making through pathogen identification and severity stratification, with a focus on multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR), viral load assessment, and inflammatory biomarkers. Results: Multiplex PCR broadens etiological characterization by detecting additional respiratory pathogens, but viral co-detection is not consistently associated with greater disease severity, while bacterial detection must be distinguished from colonization and clinically significant coinfection. Cycle threshold (Ct) values are assay-dependent proxies for the amount of target viral RNA rather than standardized quantitative viral-load measurements and have been associated with disease severity and respiratory support requirements in some pediatric cohorts. However, inter-assay variability, sampling time, and prolonged RNA shedding limit their reliability as independent prognostic indicators. Host-response biomarkers address a different diagnostic dimension. Procalcitonin (PCT) may be more informative for invasive bacterial infection than for localized bacterial coinfection, whereas C-reactive protein (CRP) lacks sufficient specificity. Leukocyte-derived indices, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte (NLR) and monocyte-to-lymphocyte (MLR) ratios, have been associated with severity in selected RSV cohorts, but their incremental prognostic utility remains unvalidated. Across these approaches, greater analytical sensitivity or more extensive biological information does not necessarily translate into greater clinical utility. Conclusions: The central challenge in pediatric RSV diagnostics is not simply detecting additional pathogens or measuring more biological parameters, but determining which findings meaningfully contribute to patient assessment, risk stratification, and antibiotic decision-making. Current evidence does not support the isolated use of molecular co-detection, Ct values, or inflammatory biomarkers to establish bacterial coinfection or predict disease severity. Integrated diagnostic strategies combining pathogen detection, viral burden, host-response markers, and clinical findings may improve clinical decision-making, support appropriate antibiotic use, and reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions. Future studies should evaluate their impact on patient management and antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Pan-Cancer Analysis and Functional Validation Reveal a Role for MAN1A1 in Promoting Metastasis-Associated Phenotypes in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is aggressive and prone to distant metastasis. MAN1A1 encodes a Golgi α-1,2-mannosidase involved in N-glycan processing, but its pan-cancer features and role in TNBC metastasis remain unclear. Methods: We integrated The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), Human Protein Atlas (HPA), and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) data to characterize MAN1A1 expression, clinical outcomes, Hallmark pathways, and immune features across cancers, with further analyses focused on breast cancer and TNBC. Functional effects were evaluated using MAN1A1 knockdown in LM2 cells, overexpression in MDA-MB-231 cells, Transwell assays, and a tail-vein injection model in nude mice. LM2 RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) validation, and TCGA-TNBC transcriptomic and immune microenvironment analyses were integrated to investigate MAN1A1-associated molecular features. Results: MAN1A1 exhibited marked cancer-type heterogeneity in expression, prognostic associations, and molecular alterations. It was not specifically overexpressed in TNBC; however, higher MAN1A1 expression within breast cancer and TNBC was associated with poorer overall survival and metastasis-related features. MAN1A1 knockdown suppressed LM2 migration, invasion, and experimental lung metastasis, whereas overexpression enhanced MDA-MB-231 migration and invasion. LM2 RNA-seq revealed alterations in transcriptional programs related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix remodeling, and inflammation. TCGA-TNBC showed concordant transcriptional patterns and distinct immune and stromal microenvironmental features. Conclusions: MAN1A1 promotes TNBC cell migration, invasion, and experimental lung metastasis, accompanied by alterations in transcriptional programs related to cell adhesion, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, migration, and inflammation. These findings support MAN1A1 as a context-dependent metastasis-associated molecule in TNBC and provide a basis for further investigation of its potential molecular mechanisms.

title: Therapy-Dependent Modulation of Fibroblast Activation Protein Expression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Implications for FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study investigated the treatment-dependent dynamics of FAP expression in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and preclinical xenografts to inform optimal patient selection and timing for fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted theranostics. Methods: FAP expression was assessed by immunofluorescence (IF) staining of human PDAC samples, including treatment-naïve (n = 7), chemotherapy- and chemoradiotherapy-responsive tumors (n = 8), and adjacent pancreatic tissues (n = 4), and validated at the transcript level by RNA sequencing (seq). The institutional bulk RNA-seq data were integrated with a published PDAC cohort from the Human Tumor Atlas Network, together including treatment-naïve (n = 54), treatment-sensitive (n = 9), partially resistant (n = 14), treatment-resistant (n = 56), and adjacent pancreas (n = 4) tissue samples. In parallel, dynamic FAP expression was evaluated in FOLFIRINOX-sensitive PANC-1 and FOLFIRINOX-resistant SU8686 PDAC xenografts by IF. Results: IF quantification showed increased FAP expression in treatment-sensitive human PDAC compared to treatment-naïve tumors and adjacent pancreas. Integrated transcriptomic analysis revealed therapy-dependent FAP modulation, with higher FAP transcripts in treatment-sensitive tumors compared to resistant and naïve tumors. Cell-type deconvolution showed reduced inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts in treatment-sensitive tumors and enrichment in resistant ones, while myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts remained consistently abundant across all treatment states. In xenografts, FAP expression remained unchanged in PANC-1 tumors throughout treatment, whereas SU8686 tumors showed transient FAP upregulation on days 9 and 15 that did not persist. Conclusions: Findings highlight FAP as an abundant and actionable theranostic biomarker for PDAC patients across treatment states. Mouse models of human PDAC may not reliably recapitulate FAP changes in humans. These findings provide a framework for treatment-informed patient selection for FAP-directed theranostics in PDAC.

title: A Candidate Transcriptomic Gene Set Is Associated with Hypoxia-Related and Mesenchymal Gene Expression in Glioblastoma, but Not with Clinical Radioresistance.
abstract: Gene sets derived from radioresistant cells require independent evaluation before they can be interpreted as treatment-resistance biomarkers. We reassessed an unpublished candidate gene set archived as 360 identifiers using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, an irradiation dataset and three clinical cohorts. Its expression score was associated with hypoxia-, glycolysis- and mesenchymal-related transcription after removal of overlapping genes and adjustment for transcript detection. Median partial correlations across seven independent single-cell patients were 0.228, 0.107 and 0.239, respectively, with concordant associations across nine spatial patients. Reconstruction with the standard statistical implementation selected 29 genes; matched donor comparisons showed that the two sets were not interchangeable. No inferred metabolic module passed donor-level false discovery rate correction. Three patient-derived models showed inconsistent score changes two days after irradiation. A fixed survival model achieved external concordance indices of 0.460 and 0.545. Adrenomedullin RNA and protein abundance were correlated, without positive susceptibility-genetic support. These findings support reproducible associations with transcriptional programs, not measurements of oxygenation, metabolic flux or radiation survival. The candidate remains exploratory, and clinical radioresistance or prediction of radiotherapy benefit has not been established.

title: Integrated Single-Cell Analysis and Network Pharmacology Reveal the Potential Mechanisms of Baicalein in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Baicalein, a major flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, exhibits multiple antitumor activities, but its key targets and mechanisms in PC remain unclear. This study integrated network pharmacology, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), molecular docking, and in vitro experiments to investigate the potential mechanisms of baicalein against PC. Network pharmacology identified baicalein-related targets associated with PC, which were mainly enriched in receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, PI3K-AKT, MAPK, Ras, and apoptosis-related pathways. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed heterogeneous SRC expression across epithelial subpopulations, with higher expression observed in Cluster 1, and dynamic changes during epithelial cell state transitions. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions between baicalein and key proteins, including SRC and EGFR. In vitro experiments further showed that baicalein significantly reduced PC cell viability and decreased SRC protein expression. These findings suggest that baicalein may exert antitumor effects in PC through multiple targets and pathways, with SRC representing a potential key target, providing a theoretical basis for further evaluation of baicalein as an adjuvant therapeutic candidate for PC.

title: Epithelial Alternative Polyadenylation Identifies Hepatoma-Derived Growth Factor as a Genetically Supported Candidate in Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Alternative polyadenylation (APA) remodels 3' untranslated regions and may affect transcript stability, translational efficiency, and protein output without proportional changes in total mRNA abundance. Its tumor-epithelial landscape and protein-level genetic relevance in prostate cancer remain incompletely defined. We compared tumor and luminal epithelial cells across two patient-derived single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts and identified recurrent 3'UTR shortening events. These genes were integrated with cis-protein quantitative trait locus-based Mendelian randomization, outcome replication, and colocalization analyses of prostate cancer risk. Prioritized candidates were further assessed using transcriptomic, proteomic, histological, computational perturbation, and structure-based screening analyses. Tumor epithelial cells showed widespread 3'UTR shortening, with 1066 shortened genes shared across cohorts. Integrating recurrent epithelial APA shortening with protein-genetic evidence prioritized hepatoma-derived growth factor (HDGF). Genetically proxied higher plasma HDGF was associated with higher prostate cancer odds across datasets, although the strength of genetic support was sensitive to instrument correlation and colocalization assumptions. HDGF also showed preferential proximal poly(A)-site use and increased RNA and protein abundance in prostate tumors, and higher expression was associated with shorter biochemical recurrence-free survival. HDGF is an APA-associated candidate supported by complementary protein-genetic and tissue-level evidence in prostate cancer.

title: Unveiling Key Gene Signatures in Pancreatic Cancer: Advanced Computational Insights for Biomarker and Therapeutic Target Discovery.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains the most lethal type of pancreatic cancer, with a dismal 11% 5-year survival rate, owing to its rapid progression and metastasis. Its aggressive nature, coupled with late diagnosis and inadequate therapeutic approaches, necessitates the urgent identification of novel disease-associated genes for more targeted therapy. Using the extensive RNA-seq and microarray data from PDAC patients, this study aimed to computationally screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between tumor and non-tumor samples to discover potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Three gene expression datasets (GSE62452, GSE183795, and GSE28735) include microarray gene expression profiles of 461 samples, comprising 253 pancreatic tumor tissues and 208 adjacent non-tumor tissues from patients with PDAC was analyzed to identify DEGs. These were then subjected to functional enrichment analysis and protein interaction network mapping. The top 25 hub genes were identified based on four scoring algorithms in Cytoscape's cytoHubba plugin. Seventeen genes common across all four algorithms were further verified for differential expression using the GEPIA2 web server. Kaplan-Meier survival plots revealed ITGA2, ITGA3, ITGB6, LAMA3, and LAMB3 as top-ranked targets with poor prognosis in PDAC, implicating their potential oncogenic roles. The identified hub genes were further analyzed through genetic, epigenetic, and protein expression analysis to gain mechanistic insights into their potential roles in pancreatic cancer progression. Genetic alterations were associated with poorer survival outcomes. Promoter methylation levels were notably reduced for LAMA3 and LAMB3 in tumor samples. Concordant expression levels were observed at both transcriptomic and protein levels. Collectively, ITGA2, ITGA3, ITGB6, LAMA3, and LAMB3 may serve as promising targets for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in PDAC. Further clinical investigations involving in vivo studies are required to assess the potential of the markers.

title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Decode Tumor-Microenvironment Crosstalk in Colorectal Cancer Metastasis.
abstract: Metastasis remains the principal cause of death in colorectal cancer (CRC), and accumulating evidence indicates that it is not a tumor-autonomous process. Dissemination and organ-specific colonization of the liver, lung, and peritoneum are governed by continuous, bidirectional crosstalk between malignant cells and the cellular and extracellular compartments of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Deciphering this crosstalk requires knowing not only which cell states are present but also where they reside and with whom they interact. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves cellular heterogeneity at single-cell resolution but requires tissue dissociation, which erases in situ spatial information; spatial transcriptomics (ST) restores that dimension by mapping gene expression on intact sections and, with deconvolution algorithms, anchoring scRNA-seq-defined subpopulations back to their native coordinates. Organized around the metastatic cascade of local initiation, circulatory dissemination, and distant colonization, this review examines how the combined application of the two technologies has clarified tumor-microenvironment crosstalk at each stage. At the primary site, cancer stem cell heterogeneity, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plasticity, and reciprocal signaling between budding cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts at the invasive front jointly determine invasive capacity and organotropism. During dissemination, we consider the clonal origins and transcriptional phenotypes of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and the clustering and immune-evasion programs that enable their survival under shear stress and immune surveillance. At the metastatic site, we address multilayered remodeling of the immune contexture, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix organization, vascular structure, and metabolic programs, emphasizing how macrophages, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and extracellular vesicles jointly construct an immunosuppressive niche permissive to colonization. Together, these findings frame organ-specific metastasis as the spatially coordinated co-evolution of tumor cells with tissue-resident immune and stromal populations, and highlight microenvironment-directed therapeutic opportunities and spatially informed prognostic biomarkers for precision oncology.

title: Ferulic acid attenuates hepatic steatosis and modulates PTGS2, PPARG, and FADS2 expression: an integrated network pharmacology, molecular dynamics, and experimental study.
abstract: Ferulic acid (FA), a principal phenolic constituent of Angelica sinensis, attenuates hepatic steatosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Here, we employed an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, transcriptomics, molecular dynamics (MD), single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) pseudobulk analysis, and in vitro validation in a PA/OA-induced HepG2 model. External validation revealed consistent upregulation of FADS2 across cohorts, whereas PTGS2 exhibited cohort-dependent directionality. Single-cell pseudobulk analysis suggested a hepatocyte-intrinsic trend for FADS2 and PPARG, although donor-level significance was not reached (p = 0.29 and p = 0.10, respectively). Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of FA to FADS2 (-8.539 kcal/mol), PTGS2 (-7.146 kcal/mol), and PPARG (-5.882 kcal/mol). In vitro, FA dose-dependently reduced lipid accumulation (Oil Red O and TC/TG) without cytotoxicity (confirmed by CCK-8). qPCR revealed that FA suppressed lipogenic genes (SREBP-1c, FASN, ACC1) and the desaturase SCD, while restoring the expression of the fatty acid oxidation marker CPT1A and the hepatocyte-intrinsic desaturase FADS2. Western blot confirmed FA suppressed PTGS2 and PPARG protein expression. The coordinated suppression of lipogenesis and restoration of FADS2 expression is consistent with a 'lipid remodeling' hypothesis-FA may shift lipid flux toward less toxic, highly desaturated species-which warrants dedicated mechanistic validation. We identify FADS2 as a novel transcriptional signature of FA, with PTGS2 and PPARG as supported candidate targets.

title: A Machine Learning Prognostic Signature for Microsatellite-Stable Endometrial Cancer: Complementary Transcriptomic, Immune, and Pharmacogenomic Analyses.
abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) prognosis varies, particularly in microsatellite-stable (MSS) subtypes lacking effective immunotherapy strategies. This study integrated bulk RNA-seq and weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify immune-related genes (IRGs), followed by a machine learning framework (117 algorithms) to construct a prognostic model. Complementary validations were performed using multiple omics datasets, including survival analysis, immune infiltration assessment, and single-cell transcriptomic profiling. A three-gene (GAL, PGR, and THRB) model stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups, with high-risk correlating significantly with MSS status. Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis described cell type-specific expression patterns of PGR and THRB in one anti-PD-1 responder and one nonresponder; these observations were hypothesis-generating and not confirmatory. Drug sensitivity analysis computationally identified candidate agents (e.g., dasatinib and foretinib) for MSS/high-risk subgroups; these in silico findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation before clinical translation. This model provides a computationally derived candidate tool for prognosis and immune contexture-associated prognostic stratification in EC, awaiting further external validation. GAL and THRB (candidate adverse-risk genes) and PGR (a candidate favorable marker) may serve as research targets for MSI and MSS subtypes and potential prognostic biomarkers.

title: Identification of Hypoxia- and Circadian Rhythm-Related Prognostic Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Integrative Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis.
abstract: Hypoxia perturbs circadian rhythm gene expression in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet prognostic genes associated with both processes remain insufficiently characterized. Data from the liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) cohort in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with 27 hypoxia- and circadian rhythm-related genes and were further refined using univariate Cox regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression; a random survival forest (RSF) risk model was then constructed and validated. Independent prognostic and functional enrichment analyses, immune infiltration profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were subsequently performed. Four prognostic genes (ADM, PFKFB3, SERPINE1, and RORA) were identified through integrative computational analysis. The RSF model stratified LIHC patients into the high-risk group (HRG) and the low-risk group (LRG), which had significantly different survival outcomes, and the risk score and tumor stage were combined in a nomogram. The four genes were co-enriched in four pathways; eight immune cell types, including natural killer T (NKT) cells, differed between the risk groups. scRNA-seq identified stem-like/hypoxic malignant cells whose differentiation trajectory showed distinct expression dynamics of the four genes. IHC confirmed significantly higher ADM and PFKFB3 protein expression in LIHC tissues, whereas protein-level evidence for SERPINE1 and RORA was inconclusive. These findings support further prognostic evaluation of LIHC and investigation of the links among hypoxia, metabolic reprogramming, and stemness.

title: Identification and characterization of ion channel-related signatures in ulcerative colitis: an integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Human ion channel genes (HICGs) are involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating immune function, but their expression patterns and diagnostic value in UC have not been systematically investigated. This study aimed to identify UC-associated HICGs and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers using an integrative multi-omics approach. Multiple transcriptomic datasets were integrated with HICGs to identify UC-associated genes. Differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and machine learning were used to identify biomarkers and construct a diagnostic model validated in independent cohorts. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, cell-cell communication, virtual screening, and DSS-induced colitis validation were performed to characterize their biological and immune relevance. By integrating differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and machine learning, four core HICGs (TRPM6, FXYD3, CNGA1, and KCNJ15) were identified. The diagnostic model showed good performance in the training cohort (AUC = 0.979) and independent cohorts (AUC range: 0.864-0.981). TRPM6, FXYD3, and CNGA1 were downregulated in inflamed UC tissues, whereas KCNJ15 was upregulated. Their expression patterns were associated with histopathological mucosal status and disease activity. Immune infiltration analysis showed that TRPM6, FXYD3, and CNGA1 were negatively correlated with pro-inflammatory immune populations, whereas KCNJ15 showed the opposite pattern. Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that TRPM6, FXYD3, and CNGA1 were mainly expressed in intestinal epithelial cells and reduced in UC, while KCNJ15 was enriched in mononuclear phagocytes and neutrophils and increased in UC. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed reduced expression of TRPM6, FXYD3, and CNGA1 in UC. RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry (IHC) further confirmed the expression changes of these four HICGs in DSS-induced colitis, which were consistent with those observed in clinical UC samples. TRPM6, FXYD3, CNGA1, and KCNJ15 were identified as HICG-based biomarkers with diagnostic potential for UC. Multi-omics analyses revealed their cell-type-specific expression patterns and associations with immune microenvironment remodeling, highlighting their potential roles in UC pathogenesis.
